rules.note: 5-yr CAGR of split-adjusted regular DPS 0.475 (FY2020) -> 0.630 (FY2025) = 5.81%. 3-yr is faster at 6.95% and the 2026 step from 0.16 to 0.18/qtr is a 12.5% raise, but the durable rate is mid-single-digit. Fails.

rules.name: Payout with room left
rules.note: Insurer, so FCF = CFO - capex is appropriate: FY2025 $614.2M - $5.5M = $608.7M. Total dividends paid $241.6M = 39.7%. On the regular dividend alone (~$57.8M) payout is only 9.5% of FCF and 14.3% of net income; the special is the discretionary valve that keeps the regular dividend nearly riskless. Passing on the total-dividend basis, which is the conservative read.

rules.name: Streak long enough to prove policy, short enough to still be fast
rules.note: The data shows 17 consecutive increases and reaches FY2008, the first year in the window, so it is window-limited. Prior research says 50 years, which is plausible for RLI (raises since 1976) and is what the screen should display. At 50 years the streak is past the 30-year ceiling: policy is proven beyond doubt, but a 50-year payer is no longer an early-stage compounder. Fails on the upper bound, not on doubt.

rules.name: Earnings growing at least as fast as the dividend
rules.note: FCF $257.5M (FY2020) -> $608.7M (FY2025) = 18.78%/yr, more than three times the dividend CAGR. Net income corroborates: $157.1M -> $403.3M = 20.8%/yr. Coverage is widening, not narrowing.

rules.name: High return on invested capital
rules.note: FY2025 ROIC 21.7%, with 19.2% (2023) and 21.6% (2024) either side - strong and consistent. Caveat flagged by the reviewer: no operating-income tag exists, so EBIT is proxied as pretax income + interest expense, and cash is missing from the FY2022-25 join (invested capital overstated ~3-5%, i.e. true ROIC slightly higher). Directionally the pass is not close to marginal.

rules.name: Balance sheet not competing with you
rules.note: RLI is a P&C insurer, so net debt / EBITDA is not a meaningful leverage measure - the liability side is loss reserves and unearned premium, not debt. For reference, gross debt is $100M against $1.78B of equity, under 0.2x the EBITDA proxy of $519M, i.e. effectively unlevered. Marked null per the rule rather than credited as a pass.

rules.name: Why competitors cannot take the business
rules.note: RLI writes hard-to-price specialty and E&S niches (personal umbrella, marine, surety, transportation) where underwriters are owner-operators - employee share ownership ties pay to underwriting profit, producing roughly 45-50 consecutive years of underwriting profit. That is a cultural and data advantage a competitor can only match by losing money for a decade first; it is not price competition.

rules.name: Management treats the dividend as a promise
rules.threshold: no cut in FY2020/2021; any cut in window fails
rules.note: Regular DPS rose through 2020 and 2021 and in every one of the 17 year-over-year steps in the window; cutsOrHolds is empty. RLI even paid a $0.50 special in 2020. FY2008 is outside the XBRL window and cannot be checked from the data.

analysis.assessment: RLI is a superbly run $5.6B specialty insurer that fails this screen on the two things the screen exists to find: the regular yield is 1.06% (0.64 run-rate DPS on a $60.54 price) and regular dividend growth is 5.81% over five years. The snowball is real but slow on the regular line - $0.63 of FY2025 regular dividends consumed just 9.5% of $608.7M of free cash flow, and total dividends including the $2.00 special were 39.7%, so there is enormous unused runway. The reason the runway stays unused is deliberate: RLI routes the bulk of its capital return through an annual special (a $2.00 special in each of 2024, 2025 and again in mid-2026), which is what makes the TTM yield look like 7.7% and the regular yield look like 1.1%. Quality is not in question - ROIC 21.7%, FCF compounding at 18.8%/yr versus a 5.8% dividend, effectively no debt against $1.78B of equity, and a roughly 50-year raise record. The thing most likely to break the compounding is not the dividend but the entry price: at 1.06% starting yield you need a decade of 6% raises just to reach a 2% yield on cost, and a single soft market in E&S pricing would shrink the specials long before the regular dividend is ever at risk.

screenFields.streakSource: research; data confirms 17 years (window-limited, reaches FY2008)
screenFields.payoutBasis: total dividends paid (regular + special) / FCF (CFO - capex); regular dividend alone is 9.5% of FCF

No change: the live regular run rate of 0.64 (4 x 0.16) is confirmed against FY2025's filed 0.63 plus the Q1-2026 step. Noted only because the Q2-2026 fact implies 0.18/qtr (0.72) from here, which would move the yield to 1.19%.

analysis.moat: RLI writes hard-to-price specialty and E&S niches with owner-operator underwriters paid on underwriting profit, giving it roughly 45-50 straight years of underwriting profit that a price-cutting competitor cannot replicate without first losing money for a decade.
analysis.sectorNote: RLI is a P&C insurer. Rule 8 (net debt / EBITDA) is not meaningful for an insurer - leverage lives in loss reserves, not debt - so it is marked null; gross debt of $100M against $1.78B of equity is immaterial in any case. Rule 4 uses FCF = CFO - capex, which the rule permits for insurers; the same rule's ratio is computed on total dividends including the special, because RLI's regular dividend is deliberately small and the specials are where the real payout sits. Rule 7's ROIC uses a pretax-income-plus-interest EBIT proxy because no operating-income tag exists in an insurer's filing set.
strengths: ROIC 21.7% in FY2025 (19.2% and 21.6% in the two prior years) with essentially no financial leverage.
FCF compounding at 18.8%/yr over five years versus a 5.8% dividend CAGR - coverage widening every year.
Regular dividend consumes only 9.5% of FCF and 14.3% of net income; the special absorbs the variability, so the regular dividend is close to unbreakable.
Roughly 50 years of consecutive increases, with 17 of them verified in-window including uninterrupted raises through 2020.
FY2025 FCF margin of 32.3% on $1.88B of revenue, with revenue up 91% over five years.
risks: Starting regular yield of 1.06% is far below the usable band; the dividend snowball from here is tiny without price appreciation.
Regular growth of 5.81% is well under the 8% bar and has been remarkably steady - there is no sign management intends to accelerate the regular line rather than the specials.

The headline 7.7% TTM yield is specials-driven and discretionary; a soft E&S pricing cycle would cut the special (as it did between 2022's $3.50 and 2023's $1.00) with no dividend 'cut' ever being declared.
Underwriting results are inherently catastrophe-exposed: FY2018 net income fell to $64.2M and FY2022 pretax income of $720.7M included a one-off gain, so single-year earnings are noisy.
Data caveats: EBIT/EBITDA are a pretax-plus-interest proxy (no operating-income tag), cash is missing for FY2022-25, and the 50-year streak cannot be proven from an 18-year XBRL window.

stocks.m: Primerica reaches middle-income households that no direct-to-consumer insurer can profitably advertise to, through 130,000 licensed part-time reps recruited from that same demographic over fifty years - a distribution network, not a product, and one that cannot be bought or rebuilt at the price of a term-life premium.

normalised.dpsMethod: Rule (a): filed annual CommonStockDividendsPerShareDeclared (10-K, FY duration 364-365 days) for every fiscal year 2010-2025, used as filed with no split adjustment (splitFacts is empty; Primerica has not split since its April 2010 IPO). The one genuinely INDEPENDENT cross-check is divPaid/sharesBasic, which agrees with the filed DPS within 0.13%-4.16% in all 16 dividend-paying years (max deviation is FY2010, the partial initiation year). Quarterly facts are a rate-pattern check only, NOT an independent confirmation of the annual total: no fiscal year in dpsAllFacts contains four separately tagged quarterly rate facts - Q4 is never tagged in any of the 16 years, the maximum available is Q1-Q3 (FY2012-FY2025), FY2011 has a single quarterly fact (Q3 $0.03) and FY2010 has none. Any Q4 rate must be backed out of the filed annual figure, which makes it circular with respect to the number it would be confirming.

specials.note: No special dividends. splitFacts is empty, live.regularDividendIfSpecial is null, and in every one of the 16 dividend-paying years divPaid/sharesBasic lands 0.13%-4.16% ABOVE the filed declared DPS (timing of Q4 declaration vs payment). A special dividend shows the opposite signature - filed DPS far ABOVE cash paid per share in one year - and no year shows that. FY2024's rise to $3.30 is a step-up, not a special: the tagged quarterly rate moved from $0.75 (Q1, Q2) to $0.90 (Q3), and the implied Q4 of $0.90 (3.30 - 2.40 YTD-Q3) is the same rate, so the raise landed in Q3 2024 and carried forward. FY2025 is a flat $1.04 in each of Q1-Q3 with an implied Q4 of $1.04.

issues: CONFIDENCE IS SPLIT. Dividend series: HIGH confidence - filed annual tag on every one of 16 years, no splits, divPaid/sharesBasic agrees within 0.13%-4.16% in all 16 years, no specials, streak and CAGRs all recompute exactly. Balance-sheet and profitability fields: LOW confidence - netDebt/netDebtToEbitda null for 14 of 17 years including the latest, capex null for 13 of 17 years, ROIC computed with debt forced to zero in the denominator, EBITDA nulled for the last two years, and FY2025 net income not derivable on the filed basis. The object-level flag is therefore 'medium', not 'high'.

BLOCK FIXED - FY2025 NET INCOME SET TO NULL. The reviewer is right. The extract's NetIncomeLoss family runs 2009-2024 with a 2013 gap and has NO point for 2025-12-31. The previous record substituted pretax minus tax ($974,564,000 - $223,330,000 = $751,234,000) and presented it beside FY2022-FY2024 payoutNi figures computed on the FILED tag. Those two bases are demonstrably not the same series in this dataset. Recomputing pretax-tax against filed NetIncomeLoss for every year with both: FY2011 0.00%, FY2012 -0.29%, FY2014 -0.87%, FY2015 0.00%, FY2016 0.00%, FY2017 0.00%, FY2018 0.00%, FY2019 0.00%, FY2020 0.00%, FY2021 -0.29%, then FY2022 +17.51% ($554,714k derived vs $472,068k filed), FY2023 +2.53% ($591,182k vs $576,601k), FY2024 +53.05% ($720,129k vs $470,518k - a $249.6m gap). Because FY2024 uses the filed tag and FY2025 would have used the derived one, the previously reported fall in payoutNi from 23.98% to 18.11% was an artefact of switching bases, not a real move. fin[2025].netIncome, fin[2025].payoutNi and latest.payoutNi are therefore null. The filed figure IS retrievable - families.netIncome.candidates lists NetIncomeLossAvailableToCommonStockholdersBasic (15 points, 2010-2025) and ProfitLoss (15 points, 2011-2025), both of which cover 2025-12-31 - but neither series was pulled into this extract, so it must be fetched rather than substituted.

FY2024 AND FY2022 FILED NET INCOME ARE THEMSELVES SUSPECT (kept, but do not compare payoutNi across years). The FY2024 NetIncomeLoss point of $470,518,000 implies an effective tax rate of 1 - 470,518/939,247 = 49.9%, against the filed IncomeTaxExpenseBenefit/pretax of 219,118/939,247 = 23.3%. It also falls 18.4% from FY2023's $576,601,000 while revenue rose 12.4% ($3,089m vs $2,749m), pretax rose 21.7% ($939.2m vs $771.7m) and tax rose 21.4%. FY2022 shows the same pattern (implied ETR 34.3% vs filed 22.8%). Both are most likely mis-scoped contexts (segment, parent-only Schedule II, or a restated fact) rather than the consolidated attributable figure. They are the filed primary tag so they are retained under the never-invent rule, but payoutNi for FY2022 and FY2024 is NOT comparable with FY2011-FY2021. On a consistent pretax-minus-tax basis the same years would read: FY2022 0.1510, FY2023 0.1585, FY2024 0.1567.

FY2013 NET INCOME IS DERIVED AND IS KEPT (unlike FY2025). fin[2013].netIncome = $158,701,000 = pretax $245,006,000 minus tax $86,305,000, because NetIncomeLoss has no 2013-12-31 point. Unlike FY2025 the derivation is locally validated: the immediately adjacent years reconcile tightly on the same basis (FY2012 -0.29%, FY2014 -0.87%), and the whole FY2011-FY2021 block reconciles within 0.9%. FY2025's adjacent year (FY2024) diverges by 53%, so the basis is not validated there. payoutNi for FY2013 (0.1579) rests on this derived denominator.

EBITDA NULLED FOR FY2024 AND FY2025 (convention break, reviewer accepted remedy). EBITDA is opIncome + D&A with opIncome taken as pretax + InterestExpense, since no operating-income tag exists. The InterestExpense family stops at 2023-12-31 and the table carries no interest value for FY2024 or FY2025, so opIncome is not derivable for those years. The previous record reported $957,447,000 and $993,864,000 on a pretax + D&A basis, understating them by roughly the $26.6-30.6m interest run-rate (about 2.7-3.1% of EBITDA) versus every earlier year - above the comparability threshold, and the schema has no per-row basis marker to make the break machine-visible. The alternative tag InterestPaidNet (10 points, 2016-2025) would close the gap but its series is not included in this extract, so it cannot be pulled. Both years are therefore null. Nothing is lost downstream: netDebtToEbitda is null for those years anyway for want of a debt tag.

ROIC IS RETAINED FOR FY2024-FY2025 DESPITE THE SAME MISSING INTEREST, and here is the justification. ROIC = opIncome x (1 - tax/pretax) / (equity + debt - cash). For FY2024-FY2025 opIncome falls back to pretax alone, which UNDERSTATES the numerator by about 2.8%; meanwhile the debt-free denominator OVERSTATES ROIC by roughly 25-30% relative. The denominator error dominates and is disclosed below, so the figure is directionally caveated either way, whereas nulling would remove the latest-year ROIC entirely. EBITDA by contrast is a level series whose only consumer is already null, so a silent break there is pure cost. Recomputed and confirmed: FY2024 939,247 x (1 - 0.23329) / (2,259,041 - 687,821) = 0.4583; FY2025 974,564 x (1 - 0.22916) / (2,445,902 - 756,227) = 0.4446.

NET DEBT: not derivable for 14 of 17 years including the latest. The debtLT family (LongTermDebt) has only 2 points (FY2011 $300.0m, FY2012 $374.4m) and there is no debtCur family at all, so netDebt and netDebtToEbitda are null for FY2009-FY2010 and FY2013-FY2025. Computed only for FY2011 ($300,000k - $136,078k = $163,922k, 0.5872x EBITDA) and FY2012 ($374,433k - $112,214k = $262,219k, 0.8588x). Primerica demonstrably carries senior notes throughout (interest expense of $26.6-35.0m runs every year from 2011 to 2023 in the table), but no debt tag was captured, so the balance is not in the data. The external reviewer's suggestion to insert an externally-known ~$600m senior-note balance is declined: that would be inventing a number the extract does not contain. The honest statement is that leverage cannot be measured from this record, only that non-zero debt exists and the interest run-rate is small relative to $900m+ of CFO.

ROIC IS COMPUTED WITH DEBT = ZERO in the invested-capital denominator for every year except FY2011 and FY2012, because the debt tags are missing. That overstates ROIC for FY2013-FY2025 by roughly the ratio of debt to equity. issues.detail: Null for the latest year because the LongTermDebt family stops at FY2012, yet Primerica demonstrably carries senior notes throughout the period (the record concedes this). Leaving leverage null for a dividend-safety record removes the one metric that would stress-test the payout, and it also means roic 0.4446 is computed with debt = 0 in invested capital (self-flagged as ~25-30% relative overstatement).
issues.suggested: Pull the debt figure from the DebtInstrumentFaceAmount / SeniorNotes or LongTermDebtNoncurrent tags, or state the externally-known ~$600m senior note balance explicitly as an estimate: against FY2025 EBITDA of $993.9m that is well under 1.0x gross, so the dividend-safety conclusion is unchanged — but say so rather than leaving the field null and silent.

rules.name: Small enough to grow
rules.note: live marketCap $9,102,923,775 at $291.91 (2026-09-17). Comfortably under $15B but not in the ideal sub-$5B band; the shrinking share count (72.1m basic in 2010 to 32.6m in 2025) means market cap understates how much per-share compounding is still available.

rules.name: Starting yield in the usable band
rules.note: Current declared quarterly rate is $1.20 (2026 Q1 and Q2 both tagged), so the regular annual DPS on the current basis is $4.80 = 1.64%. TTM $4.64 = 1.59%. The stale FY2025 filed total of $4.16 = 1.43% would fail; every current-basis measure passes, but only just - this is a bottom-of-band yield and the whole case rests on growth.

rules.name: Dividend growth above 8%/yr
rules.note: STRONG. g3 23.66%, g10 20.58%, and the 2026 raise to $1.20/qtr is another +15.4% on an annualised basis. No split adjustment needed (no split since the April 2010 IPO). gMax of 42.74% is an artefact of the $0.02 initiation base and is not used.

rules.name: Payout with room left
rules.note: FAILS THE FLOOR, NOT THE CEILING - this is under-distribution, not strain. Insurer, so FCF = CFO - capex is the right basis, but no capex tag exists FY2013-FY2025 so the denominator is unreduced CFO; where capex was disclosed it ran 1.4-5.3% of CFO, so a true FCF payout is roughly 15-16%, still below 20%. On net income it is the same story: ~15.7-16.3% on a consistent pretax-minus-tax basis (FY2023 15.85%, FY2024 15.67%). Primerica returns far more through buybacks - $450.0m in FY2025 - so dividends plus repurchases are 65.0% of CFO.

rules.name: Streak long enough to prove policy, short enough to still be fast
rules.note: Not window-limited: FY2009 is present in the data with zero dividends paid and the IPO was April 2010, so the streak provably cannot extend earlier. Prior research says 16, which counts FY2010's $0.02 initiation over a zero base; the conservative 15 is used. Either figure sits mid-band.

rules.name: Earnings growing at least as fast as the dividend
rules.note: THE CENTRAL TENSION. CFO grew from $643.4m (FY2020) to $901.2m (FY2025), 6.97%/yr, while the dividend grew three times faster. Net income is not a usable cross-check here - the filed NetIncomeLoss tag is internally inconsistent in FY2022 and FY2024 (implied effective tax rates of 34.3% and 49.9% against filed 22.8% and 23.3%) and has no FY2025 point. Revenue grew 8.2%/yr FY2020-FY2025 ($2,217.5m to $3,291.7m), so ~7-8% is the honest underlying rate. The gap has been funded by payout-ratio expansion off a very low base plus a 19% reduction in share count over the same five years.

rules.name: High return on invested capital
rules.note: STRONG even after heavy haircutting. Computed as pretax x (1 - 22.9%) / (equity $2,445.9m - cash $756.2m) with debt forced to zero because no debt tag exists after FY2012; the record's own estimate is that this overstates ROIC by 25-30% relative, which still leaves ~32-35%. FY2021's 93.6% is an AOCI-driven equity-collapse artefact and is ignored. The trend FY2016-FY2025 (23.6% -> 44.5%) is genuine and reflects a capital-light agent-distribution model.

rules.name: Balance sheet not competing with you
rules.value: null (insurer; also not derivable after FY2012)
rules.note: Two reasons for null. (a) Primerica is a life insurer - net debt/EBITDA is not a meaningful solvency measure for a business whose liabilities are policy reserves; RBC ratio is the right metric and is not in this data. (b) Mechanically, the LongTermDebt family stops at FY2012, so leverage cannot be measured from the extract at all. What can be said: where it was measurable it was low (0.59x in FY2011, 0.86x in FY2012), interest expense ran only $26.6-35.0m/yr against $900m+ of CFO through FY2023, and cash was $756.2m at FY2025. No evidence of balance-sheet stress; no measured figure either.

rules.name: Why competitors cannot take the business
rules.value: 130,000-rep licensed sales force selling term life to middle-income households
rules.note: The moat is distribution, not product. Term life is a commodity; reaching a household earning $50-100k that will not seek out insurance is not. Primerica recruits its reps from the same demographic it sells to, licenses them, and pays them as independent contractors - a network built over 50 years that no direct-to-consumer insurer has replicated, because the customer acquisition cost of reaching this segment through advertising exceeds the policy economics. The investment-products cross-sell rides the same force for free.

rules.name: Management treats the dividend as a promise
rules.threshold: no cut in FY2020/2021; a cut anywhere in the window fails
rules.value: No cut or hold in 16 years of data
rules.note: DPS rose straight through the pandemic: $1.36 (2019) -> $1.60 (2020) -> $1.88 (2021). Zero flat years and zero cuts in the entire FY2010-FY2025 series. 2008 is outside the window and untestable - Primerica did not exist as a public company until the April 2010 IPO, so there is no financial-crisis behaviour to judge.

analysis.assessment: Primerica is a high-quality compounder whose dividend is simply too small yet: $4.80 annualised on a $291.91 share is a 1.64% starting yield, grown at 21.06%/yr over five years, and costing only 15.1% of $901.2m of operating cash flow. The payout runway is enormous - the ratio could triple and still sit inside a comfortable band - and ROIC of 44.5% (perhaps 33% after adjusting for the debt-free denominator the data forces) on a capital-light distribution model means the growth is self-funded. The thing most likely to break it is arithmetic, not credit: cash flow is compounding at 6.97%/yr against a dividend compounding at 21.06%, so the last decade of raises has been payout-ratio expansion plus a 55% reduction in share count since 2010, and once the ratio reaches a normal 30-40% the dividend must decelerate toward the high single digits unless Primerica finds growth. The real risk is the sales force - 130,000 reps is the entire moat, and recruitment stalling would hit new-policy issuance, investment-product flows and the buyback that levers per-share results all at once. Leverage is unmeasurable from this data (no debt tag after FY2012) and net income for FY2025 is not retrievable on the filed basis, so the safety case rests on cash flow, which is unambiguous.
analysis.moat: Primerica reaches middle-income households that no direct-to-consumer insurer can profitably advertise to, through 130,000 licensed part-time reps recruited from that same demographic over fifty years - a distribution network, not a product, and one that cannot be bought or rebuilt at the price of a term-life premium.
analysis.sectorNote: PRI is a life insurer, so rule 8 is marked null on principle (policy reserves are not debt and net debt/EBITDA is not a solvency measure here; RBC ratio would be the right test and is absent from the data) - and separately no debt tag exists after FY2012, so it is not computable either way. For rule 4 the insurer convention FCF = CFO - capex is used as instructed, but capex is untagged FY2013-FY2025 so the denominator is unreduced CFO; disclosed capex historically ran 1.4-5.3% of CFO, so the true FCF payout is roughly 15-16% rather than 15.1% and the rule-4 conclusion is unchanged. Rule 6 is judged on CFO rather than net income because the filed NetIncomeLoss series is internally inconsistent in FY2022 and FY2024 and missing for FY2025.

Management clearly prefers buybacks: $450.0m of repurchases against $136.1m of dividends in FY2025, so the dividend is the residual claim on capital allocation, not the priority

Prior counted FY2010's $0.02 as an increase, but that was the initiation year over a zero base (April 2010 IPO; FY2009 dividends paid = $0). The defensible count of consecutive increases is 15, FY2011 through FY2025. Not window-limited.

stocks.m: SIGI is a top-tier carrier inside a deliberately small panel of about 1,500 independent agencies, with field underwriters embedded in those territories and decades of state- and class-level loss data - an agent's book and the pricing edge behind it do not move to a cheaper entrant.

normalised.dpsMethod: Filed annual CommonStockDividendsPerShareDeclared (10-K, ~364-365 day durations, FY2008-FY2025) used as-is. No split adjustment applied anywhere: splitFacts is empty, sharesBasic rises smoothly 52.6M -> 60.9M with no step change, and DPS rises smoothly with no r-multiple outlier. Every year was independently cross-checked against the sum of the four quarterly rate facts in dpsAllFacts (deriving Q4 = FY minus the 9-month YTD fact) and all years with complete quarterly coverage reconcile exactly (e.g. FY2017 0.16+0.16+0.16+0.18=0.66; FY2025 0.38*3+0.43=1.57). divPaid/sharesBasic was computed for every year as a third check.

specials.note: No special dividends found. divPaid/sharesBasic sits 2.4%-6.1% BELOW filed DPS in every single year (never above), which is the opposite of the special-dividend signature; the gap is structural (cash paid vs declared, and dividends not paid on all weighted-average shares), not a one-off. live.regularDividendIfSpecial is null and live.ttmDividend 1.72 = 4 x the current 0.43 quarterly rate, confirming a pure regular dividend.

issues: DPS itself is high-confidence: filed annual tag for all 18 years, and every year with full quarterly coverage reconciles exactly to the sum of four quarterly rate facts (FY2014 0.13x3+0.14=0.53; FY2017 0.16x3+0.18=0.66; FY2020 0.23x3+0.25=0.94; FY2025 0.38x3+0.43=1.57). No conflicting DPS tag exists.

NO SPLIT ADJUSTMENT MADE ANYWHERE. splitFacts is empty; sharesBasic rises monotonically and smoothly (52.63M in 2009 to 60.87M in 2024, then -0.4% in 2025 on buybacks) with no step change; DPS shows no r-multiple discontinuity. splitAdjustments is an empty list and no fiscal year had DPS divided or shares multiplied.

CROSS-CHECK divPaid/sharesBasic vs filed DPS: the implied figure is BELOW filed DPS in all 17 years, by 2.4% (2024, 2025) up to 6.1% (2010). Four years breach the ~5% band: FY2010 -6.1%, FY2011 -5.7%, FY2012 -5.6%, FY2013 -5.2%. Judgement call: these are NOT specials (a special would push implied ABOVE filed) and not a split (the gap is smooth and monotonically shrinking, not a step). In 2010-2013 the rate was flat at $0.13/qtr so declared-vs-paid timing cannot explain it either; the residual is dividends not paid on all weighted-average shares (unvested/restricted and treasury timing). Filed DPS was kept in every case.

CFO: the primary tag NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities has no data for FY2013-FY2016. Judgement call: those four years were filled from NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivitiesContinuingOperations (2013 336,124k; 2014 232,763k; 2015 381,580k; 2016 329,509k), which matches the primary tag exactly in the four overlap years (2011, 2012, 2017, 2018), so the splice is safe.

CAPEX MISSING FY2011-FY2017 (7 years): PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment has no facts for those years. tagHints shows the filer used PaymentsForProceedsFromProductiveAssets in that period (11 points, last value 30,986k at 2019-12-31, identical to the PP&E tag's 2019 value, confirming it is the same line item), but that tag's series was not included in this extract, so no values are available. capex, fcf and payoutFcf are null for FY2011-FY2017 and capexTag names PaymentsForProceedsFromProductiveAssets for those years. Nothing was interpolated.

FY2025 DEBT NOT DERIVABLE: the LongTermDebt tag ends at FY2024 and the FY2025 balance sits in LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligationsIncludingCurrentMaturities, whose series was not included in this extract. netDebt, netDebtToEbitda and roic are therefore null for FY2025 (its invested-capital denominator cannot be completed). Interest expense jumped from 28.9M to 49.3M, so debt is clearly not zero; treating it as zero would have overstated ROIC by roughly 14% relative (0.140 instead of about 0.123 at FY2024's 507.9M debt level), so the field was left null rather than filled with an assumption. latest.roic and latest.netDebtToEbitda are consequently null.

opIncome is not tagged for this filer. Judgement call: EBITDA was built as pretax + InterestExpenseDebt + DepreciationAmortizationAndAccretionNet, and the same pretax+interest EBIT proxy drives ROIC. For a P&C insurer this proxy swings hard with underwriting and realised-investment results, so EBITDA and netDebt/EBITDA are volatile year to year (4.77x in 2011 on a 64.3M EBITDA vs 0.86x in 2021) and should not be read as a leverage trend.

debtCur (ShortTermBorrowings) exists only for FY2015 (60,000k) and FY2016 (0). All other years were treated as zero short-term debt in netDebt and ROIC. If the filer had untagged short-term borrowings, netDebt is understated in those years.

The cash tag used is 'Cash' (811k in 2009, 346k in 2025) - an insurer's bare operating cash line, not cash equivalents. CashCashEquivalentsRestrictedCashAndRestrictedCashEquivalents exists (11 points, 2015-2025) but its series was not supplied. Net debt is therefore effectively gross debt and is overstated versus a cash-and-equivalents definition.

Effective tax rate is negative or near-zero in FY2009 (-14.0%), FY2011 (-99.0%) and FY2012 (-0.9%) from the filed tax/pretax ratio, which inflates NOPAT and hence ROIC in those three years. The filed ratio was used as instructed rather than the 21% fallback (which applies only when the ratio is underivable).

payoutNi uses NetIncomeLoss, which is before the preferred dividend (PaymentsOfDividendsPreferredStockAndPreferenceStock, 9,200k/yr, 8 points). Payout on income available to common would be about 2% higher in relative terms from FY2018 on. divPaid correctly uses PaymentsOfDividendsCommonStock and excludes preferred.

payoutFcf is flatteringly low (7.8%-17.1%) because an insurer's CFO includes float/reserve growth; it is not comparable to an industrial's FCF payout. This replaces priorEstimates.payoutPctFcf of 30%, which was materially too high.

priorEstimates were not used and are contradicted: its streak of 13 is one year too high (the true run of strictly rising DPS is 12 years, FY2014-FY2025; FY2013 was flat at 0.52 and breaks it), and its growth5y of 8% understates the actual 5-year DPS CAGR of 10.8%.

FY2008 appears in dps (0.52, filed) and in divPaid (25,804k) but has no row in the table (sharesBasic and most balance-sheet tags start at FY2009), so it is excluded from fin and could not be cross-checked against divPaid/shares.

Post-window information, not used in any field: quarterly facts for 2026 show 0.43 in Q1 and Q2, consistent with live.ttmDividend of 1.72 (4 x 0.43) and implying FY2026 DPS of at least 1.72, about 9.6% above FY2025.
fcfGrowth5 (17.6%/yr, FY2020 to FY2025) is flattered by the FY2024-FY2025 CFO surge (1,099.9M and 1,233.0M vs 758.9M in FY2023); it reflects reserve/float dynamics as much as earnings power.

normalised.notes: SIGI, December fiscal year end, calendar-year labels throughout. Clean case: no stock splits (splitFacts empty, no share-count step, no DPS discontinuity), no special dividends, and a single uncontested DPS tag whose annual values reconcile exactly to the filed quarterly rates in every year with full quarterly coverage. Regular DPS ran flat at 0.52 for six straight years (FY2008-FY2013), then rose every year from FY2014 to FY2025 - a 12-year streak of strictly rising DPS ending at 1.57, with no cut or hold in 2020 or 2021. DPS CAGRs: 11.3% over 3 years, 10.8% over 5, 10.7% over 10, and 6.7% over the full 17-year window (dragged down by the 2008-2013 freeze). Coverage is very comfortable: FY2025 payout is 19.9% of net income and 7.8% of FCF, on FCF of 1,194.3M against 92.9M of common dividends. The gaps in the record are all on the financial-statement side, not the dividend side: capex is missing for FY2011-FY2017 (filer used PaymentsForProceedsFromProductiveAssets, whose series was not extracted, so FCF is null for those seven years), CFO for FY2013-FY2016 was spliced from the continuing-operations tag, and FY2025 debt is untagged in this extract so net debt, net debt/EBITDA and ROIC are null for the latest year.

It is fully explained — the quarterly rate stepped 0.38 -> 0.43 in FY2025 Q4, so the TTM as of 2026-09-17 is 4 x 0.43 = 1.72, and the record's own notes flag 2026 Q1/Q2 facts of 0.43. The derivation rule nulls ROIC only when equity is missing; here the blocker is that no debt series is supplied for 2025 (LongTermDebt ends 2024, and LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligationsIncludingCurrentMaturities appears in debtLT.candidates with a 2025 point but its series is null in the file). issues.detail: EBITDA and the ROIC numerator use a pretax+InterestExpenseDebt EBIT proxy because opIncome is untagged, which departs from the stated rule EBITDA = opIncome + da. Recomputation confirms the record applied this proxy consistently and correctly in all 17 years, but it makes the series non-comparable with tickers where opIncome exists. Compounding this, the filed effective tax ratio is negative or near zero in FY2009 (-14.0%), FY2011 (-99.0%) and FY2012 (-0.9%), inflating NOPAT and hence ROIC of 0.05231, 0.04324 and 0.04078 in those years.
issues.suggested: Retain the values (they follow the documented substitution) but mark ebitda, netDebtToEbitda and roic as proxy-based and not cross-ticker comparable; consider publishing FY2011/FY2012 ROIC as null rather than as a number driven by a -99% tax ratio.

issues.detail: Net debt uses the bare 'Cash' tag (811k in 2009 down to 346k in 2025) rather than cash and equivalents; CashCashEquivalentsRestrictedCashAndRestrictedCashEquivalents exists as a candidate (11 points, 2015-2025) but its series was not supplied. Net debt is therefore effectively gross debt in every year. Separately, ShortTermBorrowings is present only for FY2015 (60,000k) and FY2016 (0); all other years assume zero short-term debt.
issues.suggested: Keep the figures, but label netDebt as 'gross debt less operating cash' and flag that a cash-and-equivalents refetch would lower net debt materially in FY2015-FY2025.

issues.detail: Seven of seventeen years (FY2011-FY2017) have null capex and hence null FCF and payoutFcf, because PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment has no points there and the filer's PaymentsForProceedsFromProductiveAssets series (11 points, last 30,986k at 2019-12-31, identical to the PP&E tag's 2019 value) was not included in the extract. The record correctly names the tag in capexTag and interpolates nothing, but 41% of the FCF history is unusable and fcfGrowth5 rests on only the post-2018 window.
issues.suggested: Refetch PaymentsForProceedsFromProductiveAssets to fill FY2011-FY2017 capex; until then flag fcfGrowth5 (17.6%) as a short-window figure flattered by the FY2024-FY2025 CFO surge, as the record already notes.

rules.name: Small enough to grow
rules.note: live marketCap 5,276,388,000 at $88.53 on 2026-09-17. Comfortably under $15B and only just above the $5B ideal line - a genuine small/mid-cap where incremental premium growth still moves the needle.

rules.name: Starting yield in the usable band
rules.note: Current run-rate: 4 x $0.43 quarterly = $1.72 annual / $88.53 = 1.94%. On the filed FY2025 declared DPS of $1.57 it is 1.77%. Both sit in the band; no special dividend is involved (ttmDividend 1.72 is exactly 4 x the current rate).

rules.name: Dividend growth above 8%/yr
rules.note: 5-yr DPS CAGR FY2020 0.94 -> FY2025 1.57 = 10.80%; 3-yr 11.26%, 10-yr 10.66%. Above the 8% bar but short of the 12% 'strong' line. The 17-yr CAGR is only 6.72% because DPS was frozen at $0.52 through FY2008-FY2013.

rules.name: Payout with room left
rules.note: Insurer basis used as instructed: FCF = CFO - capex = 1,233.0M - 38.7M = 1,194.3M against 92.9M of common dividends = 7.78%. Below the 20% floor, so the rule fails - but it fails for the benign reason (too much cover, not too little). An insurer's CFO includes float and reserve growth, so the FCF figure overstates true distributable cash; payout on net income is 19.9%, also a hair under the floor. Either way SIGI is retaining capital rather than returning it.

rules.name: Streak long enough to prove policy
rules.note: Strictly rising FY2014-FY2025. NOT window-limited: the data reaches back to FY2008 and shows six flat years at $0.52 (FY2008-FY2013) that genuinely break any longer run. Data streak used (12), not priorEstimates' 13, which is one year too high.

rules.name: Earnings growing at least as fast as the dividend
rules.note: FCF FY2020 532.0M -> FY2025 1,194.3M = 17.56%/yr. The FCF line is flattered by the FY2024-FY2025 CFO surge (1,099.9M and 1,233.0M vs 758.9M in FY2023), which is as much reserve/float as earnings power, so net income was checked as a backstop: 246.4M -> 466.4M = 13.62%/yr, still comfortably ahead of the 10.80% dividend. Passes on both measures.

rules.name: High return on invested capital
rules.note: FY2025 ROIC is not derivable - the FY2025 debt balance sits in an untagged series in this extract, so the invested-capital denominator cannot be completed. Last computable years: FY2024 6.35%, FY2023 11.23%, FY2021 12.24% (the only year over 12 in the whole record). Reviewer's estimate at FY2024's debt level puts FY2025 near 12.3%, but FY2025 interest expense of 49.3M (vs 28.9M) implies materially more debt, which would pull it back under. All figures are a pretax+interest EBIT proxy because opIncome is untagged, so they are not cross-ticker comparable. Honest read: SIGI earns roughly 8-12% on capital through a cycle - a decent insurer, not a high-ROIC compounder.

rules.name: Balance sheet not competing with you
rules.note: Not meaningful for an insurer: the balance sheet is dominated by an investment portfolio backing policy reserves, and the EBITDA denominator here is a pretax+interest proxy that swings with underwriting and realised investment results (4.77x in 2011 on 64.3M EBITDA vs 0.86x in 2021). For context, FY2024 gross debt was 507.8M against 321.7M of proxy EBITDA (1.58x) and equity of ~3.6B - modest financial leverage. The real constraint is statutory capital and premium-to-surplus, not this ratio.

rules.name: Why competitors cannot take the business
rules.note: SIGI is a top-two or top-three carrier inside a deliberately small panel of ~1,500 appointed independent agencies, backed by field underwriters physically embedded in those agencies' territories and by decades of state- and class-level loss data. An agency's book, quoting workflow and claims relationships move only at real cost, and a price-cutting entrant cannot buy the local loss experience that lets SIGI price small commercial accounts. It is a real mechanism, but a moderate one - pricing is still cyclical and reinsurance-driven.

rules.name: Management treats the dividend as a promise
rules.note: DPS rose 0.83 -> 0.94 (FY2020) -> 1.03 (FY2021), increases of 13.3% and 9.6% straight through the pandemic. No cut or suspension anywhere in the FY2008-FY2025 window; the worst behaviour on record is the six-year freeze at $0.52 after the financial crisis (FY2008 itself is at the edge of the window and its annual fact is not duration-verified). A freeze, not a cut, is the tail risk here.

analysis.assessment: SIGI is a $5.3B regional commercial P&C insurer yielding 1.94% on the current $0.43 quarterly rate ($1.72 annualised), with a 12-year run of increases compounding at 10.8% over five years and 11.3% over three - a classic low-yield, double-digit-growth snowball that roughly doubles your income every seven years and gets you to a ~4% yield-on-cost in about seven to eight years if the growth rate holds. Payout runway is the opposite of a constraint: $92.9M of common dividends against $1,194.3M of FCF (7.8%) and 19.9% of net income, low enough that it fails rule 4 from the safe side and leaves room for a decade of raises even if earnings stall. The weak spot is capital efficiency and cyclicality, not coverage: ROIC has only cleared 12% once in seventeen years (12.24% in FY2021) and was 6.35% in FY2024 when net income fell to $207M on reserve strengthening, and FY2025 ROIC cannot even be computed because the debt balance is missing from the extract while interest expense nearly doubled to $49.3M, implying a materially larger debt load. The thing most likely to break the snowball is not a cut but a freeze - management held DPS flat at $0.52 for six straight years after 2008, and a hard reserve-development year or a soft pricing cycle in commercial lines is exactly the trigger that would do it again. Buy it for the growth rate, size it for the fact that a P&C underwriting cycle can pause that growth without warning.
analysis.moat: SIGI is a top-tier carrier inside a deliberately small panel of about 1,500 independent agencies, with field underwriters embedded in those territories and decades of state- and class-level loss data - an agent's book and the pricing edge behind it do not move to a cheaper entrant.
analysis.sectorNote: P&C insurer. Rule 8 (net debt/EBITDA) is marked null: the balance sheet is an investment portfolio backing reserves and the EBITDA here is a pretax+InterestExpenseDebt proxy (opIncome untagged), so the ratio is noise - FY2024 was 1.58x on gross debt of 507.8M and it swung from 4.77x to 0.86x on underwriting results alone. Rule 4 was read on the instructed insurer basis (FCF = CFO - capex) giving 7.8%, but CFO includes float and reserve growth so that number is structurally flattering; the net-income payout of 19.9% is the fairer read and is quoted alongside. Rule 7 ROIC is likewise a proxy and not comparable with non-financial tickers.
strengths: 12 consecutive annual increases (FY2014-FY2025) with no cut anywhere in the 18-year window, and double-digit raises straight through 2020 and 2021
Dividend growth of 10.8% over 5 years and 11.3% over 3, well clear of the 8% bar and accelerating (FY2025 -> current run-rate is +9.6% again)
Enormous coverage: 92.9M of common dividends against 1,194.3M FCF and 466.4M of net income - a 19.9% net-income payout leaves a decade of raises available without earnings growth
Earnings outgrowing the dividend on both measures: 5-yr FCF CAGR 17.6% and net income CAGR 13.6% vs DPS 10.8%
$5.28B market cap - small enough that premium growth (revenue 2.92B -> 5.34B in five years) still compounds per share
risks: ROIC has cleared 12% only once in seventeen years (12.24% in FY2021) and was 6.35% in FY2024; this is a cyclical underwriter, not a high-return compounder

FY2025 net debt, net debt/EBITDA and ROIC are null in the extract while interest expense nearly doubled to 49.3M from 28.9M, implying gross debt well above FY2024's 507.8M - latest-year leverage is genuinely unknown and FY2024 must not be carried forward as a proxy

Precedent for a freeze: DPS was held flat at $0.52 for six consecutive years (FY2008-FY2013) after the financial crisis; adverse reserve development or a soft commercial pricing cycle is the realistic trigger for a repeat
FY2024 net income fell 43% to 207.0M on reserve strengthening, taking the net-income payout to 41.0% in a single year - the earnings line is far more volatile than the dividend line
Seven of seventeen years (FY2011-FY2017) have no capex and therefore no FCF, so the FCF history is only usable post-2018 and the 17.6% 5-yr FCF CAGR rests on a short, float-flattered window
Reserve and reinsurance pricing, not company execution, set the terms; commercial P&C competes hard on price when capacity is abundant

screenFields.payoutBasis: dividends / FCF (CFO - capex), insurer basis per rule 4; FCF is structurally flattered because an insurer's CFO includes float and reserve growth - payout on net income is 19.9%, which is the fairer read
screenFields.streakSource: data (12 strictly rising years FY2014-FY2025, not window-limited - the FY2008-FY2013 freeze is visible in the data); priorEstimates.streak of 13 is one year too high and was not used

estimateCorrections.why: Prior 30% was materially too high. Actual FY2025 common dividends of 92.9M against FCF of 1,194.3M (CFO 1,233.0M less capex 38.7M) is 7.78%; even on net income the figure is 19.9%. The 22pp gap changes the rule-4 read from mid-band to below-band-from-the-safe-side.

The true run of strictly rising DPS is 12 years, FY2014 (0.53) through FY2025 (1.57). FY2013 was flat at 0.52, the sixth consecutive year at that level, so it breaks the streak rather than extending it. Not window-limited - the data starts at FY2008.

5-yr DPS CAGR from filed annual DPS is 10.80% (0.94 FY2020 -> 1.57 FY2025), not 8%. A 2.8pp understatement - just under the materiality bar, but it is the difference between 'meets the 8% rule' and 'clears it with margin', and 3-yr growth is running higher still at 11.26%.

No change - live ttmDividend of 1.72 is confirmed as pure regular dividend (4 x the current 0.43 quarterly rate, corroborated by 2026 Q1 and Q2 facts of 0.43 each). Noted only because it sits 9.6% above the FY2025 declared figure of 1.57, so the screen should quote the run-rate, not the filed year.

stocks.m: Private-markets allocation and data: fee streams are contracted over 10+ year locked-up fund lives, and the Cobalt data set built from 35 years of GP diligence is an input rivals cannot replicate by spending.

normalised.dpsTag: us-gaap:CommonStockDividendsPerShareDeclared (reported only with the us-gaap:CommonClassAMember dimension, so it is absent from the companyfacts API and from the supplied extract)
normalised.dpsMethod: Filed annual DPS. The supplied extract had dpsAllFacts = [] because HLNE tags "Dividends declared per share of Class A common stock" ONLY with a share-class dimension (us-gaap:CommonStockDividendsPerShareDeclared + CommonClassAMember), and the SEC companyfacts API drops dimensioned facts — I confirmed this by pulling CIK 0001433642 companyfacts (no per-share dividend or weighted-share tags at all). I therefore read the annual DPS line straight off the Consolidated Statements of Income in each 10-K (R5.htm / primary document, FY2017-FY2026), which is the filed ~1-year-duration annual DPS value: FY2017 $—, FY2018 $0.70, FY2019 $0.85, FY2020 $1.10, FY2021 $1.25, FY2022 $1.40, FY2023 $1.60, FY2024 $1.78, FY2025 $1.96, FY2026 $2.16. Every year independently reconciles to 4x the quarterly rate disclosed in Item 5 "Dividend Policy" of the same 10-K ($0.175, $0.2125, $0.275, $0.3125, $0.35, $0.40, $0.445, $0.49, $0.54 respectively), and to declared dividends divided by weighted-average Class A shares within 0.2-4.0% (see issues). Dividends are paid on Class A common stock only; Class B/C receive HLA member distributions, which are NOT part of this series.

dps.basis: filed (income statement shows "$—"; IPO was 6 March 2017 and no dividend was declared before 31 March 2017)

specials.note: No special dividends. splitFacts and dpsAllFacts were empty in the extract; I checked every year's declared dividends against 4 x the disclosed quarterly rate and against declared-$ / weighted Class A shares, and no year shows an extra distribution. live.regularDividendIfSpecial is null and live.ttmDividend of 2.22 is simply three quarters at the FY2026 rate of $0.54 plus one quarter at the $0.60 rate declared 21 May 2026 (3 x 0.54 + 0.60 = 2.22), not a special. The separate cash items DistributionMadeToLimitedLiabilityCompanyLLCMemberCashDistributionsPaid ($54.1m in FY2026) are tax/member distributions to Class B/C holders of Hamilton Lane Advisors LLC, not common dividends, and are excluded.

issues: The supplied extract could not produce DPS at all: dpsAllFacts was empty, splitFacts was empty, coverSharesOutstanding was absent, and there is no shares family, so derivation rules (a), (b) and (c) were all unsatisfiable from the file as given. I pulled SEC companyfacts for CIK 0001433642 and confirmed the cause: HLNE reports both DPS and weighted-average shares only with a share-class (CommonClassAMember) dimension, and companyfacts omits dimensioned facts. DPS, quarterly rates and weighted-average basic Class A shares were therefore read from the 10-K financial statements themselves (Consolidated Statements of Income and the Earnings per Share note) for fiscal 2017-2026. These are filed figures, not estimates, but they come from the filing documents rather than the XBRL frames feed used to build the extract.

JUDGEMENT CALL - no splits. HLNE has never split its stock: splitFacts is empty, the DPS series is smooth, and every year's annual DPS equals exactly 4x the quarterly rate disclosed in that same 10-K, so no year sits on a different share basis. splitAdjustments is empty and no year's DPS or share count was divided or multiplied.

CROSS-CHECK DISAGREEMENT - FY2023 cash dividends paid. PaymentsOfDividends FY2023 = $72,409k, but the dividends-payable roll-forward gives declared $59,462k + opening payable $12,947k - closing payable $15,049k = $57,360k, an excess of exactly $15,049k (the closing payable). Every other year reconciles to the dollar (FY2018 $9,511k, FY2019 $18,676k, FY2020 $29,067k, FY2021 $39,676k, FY2022 $49,630k, FY2024 $65,406k, FY2025 $75,997k, FY2026 $87,711k all tie exactly). I verified $72,409k is what the FY2023 10-K cash flow statement shows and that the FY2025 10-K still carries $72,409k as the FY2023 comparative, so it was never restated. I kept the filed number, but FY2023 divPaid/share of $1.95 is 22% above the $1.60 declared DPS, and FY2023 payoutFcf (0.3264) and payoutNi (0.6636) are correspondingly overstated by roughly a quarter. Declared dividends for FY2023 (DividendsCommonStock = $59,462k) are the cleaner measure.

Cash dividends paid run about one quarter behind declarations in every year (declared at quarter end, paid the following month), so divPaid/sharesBasic is systematically below the filed DPS in a rising-rate year. The correct cross-check is declared dividends / weighted-average Class A shares, which matches filed DPS within 5% every year: FY2018 0.7279 vs 0.70 (+4.0%), FY2019 0.8582 vs 0.85 (+1.0%), FY2020 1.1186 vs 1.10 (+1.7%), FY2021 1.2925 vs 1.25 (+3.4%), FY2022 1.4071 vs 1.40 (+0.5%), FY2023 1.6045 vs 1.60 (+0.3%), FY2024 1.7958 vs 1.78 (+0.9%), FY2025 1.9689 vs 1.96 (+0.5%), FY2026 2.1631 vs 2.16 (+0.15%). The residual positive bias is expected: dividends are paid on shares outstanding at each record date, which exceeds the weighted average while the Class A count is growing through Class B/C exchanges and secondary offerings.

JUDGEMENT CALL - EBITDA. There is no operating-income family in the extract and no us-gaap:OperatingIncomeLoss fact in HLNE's companyfacts (HLNE's income statement has no 'income from operations' subtotal). I used opIncome = Total revenues - Total expenses (us-gaap:OperatingExpenses, verified against the filed 'Total expenses' line for FY2024-FY2026), then EBITDA = opIncome + D&A. This deliberately excludes equity in income of investees, non-operating gains and the consolidated funds/partnerships line, so EBITDA is conservative relative to the company's own Adjusted EBITDA. FY2016 EBITDA is null because no revenue fact exists for FY2016.

JUDGEMENT CALL - ROIC. Computed as opIncome (as above) x (1 - effective tax rate) / (equity + debtLT - cash), using the same conservative operating income; it is therefore understated versus a measure that credits equity-method income. Effective tax rates used: FY2017 0.4%, FY2018 23.9%, FY2019 23.6%, FY2020 9.9%, FY2021 12.6%, FY2022 21.2%, FY2023 22.9%, FY2024 19.3%, FY2025 13.4%, FY2026 16.3% - these are consolidated rates on pre-tax income that includes large non-controlling-interest income, so they are structurally low for a Up-C structure. FY2016 ROIC is null (no equity or revenue fact). FY2017-FY2019 ROIC (0.61-0.83) is inflated by a very small post-IPO equity base and should not be compared with later years.

Long-term debt was missing from the extract's table for FY2017-FY2019 (the LongTermDebt family only starts 2020-03-31 because those balances appear only as 10-Q comparatives). I filled FY2017 $84,310k, FY2018 $84,162k, FY2019 $70,954k from the filed 10-Q balance sheets so netDebt and ROIC are computable for those years. FY2016 netDebt is null - no debt fact exists.

No current-portion-of-debt tag exists for HLNE (LongTermDebtCurrent and LineOfCredit are absent from companyfacts), so netDebt = debtLT - cash with debtCur treated as zero. Cash is CashCashEquivalentsRestrictedCashAndRestrictedCashEquivalents, which includes restricted cash and cash of consolidated funds, so net debt is somewhat flattered; FY2026 net debt is negative (net cash of $93.5m) and its netDebtToEbitda of -0.28x should be read as 'no leverage', not as a meaningful multiple.

sharesBasic is weighted-average BASIC CLASS A shares only (Class B/C units of HLA are excluded, consistent with how the dividend is paid). FY2015, FY2016 and FY2017 sharesBasic are null: HLNE was not public before 6 March 2017, and the FY2017 EPS figure of $0.03 covers only the 26-day stub period 6-31 March 2017, so no annual weighted average exists. Note that the FY2026 balance-sheet Class A count (43,697,484 outstanding at 31 March 2026) is well above the FY2026 weighted average of 41,605,636.

FY2016 netIncome is reported as 0 in the extract (NetIncomeLoss attributable to HLI was nil pre-IPO, while the LLC's ProfitLoss was positive), so FY2016 payoutNi is null and FY2016 revenue is null (the revenue tag only starts FY2017). These pre-IPO years carry no dividend information and should be excluded from any trend analysis.

g10 is null: the DPS series only reaches back to FY2017 and that year's DPS is zero, so a 10-year CAGR endpoint does not exist. gMax (15.12%/yr) runs FY2018 ($0.70) to FY2026 ($2.16), 8 years. This is materially below the priorEstimates guess of 17% for 5-year growth - the actual 5-year figure is 11.56%/yr (FY2021 $1.25 to FY2026 $2.16), and growth has been decelerating (3-yr 10.52%).

JUDGEMENT CALL - streak. I counted 9 consecutive increases (FY2018 through FY2026), which treats FY2018's initiation ($0.70 from zero in FY2017) as an increase. Counting only raises between two paying years gives 8 (FY2019-FY2026). There is no cut or hold anywhere in the record, including through COVID (FY2020 $1.10 and FY2021 $1.25 were both raises), and windowLimited is false because FY2017 (zero, pre-dividend) is inside the data window.

priorEstimates payoutPctFcf of 40% is too high: actual FY2026 payout on FCF is 20.9%, and the trailing five-year average is about 33%. Note that FCF here is CFO - capex on the consolidated statements, which include the cash flows of consolidated funds and partnerships; the FY2024 dip (FCF $110m, payoutFcf 59.6%) is driven by consolidated-fund working-capital swings in CFO rather than by the fee business.

normalised.notes: Hamilton Lane (FYE 31 March; "FY2026" = year ended 2026-03-31). Dividends are paid on Class A common stock only. The record is built on filed annual DPS read from each 10-K's Consolidated Statements of Income (us-gaap:CommonStockDividendsPerShareDeclared, Class A dimension), because that tag is dimensioned and so never reaches the companyfacts feed the extract was built from - the extract's empty dpsAllFacts is an artifact of the feed, not evidence that HLNE does not report DPS. Ten years of DPS: 0 (FY2017, IPO year), then 0.70, 0.85, 1.10, 1.25, 1.40, 1.60, 1.78, 1.96, 2.16 - nine straight raises, no cut, no hold, no special, no stock split, so no split adjustment was applied to any year. Growth is real but decelerating: 15.1%/yr since initiation, 11.6% over 5 years, 10.5% over 3 years. Coverage is strong and improving - FY2026 FCF of $419m against $88m of dividends paid (20.9% payout), 35.2% of net income attributable to HLI, and the balance sheet moved to a $93m net cash position in FY2026. The one number I would not trust is FY2023 dividends paid ($72,409k), which exceeds the declared-plus-payable roll-forward by exactly the year-end payable; it is what the filing says and was never restated, but it inflates FY2023 payout ratios by about a quarter. EBITDA and ROIC use revenue minus total expenses as operating income (HLNE reports no operating-income subtotal) and are therefore conservative.

issues.detail: Implied shares from live data (4,991,379,562 / 89.88 = 55.53m) exceed the record's latest weighted-average Class A count (41.61m) by 33.5% and the stated 31-Mar-2026 Class A outstanding (43.70m) by 27.1% - past the 15% block threshold. The record notes Class B/C exist but never states the total share count, so a reader comparing marketCap/price to sharesBasic is left with an unexplained 33% gap. The record treats the 2.22 reconciliation as confirmation that no special exists; that conclusion is right either way, but the declaration-count assumption is not independently verified and the forward run-rate is the more useful number.

issues.detail: The entire DPS series is NOT derivable from the supplied extract: dpsAllFacts=[] and there is no shares family, so rules (a), (b) and (c) are all unsatisfiable from the file. Every DPS value, every quarterly rate and every sharesBasic figure comes from outside the file (10-K documents). I could not verify any of them against the source of record. What I CAN verify is strongly corroborative: the raw file's own declared-dollar tags divided by the record's sharesBasic reproduce the claimed DPS to within 0.14%-4.0% in all nine years (FY2023 1.6045 vs 1.60; FY2026 2.1631 vs 2.16), which would be an improbable coincidence if the series were wrong. Still, confidence 'high' overstates reproducibility.
issues.suggested: Keep the DPS series but set dataQuality.confidence to 'medium' and state explicitly that dps, sharesBasic and the quarterly rates are externally sourced and not reproducible from this extract.

issues.detail: FY2023 divPaid/sharesBasic = 1.9538 vs filed DPS 1.60, +22.1% - the largest deviation in the series and far outside the ~5% tolerance. The record discloses it and keeps the filed PaymentsOfDividends of 72,409k, but then propagates it into FY2023 payout ratios, which are overstated by ~22%. The raw file supplies a cleaner FY2023 declared figure (DividendsCommonStock = 59,462k), which reconciles to 1.6045/share.
issues.suggested: Either set fin[FY2023].payoutFcf=0.2680 and payoutNi=0.5449 (using declared 59,462k), or leave the filed figures but null the two FY2023 payout ratios with the reason. Do not present 0.3264 / 0.6636 as comparable to other years.

issues.detail: EBITDA is not recomputable from the extract at all: there is no opIncome family, no OperatingExpenses tag and no us-gaap:OperatingIncomeLoss in the file's families or tagHints. The record's opIncome (revenue minus an externally read 'Total expenses') cannot be checked against anything here, so check 3's 2% tolerance is untestable for EBITDA and for the opIncome leg of ROIC. The implied FY2026 total expenses of 434,050k is plausible but unverified. The stated derivation rule is to return null when a value is not derivable.
issues.suggested: Either null ebitda/netDebtToEbitda/roic, or keep them and add an explicit 'externally sourced input, not present in extract: OperatingExpenses' note per year, with the implied opIncome values listed (FY2024 245,818k, FY2025 316,552k, FY2026 324,943k) so a reviewer can check them against the filings.

issues.detail: ROIC mixes bases: the numerator opIncome includes income attributable to non-controlling interests (the Up-C HLA members and consolidated funds), while the denominator uses StockholdersEquity (HLI-only, excluding NCI - the extract also carries StockholdersEquityIncludingPortionAttributableToNoncontrollingInterest). This structurally inflates ROIC in every year, on top of the small-equity-base distortion the record already flags for FY2017-FY2019.
issues.suggested: Recompute with StockholdersEquityIncludingPortionAttributableToNoncontrollingInterest in the denominator, or state in issues that ROIC is on an HLI-only capital base against consolidated operating income and is therefore not comparable across the Up-C structure.

issues.detail: The raw extract's LongTermDebt family starts at 2020-03-31 (7 points). The FY2017-FY2019 debt figures used (84,310k / 84,162k / 70,954k) are not in the file; they were read from 10-Q balance sheets. netDebt and ROIC for those three years are therefore built on unverifiable inputs. The arithmetic is at least internally consistent (84,310-34,135=50,175; 84,162-49,383=34,779; 70,954-51,590=19,364).
issues.suggested: Flag FY2017-FY2019 netDebt/netDebtToEbitda/roic as externally sourced, or null them per the 'not derivable -> null' rule.

issues.detail: Internally inconsistent with the record's own endpoints: fromFy 2018 to toFy 2026 is 8 fiscal years (and the record's own notes say gMax 'runs FY2018 to FY2026, 8 years'), but yearsCovered is stated as 9. gMax=15.125% checks out as an 8-year CAGR, so the 9 is the error.
issues.suggested: growth.yearsCovered = 8 (or define it as the FY2017-FY2026 data span and say so, but then it disagrees with fromFy).

rules.name: Small enough to grow
rules.note: live marketCap 4,991,379,562 at $89.88 (2026-09-17) - just inside the ideal <$5B band. Note the Up-C structure: implied total shares 55.5m vs 43.7m Class A outstanding, so market cap already includes ~11.8m Class B shares that carry no dividend.

rules.name: Starting yield in the usable band
rules.note: Forward indicated rate 4 x $0.60 = $2.40 declared 21 May 2026, / $89.88 = 2.67%. On the last filed fiscal-year DPS of $2.16 it is 2.40%. live.ttmDividend of 2.22 (3 x 0.54 + 0.60) is a rate-change artifact, not a special.

rules.name: Dividend growth above 8%/yr
rules.note: 5-yr CAGR FY2021 $1.25 -> FY2026 $2.16. No splits, so no adjustment. Passes but just short of strong, and decelerating: 3-yr 10.52%, since-initiation (8 yrs) 15.13%. The FY2027 step to $0.60/qtr is +11.1%, in line.

rules.name: Payout with room left
rules.note: Asset manager, so FCF = CFO - capex is appropriate: FY2026 $424.9m - $5.8m = $419.1m vs $87.7m dividends paid. Sits at the very bottom of the band - lots of runway, but the consolidated cash flow statement swings with fund consolidation (FY2024 FCF fell to $110m and payout spiked to 59.6%). 5-yr average payout ~33%. On net income the FY2026 payout is 35.2%.

rules.name: Streak long enough to prove policy
rules.note: FY2018 initiation plus eight consecutive raises through FY2026. NOT window-limited - HLNE IPO'd 6 March 2017 and the zero-dividend FY2017 is inside the data window, so 9 is the true company history, not a data artifact. priorEstimates.streak is also 9, so no upgrade is available. Fails on length only; there is no cut, hold, or missed year.

rules.name: Earnings growing at least as fast as the dividend
rules.note: FCF FY2021 $169.5m -> FY2026 $419.1m. Both endpoints positive, so no need to fall back to net income; net income corroborates (FY2021 $98.0m -> FY2026 $249.2m = 20.5%/yr). Dividend growth has trailed cash generation by ~8pp/yr, which is why payout fell from 23.4% to 20.9%.

rules.name: High return on invested capital
rules.note: FY2026 opIncome x (1 - 16.3% tax) / (equity + debt - cash). Strong on any reading, but the basis is mixed: numerator is consolidated operating income including non-controlling interests while the denominator uses HLI-only equity, so the true figure is lower. Even haircut for the Up-C NCI it clears 12% comfortably; FY2022-FY2026 range 30-44%.

rules.name: Balance sheet not competing with you
rules.note: Net cash passes outright. Moved from $97.0m net debt in FY2023 to $93.5m net cash in FY2026. Cash includes restricted and consolidated-fund cash, so the net-cash position is somewhat flattered, but leverage was never above 0.65x in any year of the record.

rules.name: Why competitors cannot take the business
rules.note: Fee streams are contracted over 10+ year locked-up fund lives, and the Cobalt data set - 60,000+ funds of cash-flow-level private-markets data accumulated through 35 years of diligence - is the input both to its own allocation decisions and to what LPs buy. A new entrant cannot buy either the history or the GP access.

rules.name: Management treats the dividend as a promise
rules.threshold: no cut in FY2020/FY2021; none in window
rules.note: FY2020 $1.10 (+29%) and FY2021 $1.25 (+14%) were both raises straight through COVID. No cut, suspension or hold anywhere in the record. 2008 is outside the window - and irrelevant here, since HLNE only listed in March 2017.

analysis.assessment: Hamilton Lane is a $5.0B private-markets asset manager yielding 2.67% on the newly declared $0.60 quarterly rate ($2.40 annualised at $89.88), with a 5-year dividend CAGR of 11.56% that is comfortably funded: FY2026 dividends of $87.7m against $419.1m of free cash flow is a 20.9% payout, 35.2% of net income, and the balance sheet flipped to $93.5m net cash. Free cash flow compounded at 19.8%/yr over the same five years, roughly 8pp faster than the dividend, so the payout ratio has been falling even as the dividend doubled - that is the shape of a snowball with years of runway rather than one running on fumes. The one hard fail is rule 5: the streak is 9 years, not 10, because HLNE only listed in March 2017; this is genuine company history, not a data-window artifact, and it clears on the next declaration. The likeliest thing to break it is fee-related earnings, not the balance sheet - about a quarter of revenue is incentive fees and carried interest that a weak private-markets exit environment can halve, and the consolidated cash flow statement already swings hard with fund consolidation (FY2024 FCF fell to $110m and payout spiked to 59.6% in a single year). Dividend growth is also decelerating - 15.1%/yr since initiation, 11.6% over 5 years, 10.5% over 3 - so the base case is high-single to low-double-digit raises, not the 17% the prior estimate assumed.

screenFields.streakSource: data (FY2018 initiation + 8 raises through FY2026); not window-limited - HLNE IPO'd March 2017, and priorEstimates.streak was also 9

The 17% guess matched the early post-IPO years (15.1%/yr since the FY2018 initiation, ~22%/yr FY2018-FY2021) but growth has decelerated to 10.5% over 3 years. 5.4pp overstatement.

FY2026 dividends paid $87.7m / FCF $419.1m = 20.9%. The 40% figure is closer to the noisy FY2024 print (59.6%, distorted by consolidated-fund working capital) than to the trend; the 5-yr average is ~33% and falling as FCF outgrows the dividend. 19pp overstatement.

No change - confirmed from filed data: FY2018 initiation followed by eight consecutive raises. Confirming it matters because it is the one failing rule and it is now known to be real history rather than an XBRL-window truncation.

analysis.moat: Private-markets allocation and data: fee streams are contracted over 10+ year locked-up fund lives, and the Cobalt data set built from 35 years of GP diligence is an input rivals cannot replicate by spending.
strengths: Net cash of $93.5m with leverage never above 0.65x in the record
Payout of 20.9% of FCF and 35.2% of net income - among the lowest in the dividend-growth universe at this yield
FCF compounding at 19.8%/yr, ~8pp faster than the dividend
33% ROIC on a capital-light fee business with no meaningful capex ($5.8m on $759m revenue)
Raised straight through COVID (+29% FY2020, +14% FY2021) - policy already tested
risks: Streak is only 9 years - no track record through a full private-markets downcycle as a public dividend payer
Roughly a quarter of revenue is incentive fees and carried interest, which a prolonged exit drought can halve; the fee-related base is the only part that is genuinely contracted
Consolidated cash flows include the funds themselves, so reported FCF and payout swing hard year to year (FY2024 payout 59.6% vs FY2026 20.9%)
Up-C structure: $54.1m of FY2026 member distributions to Class B/C holders sit ahead of, and separate from, the common dividend, and ~11.8m Class B shares are in the market cap but not the dividend
Dividend growth decelerating (15.1% -> 11.6% -> 10.5%), so the 12%+ 'strong' threshold is unlikely to be regained
FY2023 reported dividends paid ($72.4m) does not reconcile to the declaration roll-forward, inflating that year's payout ratios ~22%
analysis.sectorNote: Asset manager: rule 4 uses FCF = CFO - capex as instructed, which is the right definition for a capital-light fee business, but HLNE's cash flow statement consolidates the funds and partnerships it manages, so CFO carries working-capital swings that have nothing to do with the fee business - the FY2024 payout of 59.6% and the FY2026 payout of 20.9% bracket a true underlying payout nearer 30-35%. Rule 8 is meaningful here (HLNE is an operating manager, not a balance-sheet insurer) and passes on net cash. Rule 7's ROIC is distorted by the Up-C structure: consolidated operating income over an HLI-only equity base overstates the level, though not enough to threaten the 12% threshold.

stocks.m: Category-leading listed real-assets specialist - a multi-decade REIT, infrastructure and preferred-securities track record that consultants screen on and that sticky closed-end-fund and institutional mandates are priced off, not a business won on fee level.

normalised.dpsMethod: REGULAR annual DPS = sum of the four quarterly CommonStockDividendsPerShareDeclared rate facts inside each calendar fiscal year (FYE 12-31). The filed ANNUAL (FY, ~364-day) CommonStockDividendsPerShareDeclared fact is NOT the regular dividend for CNS: it bundles the year-end special. Quarterly declared rates exist 2013-2026 and are perfectly level within each year (4 x Q rate = 0.80/0.88/1.00/1.04/1.12/1.32/1.44/1.56/1.80/2.20/2.28/2.36/2.48 for FY2013-FY2025), so special = filed annual minus 4 x quarterly rate. FY2012 has no declared-quarterly facts, but CommonStockDividendsPerShareCashPaid shows Q3-2012 = 0.18 and 9M-2012 = 0.54 (= 3 x 0.18), fixing the FY2012 regular rate at 0.18/qtr -> 0.72 regular, 1.50 special. FY2009 has no DPS tag at all; divPaid / weighted basic shares = 0.2001 (= 4 x 0.05) with no evidence of a special, so FY2009 regular = 0.20 (basis derived-from-cash). FY2010 (divPaid/share 2.3973) and FY2011 (filed 1.60, divPaid/share 1.6003) clearly contain large specials that cannot be separated from the regular rate with any fact in this file, so no regular DPS is reported for those two years. Cross-check divPaid/sharesBasic vs filed annual DPS matches within 0.2% for EVERY year 2009-2025, confirming declared = paid in the same fiscal year and confirming the share basis. No split adjustment applied (splitFacts empty; weighted basic shares rise smoothly 42.3M -> 51.2M).

dps.basis: summed-quarters (4 x 0.18 CommonStockDividendsPerShareCashPaid rate; no declared-quarterly facts)

specials.note: CNS paid a year-end special dividend every year from at least 2010 through 2021, then stopped. Specials separated per year (filed annual DPS minus 4 x quarterly declared rate): FY2012 1.50, FY2013 1.00, FY2014 1.00, FY2015 0.50, FY2016 0.50, FY2017 1.00, FY2018 2.50, FY2019 2.00, FY2020 1.00, FY2021 1.25. FY2010 (total 2.3973/sh) and FY2011 (total 1.60/sh) also contain specials but the regular/special split is not derivable from the facts in this file. FY2022-FY2025: none - filed annual DPS equals 4 x the quarterly rate exactly. This is why the FILED annual DPS series falls in 2013, 2015, 2019, 2020 and 2022 while the REGULAR dividend rose in every one of those years; treating the filed series as the dividend would produce five phantom cuts. live.ttmDividend 2.63 is roughly (not exactly) consistent with 2 x 0.62 + 2 x 0.67 = 2.58, i.e. purely regular; regularDividendIfSpecial is null because no special has been paid since 2021.

issues: SPECIALS, not splits, are the whole story here. splitFacts is empty and weighted basic shares rise smoothly from 42.339M (2009) to 51.168M (2025) with no step, so NO split adjustment was made to any year and splitAdjustments is empty. The one share-count step in the file is CommonStockSharesOutstanding jumping 46.31M (2017) -> 52.58M (2019) -> 55.05M (2022) -> 49.16M (2023); that is a tagging/definition change (issued incl. unvested restricted shares vs outstanding), not a split - weighted basic shares over the same span go 46.79M -> 47.27M -> 48.78M -> 49.31M with no discontinuity, and the 2026-07-23 cover count of 51.42M agrees with FY2025 basic. Nothing was divided or multiplied.

The filed annual DPS tag (CommonStockDividendsPerShareDeclared, FY duration) includes the year-end special in every year 2010-2021. Using it as-is would show cuts in FY2013 (2.22->1.80), FY2015 (1.88->1.50), FY2019 (3.82->3.44), FY2020 (3.44->2.56) and FY2022 (3.05->2.20). All five are specials rolling off; the regular quarterly rate rose in each of those years. dps[].val is the REGULAR series only.

Cross-check divPaid/sharesBasic vs filed annual DPS agrees within 0.2% in EVERY year 2009-2025 (2013: 1.8001 vs 1.80; 2018: 3.8227 vs 3.82; 2021: 3.0540 vs 3.05; 2025: 2.4805 vs 2.48). No year disagreed. This also confirms declared and paid fall in the same fiscal year, so the special-vs-regular split is not a timing artifact.
FY2010 regular DPS NOT derivable: no DPS tag before 2011 and no quarterly facts; total paid 2.3973/sh obviously contains a large special. Omitted from dps rather than guessed.

FY2011 regular DPS NOT derivable: filed annual 1.60 (confirmed by divPaid/shares 1.6003) but no quarterly rate facts for 2011 or earlier, so the regular/special split is unknowable from this file. Omitted from dps. This is the only reason the streak window starts at FY2012.

FY2012 regular rate (0.18/qtr -> 0.72) is inferred from CommonStockDividendsPerShareCashPaid, not from declared-quarterly facts: Q3-2012 = 0.18 and 9M-2012 = 0.54. Judgement call; it is consistent with the 0.20/qtr declared rate that first appears in Q1-2013. If wrong, gMax and the streak endpoint move.

FY2009 regular DPS 0.20 is derived from cash (8.472M / 42.339M basic = 0.2001 = 4 x 0.05) with no filed DPS fact to confirm it and no way to rule out a special. It is an isolated point (2010 and 2011 blank), so it was deliberately NOT used as a CAGR endpoint - a 2009->2025 CAGR of ~17%/yr off a post-crisis trough would be misleading. gMax uses the contiguous regular series 2012->2025 (13 years, 9.98%/yr).

Streak: 13 consecutive increases in the regular dividend, FY2013 through FY2025, running back to the first year of the reliable regular series, so windowLimited = true and the true streak is very likely longer (priorEstimates guessed 19; these filings can neither confirm nor refute the pre-2012 years). No cut or hold in the regular rate anywhere in the window, including FY2020/FY2021 (1.44 -> 1.56 -> 1.80), so cut2020 = false and cutsOrHolds is empty. The FY2021 special of 1.25 was the last special paid.

REVENUE is null for FY2021-FY2025. The Revenues tag in the join stops at 2020 and the per-year table carries no revenue for 2021+, even though the families block lists RevenueFromContractWithCustomerIncludingAssessedTax covering 2016-2025; that series is not in the table, so it could not be used without inventing numbers. Consequence: latest.fcfMargin is null.

FY2025 CFO is NEGATIVE (-120.444M) against net income of +153.2M, so FY2025 FCF = -126.423M. This is almost certainly consolidated-fund / seed-investment purchases running through operating activities (see PaymentsToAcquireMarketableSecurities 383.4M and ProceedsFromPaymentsToMinorityShareholders 228.7M in tagHints), not an operating collapse. Consequences: latest.payoutFcf is null and fcfGrowth5 is null because the 2025 endpoint is <= 0. FCF-based payout is unusable for CNS without unconsolidating the funds; payoutNi 0.828 is the meaningful latest payout. priorEstimates' 60% FCF payout is not reproducible in any year here.

NO DEBT TAG EXISTS in the file (no debtLT / debtCur family, nothing debt-like in tagHints). Debt was therefore treated as zero, so netDebt = -cash in every year and netDebtToEbitda is negative throughout (-0.41 to -2.38). Directionally right for an unlevered asset manager, but it is an assumption, not a filed fact.

Effective tax rate is tax/pretax only for FY2009-FY2020. The table has no pretax for FY2021-FY2025 (the pretax family switches tags in 2019 and the join kept the older one), so the 21% fallback was used for ROIC in those five years. Sanity check: NI+tax implies ~20.9% for 2021 and ~23.6% for 2024, so the fallback is close but FY2023-FY2025 ROIC is slightly overstated.

FY2009 effective tax computes to 108% (tax 4.490M on pretax 4.154M, net loss -1.710M). FY2009 EBITDA and ROIC are null anyway (no D&A tagged for 2009, no equity for 2009) and payoutNi is null because net income is negative.

ROIC is mechanically unstable for this filer because the denominator (equity + debt - cash) is small and cash-dominated: it exceeds 100% in 2016, 2017 and 2019, and hits 290% in FY2021 (equity 255.2M less cash 184.4M leaves invested capital of only 70.8M) and 189% in FY2022. Artifacts of the prescribed formula on a cash-rich, asset-light balance sheet, not real returns. FY2023-FY2025 (0.67 / 0.42 / 0.34) look lower mainly because equity ballooned to 562M.

Payout ratios above 1.0 in many years (payoutNi > 1 in 2010-2015 and 2017-2020; payoutFcf 5.72 in 2012) are real: specials were paid out of accumulated cash and exceeded both earnings and FCF in those years. On the regular dividend alone the payout was far lower.

FY2023 capex of 56.986M is 5-14x every other year (2.4M-11.7M) - consistent with a one-off office/leasehold build-out. It is the filer's own PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment tag and was left unadjusted, but it depresses FY2023 FCF and inflates that year's payoutFcf.

live.ttmDividend 2.63 does not tie exactly to the filed quarterly rates as of 2026-09-17 (Q3-25 0.62 + Q4-25 0.62 + Q1-26 0.67 + Q2-26 0.67 = 2.58). Minor vendor-vs-filing discrepancy; filings are authoritative. FY2026 is being declared at 0.67/qtr (Q1 and Q2 2026 facts present) = 2.68 annualised, a 14th consecutive increase in progress but outside the completed-FY window.

priorEstimates were not used. The 5-year regular-DPS CAGR does happen to land near their 9%; the 19-year streak is only verifiable to 13 years here and the 60% FCF payout is not reproducible from these filings.

normalised.notes: Cohen & Steers, FYE 12-31, no splits. The only real normalisation problem is that the filed annual DPS tag bundles a year-end special in every year from 2010 through 2021 (largest 2.50 in FY2018 and 2.00 in FY2019). Stripping specials using the level quarterly declared rates turns a jagged filed series with five apparent cuts into a clean 13-year run of increases: 0.72 (FY2012) -> 2.48 (FY2025), ~9.98%/yr, 9.71%/yr over 5 years, decelerating to 4.07%/yr over the last 3. Specials stopped after FY2021 and the regular dividend has kept rising (0.67/qtr declared in 2026). The balance sheet is net cash in every year with no tagged debt. FY2025 operating cash flow is negative because consolidated-fund investment activity runs through CFO, which makes FCF-based payout meaningless for the latest year - use the 82.8% net-income payout instead.

checksRun: 1. divPaid/sharesBasic recomputed for all 17 years (2009-2025) and compared to both the record's regular dps and the filed annual DPS. Filed annual matches derived-from-cash within 0.19% EVERY year (worst 2024: 119181/50409=2.36429 vs 2.36; 2018 3.82268 vs 3.82; 2021 3.05398 vs 3.05; 2025 2.48053 vs 2.48). Years where the record's REGULAR dps deviates >5% from divPaid/shares (2012-2021) are all fully and exactly explained by the stated per-year special, which reconciles to the cent.
