It is not a price-competed business, though it is fully exposed to the passive-fee squeeze at the retail end.

The filed annual DPS series appears to fall in 2013/2015/2019/2020/2022, but those are year-end specials rolling off, not cuts - specials stopped after FY2021 and the regular rate kept rising.

analysis.assessment: CNS is a $3.7B net-cash asset manager yielding 3.45% on its FY2025 regular dividend of $2.48 (3.73% on the $2.68 rate already declared for 2026), with a clean 13-year run of regular increases in the data and probably ~19 in reality once the special-dividend noise before 2012 is set aside. Growth has been 9.7%/yr over five years but only 4.1%/yr over three, and the 2026 raise of 8.1% suggests the high-single-digit era is over, not the mid-teens one. The payout is the problem: $126.9M of dividends against $153.2M of net income is 82.8%, and FCF-based payout is unusable because FY2025 operating cash flow is -$120.4M on consolidated fund/seed purchases - either way there is very little runway to grow the dividend faster than fee earnings. The snowball here is a 3.5% yield compounding at roughly earnings growth, call it 5-8%, with no leverage and no reinvestment need, but it is levered one-for-one to AUM: a 25% drawdown in listed REIT and preferred markets takes fee revenue and the raise with it, and with 83% of earnings already committed there is no cushion to hold the line through it. The one thing most likely to break it is a multi-year outflow cycle out of listed real assets into private or passive vehicles.
analysis.moat: Category-leading listed real-assets specialist - a multi-decade REIT, infrastructure and preferred-securities track record that consultants screen on and that sticky closed-end-fund and institutional mandates are priced off, not a business won on fee level.

Regular dividend raised every single year FY2013-FY2025 including through COVID (1.44 -> 1.56 -> 1.80), and raised again to 0.67/qtr for 2026
Asset-light: capital intensity is effectively zero (capex 2-12M/yr ex the one-off FY2023 build-out) so almost all earnings are distributable
Yield 3.45% sits high in the usable band without being a distress yield; market cap $3.7B leaves room to compound
risks: Payout 82.8% of net income leaves no cushion; a fee-revenue drawdown forces the dividend to stall
AUM-sensitive single-category franchise - listed REITs, infrastructure and preferreds - so revenue, earnings and the dividend all move with one asset class
Dividend growth decelerating sharply: 9.7% over 5 years but 4.1% over 3 and 8.1% for the 2026 raise
Net income flat at 151-171M since FY2022 while the dividend keeps rising, which is what pushed the payout from 63% to 83% in three years
Structural fee pressure from passive and from the shift of real-asset allocations into private vehicles
analysis.sectorNote: CNS is an asset manager, so rule 4 was run on FCF = CFO - capex as prescribed, but FY2025 CFO is negative (-120.4M) purely because consolidated-fund and seed-investment purchases flow through operating activities - not an operating failure. The FCF payout is therefore meaningless and the payout test was read on net income (82.8%), which is the honest number for a fee-based business. Rule 7's ROIC is also a poor fit: the denominator (equity + debt - cash) is small and cash-dominated for an asset-light filer, producing readings above 100% in several years; the 33.7% FY2025 figure clears the bar on any reasonable variant but should not be read as a precise return. Rule 8's net-cash reading rests on the absence of any debt tag in the filings.

normalised.dpsMethod: Mixed by year, in the stated priority order, with the whole FY2021-FY2026 tail forced onto ONE basis (see REPAIR in notes). FY2015 = sum of the four filed quarterly CommonStockDividendsPerShareDeclared facts (all 0.00; dividend not yet initiated). FY2016 = filed annual CommonStockDividendsPerShareCashPaid 0.30 (2015-04-01/2016-03-31, 365 days), corroborated exactly by the quarterly sum 0+0+0.15+0.15 = 0.30. FY2017 = sum of the four quarterly facts 0.20x4 = 0.80; the filed annual CommonStockDividendsPerShareCashPaid fact for 2016-04-01/2017-03-31 also reads 0.30 and was REJECTED as a stale carry-forward of the FY2016 value (DividendsCommonStock FY2017 47.883m / 61.1005m weighted basic = 0.7837/sh independently confirms ~0.80, and the tag has only two points in the whole filing history). FY2018 = derived divPaid/weighted basic = 52.081m/62.4943m = 0.83337; the quarterly facts tagged Apr2017-Mar2018 (0.27/0.27/0.27/0.31) are byte-identical to the Apr2018-Mar2019 quarters and sit ~34% above both cash paid (0.8334/sh) and cash declared (51.305m/62.4943m = 0.8210/sh), so they were rejected as a duplicated block; the true rate was almost certainly 0.21/quarter (4x0.21 = 0.84, within 2.3% of cash declared). FY2019 and FY2020 = quarterly sums (0.27+0.27+0.27+0.31 = 1.12 and 0.31x4 = 1.24), both within 5% of divPaid/shares (1.0758 and 1.2977). FY2021 through FY2026 = derived divPaid/weighted basic shares, i.e. rule (c), applied CONSISTENTLY across all six years. No per-share DPS fact of any kind exists for FY2021-FY2025 (the quarterly series stops at the Jan-Mar 2020 quarter and resumes only at Oct-Dec 2025), so rule (c) is forced for those five years; FY2026 is put on the SAME basis deliberately so the array is internally comparable and no false cut appears at the most-consumed point. The rate-based FY2026 figure is 2.40 (4 x the only in-year quarterly fact, Oct-Dec 2025 = 0.60) and is reported in notes and issues, not in the array. No splits: splitFacts is empty, HLI has never split since its Aug-2015 IPO, weighted basic shares rise smoothly 55.050m -> 66.548m with no step change of any ratio, and divPaid/sharesBasic is internally consistent with the filed DPS in every year where both exist, so every year is already on today's share basis and nothing was rescaled.

specials.note: No per-share special dividend is identifiable and none is carried in the series. The one large anomaly is FY2016 (ended 2016-03-31, the IPO year, IPO Aug 2015): PaymentsOfDividends 114.297m and DividendsCommonStock (declared) 283.133m against a regular DPS of only 0.30 on 59.045m weighted basic shares (~17.7m of regular dividends). divPaid/shares = 1.9358 and declared/shares = 4.7952 versus a filed DPS of 0.30, i.e. cash is 6.5x to 16x the per-share rate. That is the OPPOSITE direction from the rule-of-thumb special test (filed DPS far ABOVE divPaid/shares); it is pre-IPO/recapitalisation distributions to pre-IPO holders, not a dividend on today's public share base, so it is NOT carried into the DPS series as a special. FY2014 (PaymentsOfDividends 1.075m) and FY2015 (2.166m) are similarly pre-IPO distributions with no public per-share equivalent, and the filed quarterly facts for all four FY2015 quarters are explicitly 0.00. FY2017 cash paid (55.293m) exceeds cash declared (47.883m) because the FY2016 dividend payable was settled in FY2017. live.regularDividendIfSpecial is null, confirming the latest TTM dividend of 2.60 contains no special.

issues: BLOCK RESOLVED - FY2026 DPS BASIS. The reviewer was RIGHT that the emitted array previously mixed two incompatible bases at its most-consumed point: FY2021-FY2025 were divPaid/weighted-basic while FY2026 was a rate-based 4x0.60 = 2.40, so a mechanical diff of the last two values read as a -4.5% cut while streak said 11 with an empty cutsOrHolds. FIX APPLIED: dps[2026] is now 174037000/66547768 = 2.61522 on the SAME derived-from-cash basis as FY2021-FY2025. The array is now strictly increasing in every year FY2016-FY2026 (+166.7%, +4.2%, +34.4%, +10.7%, +12.8%, +26.4%, +25.4%, +4.1%, +8.9%, +4.0%), so consecutiveIncreasesInData = 11 is recomputable from the array itself and cutsOrHolds is legitimately empty. The rate-based 2.40 is preserved in notes and below, not in the array.

WHY THE DERIVED FY2026 VALUE WAS CHOSEN OVER THE RATE-BASED 2.40 (the two reviewers disagreed here). The adversarial reviewer wanted dps[2026] restated to the derived value; the external-coherence reviewer wanted 2.40 kept and the earlier years restated instead. Restating FY2021-FY2025 onto a rate basis is NOT possible from the raw file without inventing numbers: dpsAllFacts contains no per-share fact of any kind between the Jan-Mar 2020 quarter and the Oct-Dec 2025 quarter, so rule (c) is forced for those five years and the only way to make the tail consistent is to extend rule (c) through FY2026. The derived FY2026 value also happens to sit closer to the externally observable dividend stream than 2.40 does: 2.61522 implies a 2.01% yield at price 130.34 versus live.ttmDividend 2.60 = 1.99%, while 2.40 implies 1.84%.

TRUE FY2026 DECLARED RATE IS 2.40, NOT 2.61522 - USE IT FOR LEVEL, NOT FOR THE SERIES. The only quarterly fact inside FY2026 is Oct-Dec 2025 = 0.60; 4x0.60 = 2.40. live.ttmDividend 2.60 = 0.60+0.60+0.70+0.70 across the Dec-25/Mar-26/Jun-26/Sep-26 payments, and the 0.70 rate first appears in the Apr-Jun 2026 fact (FY2027 Q1), so all four FY2026 quarters were at 0.60 unless the step to 0.60 happened mid-year, in which case FY2026 was ~2.34. Either way the derived 2.61522 OVERSTATES the declared FY2026 rate by 9.0-11.8%.

THE +9% DERIVED-VS-RATE GAP IS A REAL, MEASURABLE SHARE-BASE WEDGE, NOT NOISE. Implied dividend-paying share count for FY2026 = 174037000/2.40 = 72.5154m (declared basis 175335000/2.40 = 73.056m) versus 66.548m weighted basic, 68.435m weighted diluted and 69.89m implied outstanding (marketCap 9109005628 / price 130.34). HLI pays dividend equivalents on unvested restricted shares that sit outside weighted basic. Applying the same 72.5154m base to FY2025 gives an implied FY2025 rate of 2.2784 (a 0.57 quarterly rate), i.e. 0.57 -> 0.60 = a 5.3% raise, exactly matching the 5.34% rise in cash paid (165.217m -> 174.037m). This is the arithmetic a consumer needs to normalise the derived years back to rates; it is stated here as numbers rather than left in prose.

THE BIAS IN THE DERIVED YEARS IS NOT CONSTANT. Measured against years where the rate is independently known, divPaid/sharesBasic runs +13.1% (FY2017: 0.90495 vs 0.80), 0.0% (FY2018, which is itself derived), -3.9% (FY2019: 1.07578 vs 1.12), +4.7% (FY2020: 1.29769 vs 1.24) and +9.0% (FY2026: 2.61522 vs 2.40). The early negative readings come from the one-quarter lag between declaration and payment; the recent positive readings come from the restricted-share dividend-equivalent base. Treat FY2021-FY2026 DPS LEVELS as +/-10% estimates. rules.note: FY2026 operating income x (1 - 24.560% effective tax) / (equity + debt - cash) = 34.5%. Representative range FY2019-FY2020 and FY2024-FY2026 is 24.0%-34.5%; FY2021-FY2022 readings of 52.6%/72.9% are inflated because the 0.8bn cash pile shrinks the denominator. Strong on any of these.

rules.name: Balance sheet not competing with you
rules.note: Net cash in all 14 years. No debt tag exists for FY2022-FY2026 so netDebt is 0 - cash, i.e. an upper bound on the net cash position, but the sign is unambiguous: 1.189bn of cash against 2.342bn of equity. Passes outright. This is an advisory firm, not a bank, so the ratio is meaningful.

rules.name: Why competitors cannot take the business
rules.note: The mechanism is the counter-cyclical pairing: HLI is the #1 restructuring advisor globally and the most active US mid-market M&A advisor, so distress volume backfills when deal volume collapses. That plus fairness-opinion and valuation mandates (a litigation-credentialed franchise boards cannot easily swap) and a partner base that owns equity. It is not price competition.

rules.name: Management treats the dividend as a promise
rules.threshold: no cut in FY2020/FY2021; any cut in window fails
rules.note: FY2020 DPS rose 1.12 -> 1.24 and FY2021 rose again to ~1.40; cash dividends paid rose through COVID (66.9m -> 80.7m -> 92.0m). No cut or hold anywhere in the data. 2008 is outside the XBRL window and also pre-IPO (HLI listed Aug 2015), so there is no crisis-era record to test.

analysis.assessment: HLI is a $9.1bn capital-light advisory franchise paying a 1.99% TTM yield (2.60 on a 130.34 price) that it has raised every year since initiating in late 2015 - an 11-year streak with no COVID cut, and the quarterly rate has already stepped 0.60 -> 0.70 for FY2027, a 16.7% raise implying a 2.15% forward yield. The snowball is low-yield/high-growth: 13.3%/yr five-year dividend growth on a 25.5% FCF payout (174m of dividends against 682m of FCF) and 41% of net income, so the runway is long even before earnings grow. Quality behind it is real - 34.5% ROIC, 1.19bn of net cash and no debt, 22m of capex on 2.6bn of revenue - and the only rule it fails is rule 6: five-year FCF growth of 3.8%/yr (net income 6.3%/yr) is far below the 13.3% dividend growth, so the raises have been funded by rising payout, up from 16.3% of FCF in FY2021. The thing most likely to break it is a multi-year M&A drought: FY2023 already showed what that looks like, with CFO collapsing to 136m and dividends paid exceeding FCF 1.64x, and if fee income stalls while payout climbs past 40% of FCF the growth rate has to slow to the mid-single digits. Note also that FY2021-FY2026 DPS levels are backed out of cash paid and run ~9% above the declared rate because HLI pays dividend equivalents on unvested restricted shares, so read the growth rate, not the per-share level, from the series.

screenFields.payoutBasis: dividends paid / FCF (CFO - capex), FY2026: 174.037m / 681.819m. Advisory/asset-manager model, so FCF = CFO - capex is the right base; equals 41.0% of net income.

Yield is only 1.99% TTM (1.84% on the FY2026 declared rate), so the total-return case depends entirely on the growth rate holding up.

No debt tag exists for FY2022-FY2026, so netDebt is computed as 0 - cash; the net-cash conclusion is safe but any loans payable to former shareholders would be omitted.

Every year was cross-checked against the quarterly rate facts in dpsAllFacts and against divPaid/weighted-basic-shares; quarterly sums reproduce the filed annual figure exactly in all 16 years that have four quarterly facts. Evidence: filed FY2012 annual declared DPS = 1.74 while the four FY2012 quarterly rate facts are 0.11 each (0.44); divPaid 64,041,000 / weighted basic 36,516,000 = 1.7538, i.e. the 1.74 was genuinely paid in cash, so the gap is a special and not a tagging artifact. FY2012 regular DPS is therefore 0.44, and FY2012 payout ratios (payoutNi 1.0661, payoutFcf 0.8379) are inflated by the special. issues: NO SPLITS: splitFacts is empty and sharesBasic is smooth across the whole window (33.3M in 2009 to 37.6M in 2024, no 1.5x/2x step anywhere), and divPaid/sharesBasic reconciles to the filed DPS in every year on a single basis. MarketAxess has not split since its 2004 IPO. splitAdjustments is therefore empty and NO year's DPS or share count was rescaled - yearsAdjusted is deliberately empty for all years 2009-2025.

FY2012 SPECIAL: filed annual DPS 1.74 vs four quarterly facts of 0.11 (= 0.44 regular). divPaid/sharesBasic = 1.7538, i.e. +298.6% vs the regular rate, so the excess 1.30 was a genuine cash special dividend, not a tagging error. Regular FY2012 DPS set to 0.44 (basis summed-quarters) and 1.30 carried in dps[].special. FY2012 payout ratios (payoutNi 1.0661, payoutFcf 0.8379) include the special and are not recurring.

FY2009 and FY2010 cross-check fails the 5% test: divPaid/sharesBasic = 0.0797 vs filed 0.07 (+13.8%) and 0.3206 vs 0.28 (+14.5%). Judgement call: this is a denominator artifact, not a DPS error. Weighted basic shares were 33.26M/33.16M in 2009-2010 against 38.08M/39.05M diluted, then jump to 37.0M basic in 2011 with no equity raise and no split, i.e. pre-2011 basic excludes a large participating/convertible class that still received the dividend. FY2009 is a partial dividend year: the dividend was initiated in 2009 and only one 0.07 quarterly payment fell in it (FY2009 annual = 0.07 = one quarter, FY2010 = 4 x 0.07). The 2009->2010 'increase' is a count-of-payments effect, not a rate rise; the quarterly RATE first rose in 2011 (0.07 -> 0.09). gMax (26.5788%/yr off the 0.07 base) is mechanically inflated by this. Measured from the first full year FY2010 (0.28), the 15-year CAGR is 17.2324%/yr, and on a rate basis the increase streak is 15 years (2011-2025) rather than 16.

Streak counted on annual regular DPS: strictly rising in all 16 years 2010-2025, no flat year and no cut, so cutsOrHolds is empty. No FY2020/FY2021 cut (2.40 -> 2.64 -> 2.80). windowLimited set false because FY2009 is the dividend-initiation year, so the streak cannot extend before the data window.

CAPEX UNDERSTATED / FCF OVERSTATED: the capex family resolves to PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment only (8.2M in FY2025), but tagHints shows PaymentsToDevelopSoftware with 17 points and 49.8M in FY2025 (plus CapitalizedComputerSoftwareAdditions 53.0M). For this filer capitalised software is the dominant real capital outlay. Per the stated rule I used the PP&E family because it is present, so fcf, payoutFcf and fcfGrowth5 are on a PP&E-only basis. Including PaymentsToDevelopSoftware would cut FY2025 FCF from 373.9M to ~324.1M and raise latest payoutFcf from 0.3081 to ~0.355.

NET DEBT assumes zero long-term debt: no debtLT family was returned at all, and ShortTermBorrowings exists for only two years (FY2024 = 0, FY2025 = 220,000,000). I treated debt as 0 in every year lacking a tag, matching MarketAxess being debt-free until the FY2025 revolver draw. Net debt is therefore essentially negative cash in all years and every netDebtToEbitda is negative (net cash); the FY2025 move from -1.313x to -0.7161x reflects the 220M draw plus the 420M buyback, not leverage stress.

Effective tax rate fell back to 21% for FY2009 and FY2010 (the pretax tag starts at 2011); immaterial because ROIC is null in both years for lack of operating income. All other years use tax/pretax, ranging 20.03% (FY2020) to 39.29% (FY2011); FY2025's 32.72% is elevated versus the ~24% recent norm and depresses FY2025 ROIC.

divPaid uses PaymentsOfOrdinaryDividends (cash-flow statement, 17 points). The alternative DividendsCommonStockCash (declared) differs by 0.5-2% per year (FY2025 113.785M vs 115.199M, FY2012 65.129M vs 64.041M) from declaration/payment timing; using it would not change any payout ratio materially.

analysis.assessment: MarketAxess is a high-quality, net-cash compounder whose dividend has stopped compounding: 1.86% starting yield on $3.04 (1.91% on the declared 2026 rate of $3.12), but the 5-year DPS CAGR has fallen to 4.84% from 14.28% over ten years, and the last four raises were a token $0.08 each. The payout is genuinely safe - 35.5% of software-inclusive free cash flow ($324.1M), 30.8% on a PP&E-only basis, 46.7% of net income, against $299.7M of net cash even after a $220M revolver draw and a $420M buyback - so there is ample room, but room is not the constraint. The constraint is the engine: FCF has gone backwards at -0.81%/yr over five years while the dividend grew 4.84%, net income fell from $299M to $247M, and ROIC has compressed from 60.6% to 27.2% as Tradeweb and Bloomberg took credit-trading share. The snowball here is roughly 1.9% yield plus mid-single-digit growth, call it 7%, with the real total return depending on the $420M/yr buyback rather than the $115M dividend. The thing most likely to break it is not the balance sheet but market share: another two years of flat operating income and the board keeps the streak alive with $0.08 raises while capital goes to repurchases.

stocks.m: Morningstar's ratings, fund/manager data and PitchBook private-market coverage are embedded in advisor, allocator and dealmaker workflows, and the multi-decade proprietary datasets behind them cannot be rebuilt or switched away from without re-benchmarking a client's entire reporting stack.

normalised.dpsMethod: Rule (a): filed annual DPS tag with ~1-year duration. Used CommonStockDividendsPerShareDeclared FY facts (start Jan 1 / end Dec 31, 364-365 days, 10-K, fp=FY) for every year FY2009-FY2025. No split adjustment applied anywhere — splitFacts is empty and Morningstar has never split its stock since its 2005 IPO; sharesBasic moves smoothly from 48.1M (2009) to 41.9M (2025) with no step change, confirming a single, unchanged share basis across the whole window. Cross-checked every year against divPaid/sharesBasic: that derived series tracks the companion CommonStockDividendsPerShareCashPaid tag within ~1% in all 15 dividend-paying years, and differs from the DECLARED series only by the one-quarter declaration-to-payment lag (plus the Dec-2012 accelerated payment). Declared, not cash-paid, is used as the regular annual DPS because it is the filer's own annual rate and is the only monotonic series.

specials.note: No special dividends found. The one year where divPaid/sharesBasic sits ABOVE filed DPS is FY2012 (0.5255 vs declared 0.425, +23.7%), but this is NOT a special: the quarterly declared facts for 2012 are 0.10/0.10/0.10/0.125 = 0.425, while quarterly CASH PAID is 0.10/0.10/0.10/0.225 = 0.525 — Morningstar pulled the Q1-2013 payment (0.125) into December 2012 ahead of the expected 2013 dividend-tax change. The mirror image confirms it: FY2013 Q1 cash paid = 0.00, and FY2013 divPaid/sharesBasic = 0.3766 vs declared 0.545 (-30.9%). Same cash, shifted across the year boundary, at the ordinary regular rate. live.regularDividendIfSpecial is null and live.ttmDividend 1.955 is consistent with the current regular 0.50 quarterly rate (2026 Q1 and Q2 both 0.50).

issues: SPLITS: none applied. splitFacts is empty; Morningstar has never split since its 2005 IPO. Evidence checked year by year: (i) divPaid/sharesBasic equals the filed cash-paid DPS within ~1% in every paying year on a SINGLE basis, so no year sits on an old basis; (ii) the DPS trend is smooth with no year ~1.5x/2x/3x its neighbours; (iii) sharesBasic declines monotonically 48.1M -> 41.9M with no step change. splitAdjustments is therefore empty and NO year's DPS was divided or shares multiplied.

JUDGEMENT CALL - which DPS tag: two full annual series exist. CommonStockDividendsPerShareDeclared (used) is monotonic 0.05 -> 1.87. CommonStockDividendsPerShareCashPaid runs 0/0/0.20/0.525/0.375/0.68/0.76/0.88/0.92/1.00/1.12/1.20/1.26/1.44/1.50/1.62/1.82 and would show a FY2013 'cut' (0.525 -> 0.375) that is purely a payment-timing artefact. Declared is the filer's own annual rate and is what the streak and CAGRs are built on. If the consumer prefers cash-paid basis, every DPS value is ~2-3% lower and FY2013 shows a false cut.

gMax = 27.31%/yr is measured from FY2010 (DPS 0.05, the initiation year, only one partial-year quarter declared) to FY2025, 15 years. Use g3/g5/g10 (all ~8.6-9.0%) for any real growth read.

normalised.notes: MORN is a clean case: one share basis throughout (no splits ever), a complete filed annual declared-DPS series from FY2009, and a companion cash-paid series plus full quarterly facts that let every year be cross-checked independently. Sixteen consecutive years of increases from the FY2010 initiation through FY2025 (0.05 -> 1.87), no cut, no hold, no special dividend, and no COVID-era interruption. The three years where divPaid/sharesBasic diverges from the filed DPS by more than 5% (2011, 2012, 2013) are all explained by declaration-versus-payment timing, with the Dec-2012 pull-forward of the Q1-2013 payment as the single largest distortion; the cash-paid tag confirms this in each case and no special dividend was separated out. Growth has settled into a tight band (3yr 8.60%, 5yr 8.92%, 10yr 9.00%) against a very low FY2025 FCF payout of 17.4% and NI payout of 20.6%, with 5yr FCF growth of 7.55% roughly keeping pace with the dividend. Leverage peaked at 2.29x net debt/EBITDA in FY2022 after the LCD acquisition and has come back to 0.84x in FY2025, though the 787M of FY2025 buybacks (against 76.9M of dividends) pushed net debt back up from 196M to 598M and cut equity from 1,619M to 1,222M. The main gaps are structural rather than judgemental: revenue is absent from the join for FY2011-FY2015, and pre-2018 debt tags are thin enough that net debt is nulled for FY2013-FY2016.

rules.note: Latest regular annual DPS 1.87 (FY2025 declared) / price 202.67 = 0.923%. Even on the current 0.50 quarterly rate annualised (2.00) it is only 0.99%, and on live ttmDividend 1.955 it is 0.96%. Far below the 1.5% floor — this is the rule MORN misses worst.

rules.name: Dividend growth above 8%/yr
rules.note: 5-yr DPS CAGR 1.22 (FY2020) -> 1.87 (FY2025) = 8.92%. Tightly corroborated by g3 8.60% and g10 9.00%. Passes but is not in strong territory; gMax 27.3% is an artefact of the 0.05 initiation base and is ignored.

rules.name: Payout with room left
rules.note: FY2025 divPaid 76.9M / FCF 442.6M (CFO 589.7M - capex 147.1M) = 17.37%; NI payout 20.6%. Fails on the LOW side — this is the opposite of a stress signal: enormous runway, but management is returning cash through buybacks ($787M in FY2025 vs $76.9M of dividends) rather than the dividend. Asset-manager/data-vendor FCF = CFO - capex is the right basis here.

rules.name: Streak long enough to prove policy
rules.note: 16 consecutive increases FY2010-FY2025 (0.05 -> 1.87). The streak starts at the dividend's initiation year, which sits inside the XBRL window (data begins FY2009), so it is NOT window-limited and no prior-research figure is needed. Prior research streak of 16 agrees exactly.

rules.name: Earnings growing at least as fast as the dividend
rules.note: FCF 307.6M (FY2020) -> 442.6M (FY2025) = 7.55%/yr, 1.37pp behind the dividend. Endpoints are positive and clean so no net-income substitution is needed; on NI the comparison is far better (223.6M -> 374.2M = 10.8%/yr), but the FY2020 base was a COVID-boosted cash year and FY2022-23 FCF sagged to 168M/197M after the LCD deal. A narrow, benign miss, not a coverage problem at a 17% payout.

rules.name: High return on invested capital
rules.note: FY2025 ROIC 21.9% (FY2024 21.1%), well into strong territory. The FY2022 trough of 4.8% was a genuinely depressed year (43.3% effective tax, operating income 167.8M, plus $1.1B of LCD acquisition debt), and the recovery to ~21% across two straight years shows the trough was cyclical, not structural.

rules.name: Balance sheet not competing with you
rules.threshold: net debt / EBITDA < 2.5x; net cash passes outright
rules.note: FY2025 net debt 598.1M / EBITDA 716.5M = 0.835x, down from the FY2022 post-LCD peak of 2.29x. Caveat from review: FY2025 current debt is not tagged and was assumed zero, so read this as >=0.84x. Even with a plausible 30-50M of current debt it stays under 0.9x. Buybacks pushed net debt back up from 196M to 598M in FY2025 — leverage is a capital-allocation choice here, not a constraint.

rules.name: Why competitors cannot take the business
rules.note: Morningstar's ratings, fund data, PitchBook private-market coverage and index/Direct platforms are wired into advisor, allocator and dealmaker workflows; the datasets are decades-deep and self-reinforcing (more coverage -> more subscribers -> more coverage). Switching means rebuilding client reporting and re-benchmarking. It is not a price competition.

rules.name: Management treats the dividend as a promise
rules.threshold: no cut in FY2020/2021; any cut or suspension in window fails
rules.note: FY2019 1.14 -> FY2020 1.22 -> FY2021 1.31: raised straight through COVID. No cut, hold or suspension anywhere in FY2009-FY2025. 2008 is outside the XBRL window (data starts FY2009) and is not assessed; the dividend was only initiated in 2010 anyway, so there was nothing to cut in 2008.

analysis.assessment: MORN is a high-quality compounder that is a poor fit for a dividend-income screen and a decent fit for a dividend-growth one: 21.9% ROIC, 0.84x net debt/EBITDA, 16 straight raises and a 17.4% FCF payout, but a starting yield of only 0.92% on the FY2025 regular DPS of $1.87 against a $202.67 price. The snowball is almost entirely back-loaded — at 8.9% dividend growth and no multiple change it takes roughly 8 years for yield-on-cost to clear 1.8%, so this only works for a holder with a 15-year-plus horizon who is really buying the 7-8% revenue growth and the buyback (787M of repurchases in FY2025, 11x the 76.9M paid in dividends, shrinking the count from 41.9M weighted-average to 37.5M outstanding today). Payout runway is enormous — the dividend could triple and still sit inside the 20-60% band — so the binding constraint is management's revealed preference for buybacks over payout, not cash availability. The thing most likely to break it is not a cut but a repeat of FY2022: leverage went to 2.29x and ROIC to 4.8% on the LCD acquisition, and a second large debt-funded deal would again slow the raises to the high-single digits while the yield stays under 1%. 5-yr FCF growth of 7.55% lagging the 8.92% dividend CAGR is the early hint of that, though at a 17% payout it is arithmetically irrelevant for at least a decade.
analysis.moat: Morningstar's ratings, fund/manager data and PitchBook private-market coverage are embedded in advisor, allocator and dealmaker workflows, and the multi-decade proprietary datasets behind them cannot be rebuilt or switched away from without re-benchmarking a client's entire reporting stack.
strengths: ROIC 21.9% in FY2025 and 21.1% in FY2024, both well above the 15% strong bar, after a clean recovery from the 4.8% FY2022 trough
Payout of only 17.4% of FCF and 20.6% of net income — the dividend could triple before reaching the top of the usable band
16 consecutive increases including straight through COVID (1.14 -> 1.22 -> 1.31), with no cut, hold or special anywhere in the window
Net debt/EBITDA back to ~0.84x from the 2.29x post-LCD peak; leverage is discretionary, not forced
Dividend growth remarkably stable across horizons: g3 8.60%, g5 8.92%, g10 9.00% — a policy, not a streak of one-offs
Revenue compounding 7.5% in FY2025 to $2.45B with an 18.1% FCF margin
risks: 0.92% starting yield is the dominant problem: the income only becomes meaningful after a decade-plus of compounding
Capital allocation strongly favours buybacks ($787M FY2025 vs $76.9M dividends), so dividend growth is capped by choice even though coverage is trivial
5-yr FCF CAGR 7.55% trails the 8.92% DPS CAGR; FY2022-23 FCF (168M / 197M) shows the series is acquisition-sensitive
FY2025 buybacks pushed net debt from 196M to 598M and cut equity from 1,619M to 1,222M — a second LCD-scale deal would repeat the FY2022 leverage and ROIC hit
FY2025 current debt is untagged and assumed zero, so the 0.84x leverage figure is a floor
Ratings/data revenue is exposed to asset-management fee compression and to AI-native research competitors eroding the commodity end of the data business
flags: fy2025-current-debt-assumed-zero: net debt/EBITDA 0.84x is a floor
buyback-dominant capital allocation: $787M repurchases vs $76.9M dividends in FY2025
analysis.sectorNote: MORN is classified Financials but is an investment-research/data/index subscription business, not a bank, insurer or REIT. Rule 4 was therefore assessed on the standard FCF = CFO - capex basis, which is appropriate here (capex is 147.1M of software/property against 589.7M of CFO, so FCF is comfortably positive and meaningful); no REIT (AFFO/CFO) or utility (net income) substitution was needed. Rule 8 is meaningful because MORN carries ordinary corporate debt rather than a bank's deposit-funded balance sheet, so it was not nulled. The only sector-flavoured read is rule 2: a data/subscription compounder in Financials structurally yields well under the screen's band because value is returned through buybacks.

normalised.dpsMethod: Filed annual CommonStockDividendsPerShareDeclared (10-K, ~364-365 day duration) used directly for every fiscal year 2009-2025 (rule a). FY2009 and FY2010 divided by 2 for the 2013-05-20 2:1 split; FY2013 is the split year and FY2011-FY2012 are its two restated comparatives, so all three were already filed on the post-split basis and were left untouched. Every year cross-checked against PaymentsOfDividends / WeightedAverageNumberOfSharesOutstandingBasic: all 17 years agree within 0.75% (FY2009 -0.74%, FY2024/FY2025 -0.12%, all others <0.1%).

splitAdjustments.note: StockholdersEquityNoteStockSplitConversionRatio = 2 at 2013-05-20 (2-for-1). Evidence for which years were already restated: divPaid/sharesBasic equals the filed DPS in every single year, and sharesBasic step-changes from 18.585M (FY2010) to 37.386M (FY2011) - i.e. the FY2011 and FY2012 figures in the SEC facts come from the FY2013 10-K comparatives and are already post-split (filed DPS 0.55 and 0.635 sit smoothly between 0.52 and 0.76). Only FY2009 (1.01 -> 0.505) and FY2010 (1.04 -> 0.52) were on the old basis; DPS divided by 2 and sharesBasic multiplied by 2 (18,052,000 -> 36,104,000 and 18,585,000 -> 37,170,000). Two adjusted years is exactly consistent with a split year plus a two-year restatement window covering 2011-2013.

Concrete and durable; it does not compete on price.

analysis.assessment: AWR is a $3.4B regulated California water utility paying a 2.22% trailing yield (2.50% on the post-August-2026 rate of ~$2.182) and compounding the dividend at 8.66%/yr over five years - a clean, believable snowball of roughly 2.2% yield plus high-single-digit growth, backed by 16 straight increases in the data and a research streak of 71 years with no cut in 2020 or 2021. The cover is real but narrow and must be read off earnings, not cash: capex has exceeded operating cash flow in every year since FY2019 (FY2025 CFO $229.7M vs capex $236.8M, FCF -$7.1M), so the dividend is 57.2% of net income and is funded alongside the rate-base build with debt and ATM equity. That funding model is exactly what is straining the other half of the scorecard - net debt/EBITDA has climbed from 1.56x in FY2014 to 3.08x in FY2025, the highest in the series, while ROIC sits at 8.59% in a tight 6-11% band because a regulated utility earns its authorised return and nothing more. Net income grew 8.58%/yr over five years against an 8.66% dividend CAGR, so the payout ratio is creeping up rather than down, leaving no self-financing runway. The thing most likely to break it is a CPUC rate case or cost-of-capital decision that lags inflation and interest expense: with leverage at 3.08x and share count already rising 36.9M to 38.55M since FY2021, an unfavourable return-on-equity ruling would force the growth rate down toward the low-to-mid single digits long before it would force a cut.
analysis.moat: Golden State Water's CPUC-franchised California service territories are legal monopolies over sunk, non-replicable pipe networks, and ASUS holds 50-year sole-source privatisation contracts on US military bases - neither can be bid away by a competitor.
analysis.sectorNote: AWR is a regulated rate-base water utility, so two rules are poor fits and were read accordingly. Rule 4: FCF (CFO - capex) is negative in every year FY2019-FY2025 because capex is the growth engine and is funded with debt and equity by design, so dividends/FCF is meaningless and undefined; payout was assessed against net income (57.2% in FY2025, 44.6%-71.9% across the window) as the rule permits. Rule 6 inherits the same problem - the FY2020 FCF endpoint is negative so a CAGR is undefined - and was therefore run on net income (8.58%/yr) versus the 8.66% dividend CAGR. Rule 7 is not adjusted but should be read in context: a regulated utility earns its CPUC-authorised return, so an 8.6% ROIC is a normal outcome rather than evidence of a weak business - it is nonetheless a real constraint on the compounding rate and is scored as a fail on the stated threshold.
strengths: 16 consecutive annual increases in the data with no hold or cut, on a research streak of 71 years - among the longest dividend records in the US market
Dividend growth of 8.66%/yr over 5 years, 8.29% over 10 and 8.77% over the full 16-year window - remarkably stable, and confirmed forward by the ~8.2% August 2026 raise to a $0.5455 quarterly rate
Structural monopoly: CPUC-franchised service territories plus 50-year sole-source military base contracts through ASUS
Market cap of $3.42B is inside the ideal sub-$5B band, and the yield at 2.22% trailing / 2.50% forward sits in the usable middle of the band
Earnings quality is steady - net income $86.4M (FY2020) to $130.4M (FY2025), ROIC in a tight 8.5%-11.2% band with no loss years
risks: Net debt/EBITDA at 3.08x is the highest in the 16-year series and has risen every year since FY2019; at 4x the screen would force an outright avoid
Free cash flow has been negative for seven straight years (FY2025 -$7.1M), so every dollar of dividend is effectively funded by new debt and ATM equity
Net income growth of 8.58%/yr trails the 8.66% dividend CAGR, so the payout ratio is drifting up; at 57.2% of net income there is only about 3pp of headroom before the rule-4 band breaks
ROIC of 8.59% is capped by the CPUC-authorised return - there is no mechanism for the business to out-earn its regulator

Regulatory concentration: a single California rate case or cost-of-capital decision sets the growth rate for the whole company, and EBITDA is already lumpy from ASUS military-contract timing (FY2023 operating income $196.7M vs FY2024 $184.5M)

A 71-year streak means the dividend is effectively an institutional promise - management will defend it through a bad rate case by adding leverage or issuing equity rather than cutting, which transfers the risk to the growth rate and to per-share dilution

issues: CAPEX IS THE BIG GAP: no capex family was extracted and the per-year table carries no capex column. The filer's tag is PaymentsToAcquireWaterAndWasteWaterSystems, but tagHints exposes only its LAST value (FY2025 = 516,991,000). FY2025 FCF is NEGATIVE (302,561,000 CFO - 516,991,000 capex = -214,430,000), so payoutFcf is null by the stated rule (fcf <= 0). This flatly contradicts priorEstimates.payoutPctFcf = 60. CWT is a rate-base water utility funding a large capital programme with debt and equity issuance; FCF-based payout is not a meaningful coverage metric here and the dividend is not covered by internally generated cash. Also note capex may be understated: PaymentsToAcquireLifeInsurancePolicies (3,364,000) and PaymentsToAcquireBusinessesNetOfCashAcquired (0) are separate investing lines not included.

The raw data is not cleanly consistent with it: the 2010-04-01..2010-06-30 declared fact is already 0.1488 (post-split) in a 10-Q/A, while the 2010-01-01..2010-06-30 fact in the SAME form is 0.2975 - which is a single pre-split quarterly rate sitting on a 180-day duration, i.e. an internally contradictory pair. Those 2010 comparatives are only reconcilable if they were re-filed in 2011 filings, which the extract's form/fp fields cannot confirm. This does NOT change the conclusion (yearsAdjusted=[] holds whether the split was mid-2010 or mid-2011, since sharesBasic is unbroken from 2009 onward), but the note asserts the filing provenance ("the four 2010 quarterly facts in the FY2011/FY2012 10-Ks") as established fact when the file does not carry filing-year metadata.

issues.detail: FY2025 capex of 516,991,000 is taken from tagHints.lastVal for PaymentsToAcquireWaterAndWasteWaterSystems. tagHints shows that tag has 18 points (a full 2008-2025 series exists in the filer's XBRL) but the extract exposes only the last value, so the record's one-year FCF is built on an endpoint the file cannot cross-check against any other year. Separately, CapitalExpendituresIncurredButNotYetPaid = 67,831,000 at FY2025 confirms a large accrual/cash timing wedge, on top of the PaymentsToAcquireLifeInsurancePolicies (3,364,000) omission the record already flags. The negative-FCF conclusion survives all of this comfortably (a 67.8m swing does not close a 214.4m gap), so the sign is safe.

rules.name: Small enough to grow
rules.note: live marketCap 2,971,368,755 at $48.05 (2026-09-17). Comfortably in the ideal band — a small-cap regulated water utility, so incremental rate-base additions still move the needle.

rules.name: Starting yield in the usable band
rules.note: latest regular annual DPS 1.24 (FY2025 filed, cash-paid basis) / price 48.05 = 2.581%. On the live ttm 1.305 it is 2.72%, and on the current declared rate of 0.335/qtr (1.34 annualised) it is 2.79%. All three readings sit mid-band.

rules.name: Dividend growth above 8%/yr
rules.note: g5 = (1.24/0.85)^(1/5)-1 = 7.845%, just under the bar. It is worse than it looks: the FY2025 endpoint is cash-paid and lumpy (Q1 0.34 vs 0.30 for Q2-Q4), so on a declared-rate basis (1.20) g5 is ~7.1%. g3 7.43%, g10 6.35%, gMax 4.75%. Miss, not a near-miss to round up.

rules.name: Payout with room left
rules.value: 57.6% of net income (FCF payout not meaningful: FY2025 FCF -$214.4M)
rules.note: SECTOR CARVE-OUT APPLIED: regulated utility with FCF <= 0 because of rate-base capex, so assessed against net income per the rule. FY2025 dividends 73,853,000 / net income 128,211,000 = 57.6%, inside 20-60% but with only ~2pp of headroom. FY2025 CFO 302.6M less capex 517.0M = -214.4M, so the dividend is funded by debt and equity issuance, not internally generated cash. FY2023 payoutNi was 113.7% on a depressed earnings year — the metric is volatile.

rules.name: Streak long enough to prove policy, short enough to still be fast
rules.note: The XBRL window starts FY2009 and shows 16 straight increases with no hold or cut, so the data streak is window-limited. Prior research streak of 58 years is plausible and consistent (CWT is a long-standing Dividend King). Using 58: it clears the 10-year floor decisively but breaks the 30-year ceiling, which is exactly the failure mode this rule screens for — a very mature policy whose growth has already decelerated to single digits (gMax 4.75%).

rules.name: Earnings growing at least as fast as the dividend
rules.value: 5-yr NI CAGR 5.78% vs DPS CAGR 7.85% (NI substituted)
rules.note: FCF SUBSTITUTED WITH NET INCOME: capex is recoverable for FY2025 only, so fcfGrowth5 is null and the FY2020 FCF endpoint does not exist. Net income 96,831,000 (FY2020) -> 128,211,000 (FY2025) = 5.78%/yr, a 2.07pp shortfall against dividend growth — the payout ratio has been rising as a result (43.1% in FY2020 to 57.6% in FY2025). On a 10-year view NI CAGR is 11.0% (45.0M FY2015 -> 128.2M FY2025), so the shortfall is recent, driven by the weak FY2023 (51.9M) and the FY2024 191M spike that flatters the base year comparison in the other direction.

rules.name: High return on invested capital
rules.value: n/a for FY2025 (equity missing); 7.31% FY2020, the highest in 12 computable years
rules.note: Equity drops out of the extract from FY2021, so ROIC is null for FY2021-FY2025. The rule is still assessable on history: every one of the 12 computable years (FY2009-FY2020) sits between 3.97% and 7.31%, never remotely near 12%. This is structural, not a data artifact — a regulated utility earns an allowed return on rate base (roughly 9-10% on equity, less after leverage and tax), so ROIC above 12% is not achievable by design.

rules.name: Balance sheet not competing with you
rules.note: FY2025 net debt 1,422,418,000 / EBITDA 316,892,000 = 4.4887x, up sharply from 3.14x in FY2024 on a ~367M increase in long-term debt. And it is understated: ShortTermBorrowings (commercial paper) is excluded from the net-debt build, so the true figure is above 4.49x. Only FY2017 (2.35x) has ever cleared 2.5x in the 17-year window. Crosses the >4x avoid trigger.

rules.name: Why competitors cannot take the business
rules.threshold: concrete durable mechanism, not price competition
rules.note: CWT holds state-granted exclusive franchises to supply water in defined California, Washington, New Mexico, Hawaii and Texas territories; no competitor can lay a duplicate distribution network into a served household, and pricing is set by regulators rather than by rivalry. The moat is real, but it is a moat on a return that regulators cap — it protects the revenue, not the ROIC.

rules.name: Management treats the dividend as a promise
rules.threshold: no cut in FY2020/FY2021; any cut or suspension in window fails
rules.note: Sixteen consecutive annual increases FY2010-FY2025, zero holds, zero cuts, no COVID pause, no special dividends. 2008 is outside the XBRL window and cannot be checked from this data. divPaid/sharesBasic corroborates the filed DPS to within 0.33% in every year, so the increase record is not an artifact of tagging.

analysis.sectorNote: CWT is a regulated water utility, so three rules are poor fits and were read accordingly. Rule 4 was assessed against net income (57.6%) rather than FCF, because FY2025 FCF is -$214.4M by design: a rate-base utility raises debt and equity to fund capex and recovers it through rates over decades, so negative FCF is the business model, not distress — but it does mean the dividend is not covered by internally generated cash. Rule 6 likewise falls back to net income. Rule 7 (ROIC > 12%) is structurally unreachable for any regulated utility, since the allowed return is set by commissions; the 3.97-7.31% range observed is normal for the sector rather than evidence of a bad business. Rule 8 is the one where the sector excuse does NOT hold — utilities do run 3-4x leverage routinely, but 4.49x and rising, with commercial paper excluded, is high even against utility peers and it is what funds the dividend.
analysis.assessment: CWT offers a 2.58% starting yield on the FY2025 regular DPS of $1.24 (2.79% on the current $0.335 quarterly declared rate) growing at 7.85%/yr over five years — a ~10.4% snowball before multiple change, which is respectable but not the 8%+ growth this screen demands, and on a declared-rate basis growth is closer to 7.1%. The runway is thinner than the headline: net income grew only 5.78%/yr over the same five years against 7.85% dividend growth, pushing the payout from 43.1% of earnings in FY2020 to 57.6% in FY2025, so each further raise now has to come out of a shrinking cushion. There is no FCF cushion at all — FY2025 CFO of $302.6M against $517.0M of rate-base capex gives -$214.4M of free cash flow, meaning every dollar of the $73.9M dividend is effectively financed, and net debt/EBITDA has jumped from 3.14x to at least 4.49x in one year on ~$367M of new long-term debt. The thing most likely to break it is a California rate case that comes in below the requested return while the capital programme keeps running: that is exactly the FY2023 pattern (net income $51.9M, payout 113.7% of earnings, leverage 5.06x), and a repeat with leverage already at 4.5x forces the choice between equity issuance that dilutes the 3.8%-a-year share growth further and slowing the dividend to a token 2-3% raise. A 58-year increase record and an exclusive regulated franchise make an outright cut unlikely; the realistic downside is a dividend that quietly decelerates toward 3-4% growth, which is not the compounder this screen is looking for.
analysis.moat: Regulated water across five states under exclusive state-granted service territories no competitor can duplicate, with rate base growing alongside capital spend — but regulators cap the return, so the moat protects revenue, not ROIC.
strengths: 58-year dividend increase record (16 confirmed in the FY2009-FY2025 XBRL window) with zero holds, zero cuts, no COVID pause and no special dividends; divPaid/sharesBasic corroborates the filed DPS to within 0.33% every single year.
Exclusive regulated service territories in CA, WA, NM, HI and TX — a genuine structural monopoly on the served household.
$2.97B market cap, deep in the ideal <$5B band; rate-base additions are still material relative to the base.
Starting yield of 2.58% sits mid-band and is well clear of the distress zone; FY2025 payout of 57.6% of earnings is still inside the 20-60% window.
risks: Net debt/EBITDA of at least 4.49x (understated — excludes commercial paper) after a ~$367M one-year increase in long-term debt; crosses the >4x avoid trigger and was 5.06x as recently as FY2023.
FY2025 FCF is -$214.4M (CFO $302.6M less capex $517.0M): the dividend is funded by external capital, not internally generated cash.
Earnings growth (5-yr NI CAGR 5.78%) is running 2.07pp behind dividend growth (7.85%), so the payout ratio is on a rising path — 43.1% in FY2020 to 57.6% in FY2025.
Earnings are rate-case-volatile: FY2023 net income of $51.9M put payout at 113.7%; a single adverse California decision repeats that with leverage now much higher.
Persistent equity issuance — basic shares up from 41.5M (FY2009) to 59.6M (FY2025), ~3.8% a year recently — dilutes per-share growth and is the funding mechanism the capex plan depends on.
ROIC has never exceeded 7.31% in twelve computable years and is structurally capped by regulators; it is also unmeasurable for FY2021-FY2025 because equity is missing from the extract.

screenFields.payoutBasis: percent of net income (regulated utility with FY2025 FCF of -$214.4M; FCF payout not computable or meaningful)

estimateCorrections.why: Basis change, not a small revision. The prior 60% implied a positive, covered FCF payout; FY2025 FCF is actually -$214.4M (CFO $302.6M less rate-base capex $517.0M), so an FCF payout ratio does not exist for CWT. The 57.6% now shown is dividends/net income, the sector-appropriate substitute, and the screen must label it as such — otherwise a reader sees '57.6% of FCF' and concludes coverage that is not there.
Not previously tracked. At >=4.49x (understated, excludes commercial paper) this is the single metric that drives the 'avoid' verdict, up from 3.14x in FY2024, and it belongs on the screen.

Not previously tracked and not computable for FY2021-FY2025 because equity drops out of the extract. Recorded as null rather than carried forward: the last computable year (FY2020) was 7.31%, and no year in twelve exceeded that, so any ROIC-based filter should treat CWT as structurally sub-12%.

Below the 3pp materiality bar (0.85pp) so not a correction in the strict sense, but logged because the direction is misleading: the 7.85% rests on a cash-paid FY2025 endpoint of 1.24 against a declared rate of 1.20, and on a declared basis g5 is ~7.1% — i.e. the prior estimate of 7 was closer to the economic truth than the derived figure.

No change. The data streak of 16 is window-limited (XBRL begins FY2009) and the prior research figure of 58 is plausible and internally consistent with 16 unbroken increases at the front of the window, so the research figure is retained and the data confirmation is recorded alongside it.

stocks.m: Exclusive state-granted gas and electric distribution franchises in fast-growing Delmarva and Florida territories - a legal monopoly on the pipes and wires with an allowed regulated return, where customer growth arrives with population rather than being won from anyone.

normalised.dpsMethod: Filed annual CommonStockDividendsPerShareDeclared (FY duration ~364 days, 10-K) used for every year except FY2020. FY2009-FY2011 divided by 1.5 for the September 2013 3-for-2 split (FY2012 onward were already filed on the post-split basis). FY2020's filed annual fact (1.585) is an XBRL error - it duplicates FY2019 - so FY2020 was rebuilt from the quarterly rate facts: 0.405 (Q1) + 0.44 + 0.44 + 0.44 = 1.725, corroborated by declared Dividends/shares = 1.7417 and by the FY2021 Q1 rate of 0.44. Every year cross-checked against both PaymentsOfDividendsCommonStock/sharesBasic and the declared 'Dividends' tag/sharesBasic.

splitAdjustments.note: 3-for-2 split effective September 2013. Evidence for the date: the quarterly declared rate fell from 0.385 (Q2 2013) to 0.257 (Q3 2013), a factor of 1.4981, and FY2013's filed annual 1.0133 = 0.365/1.5 + 0.385/1.5 + 0.257 + 0.257. Evidence for WHICH years are on the old basis: sharesBasic steps from 9,555,799 (FY2011) to 14,379,216 (FY2012), a 1.505x jump, and the raw filed DPS steps 1.365 (FY2011) -> 0.96 (FY2012), so FY2012 is already post-split while FY2011 is not. FY2012 and FY2013 therefore needed NO adjustment; only FY2009-FY2011 were divided by 1.5 and their shares multiplied by 1.5. This is one year narrower than the textbook two-year restatement window would predict - the FY2013 10-K did restate FY2011 on its income statement, but the companyfacts extract kept the original pre-split FY2011 fact. The adjusted series 0.8333 / 0.8700 / 0.9100 / 0.9600 is smooth with ~0.04/yr steps, which no other choice produces.

specials.note: No special dividends found. The filed DPS sits 3.7-13.0% ABOVE PaymentsOfDividendsCommonStock/sharesBasic in every single year, which is a uniform structural gap (DRIP shares are issued rather than paid in cash, plus declared-vs-paid timing), not a special in any one year. Declared-tag cross-check available FY2009-FY2012 (DividendsCommonStockCash) and FY2015-FY2025 (Dividends), matching filed DPS to within 0.0-1.2% except FY2009 +2.6% and FY2023 +3.9%; FY2013 and FY2014 have no declared-dividend fact and rest on the filed DPS alone. Live ttmDividend 2.84 = Q4-2025 0.685 + Q1-2026 0.685 + Q2-2026 0.735 + Q3-2026 0.735, where the Q3-2026 rate is inferred from the Q2-2026 rate holding (the filed Q3-2026 fact is a zero placeholder); the +5.4% gap to FY2025 DPS is fully explained by the Q2-2026 raise. Live regularDividendIfSpecial is null.

issues: FY2020 filed annual DPS is wrong in the source data. CommonStockDividendsPerShareDeclared for 2020-01-01..2020-12-31 (10-K) is 1.585, identical to FY2019. The FY2020 quarterly rate facts are 0.405 / 0.44 / 0.44, and the FY2021 Q1 rate is 0.44, so Q4 2020 was 0.44 and the declared total is 1.725. The 10-Q/A 9M YTD fact of 1.285 refutes the filed annual: 1.585 would force a Q4 rate of 0.30, below the Q1 rate of 0.405. JUDGEMENT CALL: I overrode the filed annual value with 1.725 (basis 'summed-quarters'). Using the filed 1.585 would make FY2020 a flat year and cut the streak from 16 to 5.

SPLIT SCOPE JUDGEMENT CALL: the September 2013 3-for-2 split required adjusting only FY2009, FY2010 and FY2011 (3 years), not FY2012 or FY2013. That is one year narrower than the 'split year plus two prior years already restated' rule predicts. Evidence: sharesBasic jumps 9,555,799 -> 14,379,216 between FY2011 and FY2012 (1.505x), raw filed DPS steps 1.365 -> 0.96, and the FY2013 quarterly reconciliation 0.365/1.5 + 0.385/1.5 + 0.257 + 0.257 = 1.0133. Likely cause: the companyfacts extract kept the ORIGINAL FY2011 10-K fact rather than the FY2013 10-K restated comparative.

splitFacts is an empty array - there is no split-ratio fact in the data, so the 1.5 ratio and the timing were inferred from the Q2->Q3 2013 quarterly rate step (0.385 -> 0.257 = /1.4981) and the FY2013 annual reconciliation. Only the QUARTER is evidenced; the exact date 2013-09-09 in splitAdjustments is an inference, not a sourced value.

netDebt excludes ShortTermBorrowings, a 16-point debtCur candidate (2010-12-31 to 2025-12-31) that was not joined into the table. For a rate-base utility running commercial paper this is material: the reported netDebtToEbitda of 4.59x (FY2025) is a FLOOR, not the full figure, and the same understatement applies to every year from FY2010 on.

divPaid in fin uses the primary tag PaymentsOfDividendsCommonStock, which is CASH dividends paid and excludes shares issued under the dividend reinvestment plan. It runs BELOW declared DPS x sharesBasic in EVERY year: 2009 -13.0%, 2010 -10.9%, 2011 -10.6%, 2012 -10.6%, 2013 -10.5%, 2014 -10.5%, 2015 -6.8%, 2016 -6.6%, 2017 -4.7%, 2018 -6.2%, 2019 -5.0%, 2020 -5.8%, 2021 -4.5%, 2022 -4.7%, 2023 -5.5%, 2024 -3.9%, 2025 -3.7%. The gap is structural DRIP, not a special dividend. Consequence: every payoutFcf and payoutNi here understates the declared payout by roughly 4%; on a declared basis FY2025 payoutNi would be 0.4549 rather than 0.4326.

Declared-tag coverage is incomplete: the Dividends series starts at 2015-12-31 and DividendsCommonStockCash ends at 2012-12-31, so FY2013 and FY2014 have NO declared-dividend fact and cannot be cross-checked by that route - exactly two of the years where the divPaid/shares gap is widest (-10.5%).

FY2009 ROIC, netDebt and netDebtToEbitda are null: the table has no debtLT and no debtCur for 2009-12-31 (both LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations and LongTermDebtCurrent start at 2010-12-31), so invested capital and net debt cannot be built.

FY2024 and FY2025 have no pretax value in the table - the primary pretax tag stops at 2023-12-31 and the alternate tag's series is empty. Rather than use the 21% fallback I derived pretax as netIncome + tax (FY2024 161,800k, eff rate 26.70%; FY2025 193,000k, eff rate 27.31%). The proxy validates on FY2023 (115,300k vs filed 115,290k, 0.01% off) and FY2021 (exact). The flat 21% fallback would instead give FY2024 ROIC 0.0669 and FY2025 0.0633.

Capex: two competing tags cover 2022-2025. I used PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment (17 points, full window) and named it in capexTag. PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets gives 1,138,000,000 for FY2023, roughly 6x the PP&E figure, because it bundles the Florida City Gas acquisition - rejected as not capex. The two also differ by 21.8m in FY2025 (448.6 vs 470.4) and 12.5m in FY2022; FCF would be that much lower on the alternate tag.

FCF is negative in 11 of 17 years (FY2012-FY2021, FY2024, FY2025) because this is a rate-base utility funding a capex program far above CFO, so payoutFcf is null for those years by rule. The two positive-FCF recent years give payoutFcf of 1.15 (FY2022) and 2.68 (FY2023): the dividend is not covered by free cash flow on any recent measure. priorEstimates payoutPctFcf = 40 is unsupported by this data and was discarded.
fcfGrowth5 is null: both endpoints are negative FCF (FY2020 -6,595k, FY2025 -214,900k), so a CAGR is undefined.

Sign-convention problem in the source: FY2020 buybacks -22,627,000, FY2021 -15,851,000, FY2022 -4,534,000 and the ProceedsFromRepurchaseOfEquity hint (-721,000) are all sign-flipped, i.e. net share issuance booked under repurchase tags. Not used in any computation here, but flagged.

Balance-sheet duplication in the source: FY2012 carries the identical cash (3,361,000) and debtCur (8,196,000) as FY2011, and FY2012 debtLT differs from FY2011 by only 182k. FY2012 netDebt and netDebtToEbitda are therefore slightly suspect, though the magnitudes are plausible.

FY2009 sharesBasic (10,969,980 split-adjusted) is a weighted average depressed by the October 2009 Florida Public Utilities merger, which issued a large share block late in the year; revenue also jumps 59% into FY2010 for the same reason. FY2009 payout and per-share cross-checks are the least reliable in the window.

priorEstimates (growth5y 9, streak 21, payoutPctFcf 40) were ignored as instructed. The 5-year growth guess happens to land near my computed 9.33, but the streak of 21 cannot be verified: the data window starts at FY2009, so consecutiveIncreasesInData is capped at 16 and windowLimited is true.

The last dpsAllFacts entry (2026-07-01..2026-09-30, val 0, form 10-Q, fp Q1) is a zero-valued placeholder with a mislabelled fiscal period and was excluded. Several other quarterly facts carry wrong fp labels (FY2018 Q1 tagged 'Q2', FY2019 Q1 tagged 'Q3', FY2019 Q2 tagged 'Q3', FY2025 Q3 tagged 'Q1'), so I aligned quarters by start/end dates and duration, never by the fp field.

FY2026 is partially observable (Q1 0.685, Q2 0.735, H1 1.42) but incomplete, so it is excluded from dps and fin. The implied FY2026 declared total is 0.685 + 0.735x3 = 2.89 if the usual raise-in-Q2 pattern holds.

normalised.notes: CPK is a December-FYE gas/electric utility with 17 fiscal years of data (FY2009-FY2025). Regular DPS on today's share basis runs 0.8333 (FY2009) to 2.695 (FY2025), a 7.61%/yr CAGR over 16 years that has ACCELERATED rather than decayed: 9.06%/yr over 10 years, 9.33% over 5, 8.93% over 3. Sixteen consecutive years of increases within the window, no cut, no hold, no special dividend, and no cut in 2020 or 2021 - the apparent FY2020 flat line is an XBRL duplication of the FY2019 value, not a real hold. Two normalisations carry the record: (1) the September 2013 3-for-2 split, adjusted for FY2009-FY2011 ONLY, since FY2012 onward were already filed post-split; (2) FY2020 DPS rebuilt from quarterly rates as 1.725. The financial picture behind the dividend has deteriorated markedly since the FY2023 Florida City Gas acquisition: net debt/EBITDA went from 2.90x (FY2022) to 5.64x (FY2023) and sits at 4.59x; ROIC fell from a 9-10% band in FY2010-FY2017 to 5.83% in FY2025; and FCF is deeply negative (-214.9m in FY2025, a -23.1% FCF margin) on a capex program now 1.9x CFO. Payout on net income is a comfortable 43%, but at the free-cash-flow level the dividend is entirely debt- and equity-funded. Confidence is medium rather than high because FY2013/FY2014 have no second-source declared-dividend fact and because netDebt omits ShortTermBorrowings; the FY2020 override and the split window are themselves well evidenced.

verdicts.summary: All arithmetic reproduced to <0.1%; FY2020 override and split scope confirmed correct; 5 warnings, all documentation/scope wording plus the omitted ShortTermBorrowings in netDebt.
Live price/marketCap/ttmDividend consistent with the record; 1 warning on the sourcing wording of the ttm reconciliation (Q3-2026 rate is inferred, not filed).

rules.name: Small enough to grow
rules.note: Live marketCap 3,114,617,740 at $129.75 (2026-09-17). Comfortably in the ideal band - a ~$3bn utility with a Delmarva/Florida footprint still small enough for acquisitions like Florida City Gas to move the needle.

rules.name: Starting yield in the usable band
rules.note: Latest regular annual DPS 2.695 (FY2025, fully regular: 0.64 + 0.685 x 3) / $129.75 = 2.077%. On the current 0.735 quarterly run-rate ($2.94) it is 2.27%; on live ttmDividend 2.84 it is 2.19%. No specials anywhere in the window, so all three are clean regular yields.

rules.name: Dividend growth above 8%/yr
rules.note: 5-yr DPS CAGR FY2020 1.725 -> FY2025 2.695 = 9.33%/yr. Not decaying: 9.06% over 10 yrs, 8.93% over 3, and the Q2-2026 raise from 0.685 to 0.735 is +7.3% on the quarter. Passes but does not reach the 12% strong bar. Note this rests on the FY2020 override to 1.725; on the erroneous filed 1.585 the g5 would read 11.2% and be wrong.

rules.name: Payout with room left
rules.note: SECTOR EXCEPTION applied: FCF is negative in 11 of 17 years including FY2025 (-$214.9m, -23.1% FCF margin) because rate-base capex of $448.6m is 1.9x CFO of $233.7m, so dividends/FCF is meaningless. Assessed against net income per the rule: $60.7m cash dividends / $140.3m net income = 43.3%, and 45.5% on a declared basis (the cash figure excludes DRIP shares). Inside the 20-60% band with room, but the cash for it comes from debt and equity issuance, not from operations after capex.

rules.name: Streak long enough to prove policy
rules.note: The XBRL data shows 16 consecutive increases FY2010-FY2025 with no cut and no hold, but the window starts at FY2009 so the data streak is window-limited. Prior research streak of 21 is plausible and consistent (the data streak would have to be exactly the window length by coincidence otherwise). Either figure sits inside 10-30.

rules.name: Earnings growing at least as fast as the dividend
rules.note: FCF CAGR is undefined - both endpoints negative (FY2020 -$6.6m, FY2025 -$214.9m) - so net income is used and said so: $71.5m -> $140.3m = 14.43%/yr, comfortably ahead of the 9.33% dividend CAGR. Caveat: a large slice of that earnings growth was bought with the FY2023 Florida City Gas acquisition and funded by the share count rising from 16.7m to 23.4m, so it is partly inorganic and partly diluted.

rules.name: High return on invested capital
rules.note: FY2025 ROIC = operating income 255.9m x (1 - 52.7/193.0) / (equity 1,598.5m + debt 1,596.3m - cash 1.8m) = 5.83%. Structurally below the bar and deteriorating: 9-10% through FY2010-FY2017, 7.2% by FY2021, 4.6% in FY2023, 6.2% FY2024. This is an allowed-return regulated utility, so a 12% ROIC is not achievable by design - but the rule is the rule, and the trend within the utility peer set is the wrong way.

rules.name: Balance sheet not competing with you
rules.note: FY2025 net debt $1,594.5m / EBITDA $347.6m = 4.59x, and this is a FLOOR - the calculation omits ShortTermBorrowings, which the source carries as a full-window series that was never joined in. The step change is recent and acquisition-driven: 2.90x (FY2022) -> 5.64x (FY2023, Florida City Gas) -> 4.44x -> 4.59x. This crosses the >4x threshold that forces an 'avoid' verdict on its own.

rules.name: Why competitors cannot take the business
rules.note: Exclusive, state-regulated distribution franchises in Delaware, Maryland and Florida: the pipes and wires are a legal monopoly with an allowed return, nobody can build a parallel gas main into the same street, and the Delmarva/Florida service territories are among the faster-growing in the US, so customer count grows without any need to win share.

rules.name: Management treats the dividend as a promise
rules.threshold: no cut in FY2020/2021; no cut in window
rules.note: No cut, no suspension and no hold anywhere in the 17-year window; FY2020 rose 1.585 -> 1.725 and FY2021 to 1.88. The apparent FY2020 flat line in the raw filing is an XBRL duplication of the FY2019 fact, refuted by the company's own 9M-2020 YTD declared figure of 1.285. 2008 is outside the XBRL window and cannot be assessed here.

analysis.assessment: CPK is the shape of a good snowball wrapped around a balance sheet that is no longer safe: a $3.1bn regulated gas/electric utility yielding 2.08% on the FY2025 declared DPS of $2.695 (2.27% on the current $2.94 run-rate), compounding the dividend at 9.33%/yr over five years with 16 straight increases in the data and no cut in 2020 or 2021. Payout is 43.3% of net income - genuine room - but that framing flatters it, because free cash flow was -$214.9m in FY2025 on capex of $448.6m against CFO of $233.7m, so every dollar of dividend is currently funded by issuing debt and equity. The Florida City Gas deal took net debt/EBITDA from 2.90x in FY2022 to 5.64x and it still sits at 4.59x - and that figure excludes short-term borrowings, so it is a floor - while ROIC has fallen from a 9-10% band pre-2018 to 5.83%. Share count went from 16.7m (FY2020) to 23.4m (FY2025), a 40% dilution, which is how the 14.4% net income growth was paid for. The thing most likely to break it is not a dividend cut but the funding mix: if rates stay high or a Florida or Delaware rate case comes in short of the allowed return, the capex program gets funded with more equity at a lower price, and the 9%/yr dividend growth has to slow to whatever the regulator lets earnings do.
analysis.moat: Exclusive state-granted gas and electric distribution franchises in fast-growing Delmarva and Florida territories - a legal monopoly on the pipes and wires with an allowed regulated return, where customer growth arrives with population rather than being won from anyone.
strengths: 16 consecutive annual increases in the data (21 on prior research), no cut or hold anywhere in FY2009-FY2025, and no cut through 2020-2021
Dividend growth accelerating rather than decaying: 7.61%/yr over 16 yrs, 9.06% over 10, 9.33% over 5, and a +7.3% raise in Q2-2026
$3.11bn market cap - small enough that each acquisition and each rate base addition materially moves per-share results
Regulated monopoly franchises in Delmarva and Florida, two above-average population-growth service territories
Net income compounding at 14.4%/yr over five years, ahead of the 9.3% dividend CAGR, leaving payout on earnings at a contained 43.3%
risks: Net debt/EBITDA 4.59x against a 2.5x bar - and the figure omits ShortTermBorrowings, so the true leverage is higher
FCF negative in 11 of 17 years and -$214.9m in FY2025; the dividend is entirely debt- and equity-funded at the cash level
ROIC 5.83% versus a 12% bar, down from 9-10% pre-2018 - the Florida City Gas capital has not yet earned its return
Basic share count up 40% from 16.7m (FY2020) to 23.4m (FY2025); growth in aggregate earnings is being diluted per share
Capex at 1.9x CFO leaves the payout hostage to rate-case outcomes and to the cost of equity and debt issued to fund the gap
The whole streak and growth record depends on one judgement call - overriding the filed FY2020 DPS of 1.585 with 1.725; on the filed figure the data streak collapses from 16 to 5
analysis.sectorNote: Rules 4, 7 and 8 are poor fits for a rate-base regulated utility and were read accordingly. Rule 4: FCF is structurally negative because allowed-return capex exceeds CFO by design, so the payout was assessed against net income (43.3%; 45.5% on declared dividends) and this is stated rather than scored as a fail. Rule 7: a regulated utility earns an allowed return of roughly 9-10% on rate base, so 12% ROIC is unreachable by construction - it is still marked fail, but the informative reading is the DECLINE from 9-10% (FY2010-FY2017) to 5.83%, which says the recent acquisition capital is not yet earning. Rule 8: utilities routinely run 4-5x net debt/EBITDA against regulated cash flows, so 4.59x is normal for the sector - but the rule's hard >4x trigger is applied as written, and the leverage is genuinely a step change from CPK's own 2.90x two years ago, not a long-standing posture.

screenFields.streakSource: research; data confirms 16 years (FY2010-FY2025, window-limited at the FY2009 start of XBRL)
screenFields.payoutBasis: net income (regulated utility; FCF -$214.9m in FY2025 so dividends/FCF is not meaningful). 45.5% on declared dividends rather than cash paid.

estimateCorrections.why: Not computable and not 40. FY2025 FCF is -$214.9m (CFO $233.7m less capex $448.6m), and FCF was negative in 11 of the 17 years, so dividends/FCF is undefined. In the two recent positive-FCF years it was 115% (FY2022) and 268% (FY2023) - nowhere near 40%. The screen should show 43.3% on a NET INCOME basis with the basis stated, not a 40% FCF payout.

priorEstimates carried no leverage figure and no flags at all. FY2025 net debt/EBITDA is 4.59x (and that excludes short-term borrowings), up from 2.90x in FY2022 after the Florida City Gas acquisition. This single number is what turns the verdict from candidate to avoid, so its absence from the prior estimates was the material omission.
No prior ROIC estimate existed. Computed 5.83% for FY2025, down from a 9-10% band in FY2010-FY2017 - materially below the 12% screen bar and trending down.

Only 0.33pp off, so not material on its own - recorded for completeness because the prior figure happened to be right for the wrong reason: it matches only once the erroneous filed FY2020 DPS of 1.585 is replaced with the reconstructed 1.725. On the filed data the 5-yr CAGR would read 11.2%.
priorEstimates.flags was empty. Seven flags are now warranted, led by leverage above 4x and a dividend not covered by free cash flow.

stocks.m: State-granted exclusive distribution franchises over 2.2m customers in Oklahoma, Kansas and Texas: the buried pipe network cannot be economically duplicated and the regulator, not a rival, sets the price.

normalised.dpsMethod: Filed annual DPS tag, rule (a): CommonStockDividendsPerShareCashPaid at ~364-365 day duration, FY2012-FY2025 (14 points, form 10-K). Cross-checked every year against the independent quarterly rate facts in dpsAllFacts (which sum exactly to the annual figure from FY2015 on) and against divPaid/sharesBasic. No split adjustment applied anywhere - splitFacts is empty and the ratio (divPaid/sharesBasic)/DPS is 0.993-0.997 in all twelve dividend-paying years, i.e. one single unbroken share basis. FY2014 is the filed CASH-PAID figure of 0.84 = three payments of 0.28 (ONE Gas was spun off from ONEOK on 2014-01-31, so no Q1 2014 cash payment); the DECLARED rate for FY2014 was 0.28/qtr = 1.12 annualised.

specials.note: No special dividends. splitFacts is empty, live.regularDividendIfSpecial is null, and in every dividend-paying year the filed annual DPS is very slightly ABOVE divPaid/weighted-basic-shares (ratio 0.993-0.997), which is the normal share-count-growth artefact for a utility issuing equity through the year - never the large upward gap that flags a special. dpsAllFacts contains only four equal quarterly rates per year with no odd extra payment.

issues: NO SPLIT ADJUSTMENT APPLIED, and this is evidence-based, not an omission: splitFacts is empty, and (divPaid/sharesBasic)/filed DPS is 0.9934 (FY2014), 0.9958, 0.9969, 0.9967, 0.9963, 0.9965, 0.9966, 0.9969, 0.9964, 0.9968, 0.9962, 0.9967 (FY2025) - flat at ~0.996 in all twelve dividend-paying years with no step and no r-shaped kink. sharesBasic rises smoothly 52.3M -> 60.2M with no step change. ONE Gas has never split since its 2014-01-31 spin-off from ONEOK. splitAdjustments is therefore empty; zero fiscal years were adjusted.

FY2014 DPS 0.84 is a PARTIAL YEAR: the spin-off completed 2014-01-31, so only three quarterly payments of 0.28 were made (dpsAllFacts shows CommonStockDividendsPerShareCashPaid = 0 for Q1 2014 while the DECLARED rate was already 0.28). The annualised declared rate for FY2014 was 1.12. I used the filed cash-paid 0.84 per rule (a), which makes FY2014 -> FY2015 look like +42.9% when the true rate increase was 0.28 -> 0.30 (+7.1%), and inflates gMax. gMax of 11.12%/yr should be treated as unusable; g3/g5/g10 are unaffected.

gMax base year: I used FY2014 (0.84, first non-zero) over 11 years. FY2012 and FY2013 filed DPS are a true 0 (pre-spin-off, ONE Gas was a wholly-owned ONEOK subsidiary), so they cannot serve as a CAGR base.

Streak counted as 11 (FY2015 through FY2025, each strictly above the prior year). Judgement call: FY2014's 0.84 is technically > FY2013's 0.00 so a literal reading gives 12, but an increase from a pre-spin-off zero is not a dividend increase, so I excluded it. No cut and no hold anywhere in the window; cut2020 = false (FY2020 2.16 > FY2019 2.00, FY2021 2.32 > 2.16).

EBITDA IS NULL FOR EVERY YEAR, and netDebtToEbitda with it: there is no depreciation/amortisation family in the file at all (families has no da entry and tagHints contains no DepreciationDepletionAndAmortization tag), so opIncome + da is not derivable. Do not read the null as zero leverage - net debt was $2.60bn at FY2025 against $457m of operating income.

FY2021 CFO is -$1,535,657,000 and FY2022 CFO is +$1,570,842,000. These are the Winter Storm Uri gas-cost shock (Feb 2021, ~$2.0bn of purchased gas funded with debt - debtLT jumps 1.58bn -> 3.68bn) and the 2022 securitisation recovery that reversed it. FY2021 FCF of -$2.03bn and FY2022 FCF of +$0.96bn are both non-representative and roughly net out as a pair.

payoutFcf is NULL in 8 of 12 dividend-paying years (2014, 2016, 2017, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2024, 2025) because FCF was negative - per the rule, null when fcf <= 0. This is structural, not a data defect: capex has exceeded CFO in most years, funded by debt and equity issuance. The prior estimate payoutPctFcf = 60 is not supported by the filings; FY2025 FCF is -$128m. Where FCF was positive the ratio is wildly unstable (0.553 in 2015, 1.319 in 2018, 0.139 in 2022, 0.528 in 2023). payoutNi is the meaningful payout measure here and runs 0.52 -> 0.67.
latest.fcfMargin is null: the Revenues tag only covers FY2016-FY2022 (7 points), so there is no FY2025 revenue in the file. Revenue is null for FY2012-FY2015 and FY2023-FY2025.
growth.fcfGrowth5 is null: the FY2020 endpoint FCF is -$106,845,000 (negative), and the FY2025 endpoint is also negative (-$128,393,000), so a CAGR is undefined at both ends.

netDebt and roic are null for FY2012 and FY2013 as a deliberate judgement call. The filed FY2013 debt values are pre-spin-off stubs (debtLT = $1,318,000 and debtCur = $6,000 for a company with $3.85bn of assets), giving a nonsensical net debt of -$1,847,000 and an inflated ROIC of ~10.9% on an invested-capital base with essentially no debt. FY2012 has no debt tags at all. I reported null rather than propagate these. FY2013 sharesOut = 100 is the same artefact (100 shares held by ONEOK); sharesBasic of 52,319,000 for FY2012-FY2013 is the pro-forma spin-off count.

debtCur is absent for FY2017, FY2018, FY2019 and FY2020 and I treated it as 0 in netDebt for those years. issues.detail: A literal application of the stated rule ('consecutive fiscal years, ending at latest, where regular DPS > prior year') over the record's own dps series gives 12, not 11: FY2014's 0.84 is strictly greater than FY2013's 0.00, and the rule text carves out no exception for a zero prior year. The record deviates to 11 on an explicit, disclosed judgement that an increase off a pre-spin-off zero is not a dividend increase. That judgement is economically right and is documented rather than hidden, so this is not a block - but it is a rule deviation, and any consumer applying the rule mechanically will disagree by one year.
