rules.name: Small enough to grow
rules.note: Live marketCap 5,740,087,266 at $169.14 (asOf 2026-09-17). Comfortably under $15B and only 15% above the $5B ideal line; 33.9M shares after buying back a third of the float since 2009.

rules.name: Starting yield in the usable band
rules.note: Forward regular = 4 x $0.40 = $1.60 / $169.14 = 0.95% (FY2025 realised regular $1.56 gives 0.92%). Far below the 1.5% floor. Including the recurring $2.00 December special the total declared yield is $3.56/$169.14 = 2.10%, which would sit in the band, but the special is discretionary and cycle-sensitive so the rule is scored on the regular.

rules.name: Dividend growth above 8%/yr
rules.note: 5-yr regular DPS CAGR FY2020 $0.79 -> FY2025 $1.56. Strong. 3-yr 12.35%, 10-yr 17.92%, 17-yr 14.55%. Each quarterly step (0.21 -> 0.25 -> 0.30 -> 0.33 -> 0.36 -> 0.40) is independently filed and the live 0.40 rate confirms the endpoint.

rules.name: Payout with room left
rules.note: FY2025 total declared dividends $122.2M / FCF $215.0M = 56.9%, inside the band but only because a trough-year FCF is carrying a $2.00 special. The regular dividend alone costs $54.2M = 25.2% of FCF and 47.1% of trough net income. On the declared basis payout of net income is 106%, which is the flag: the special, not the regular, is what has no room.

rules.name: Streak long enough to prove policy
rules.note: Data streak of 11 consecutive regular increases, NOT window-limited (it starts FY2015, seven years inside the FY2008 data edge), so the data streak is used and priorEstimates.streak of 15 is not. The run is broken at FY2014 only by the filed FY2013 declaration of $0.35 vs $0.26 in FY2014; the underlying quarterly rate never fell, so the true policy streak is probably longer, but 11 is what the filings support.

rules.name: Earnings growing at least as fast as the dividend
rules.note: FCF $180.1M (FY2020) -> $215.0M (FY2025) = 3.61%/yr, 11 points behind the dividend. Net income is worse: $192.1M -> $115.0M, a negative CAGR. Both endpoints are positive so FCF is used as specified. FY2025 is a freight-recession trough (EBITDA $198.0M vs $628.5M in FY2022), so this is cycle position more than secular decay, but the dividend has been compounding off a shrinking earnings base for three years.

rules.name: High return on invested capital
rules.note: FY2025 ROIC 29.02% at the bottom of the cycle, against 79.2% at the FY2022 peak and a 17-year range of 25-79%. Asset-light: FY2025 capex $9.9M on $4.74B of revenue. Strong on any reading.

rules.name: Balance sheet not competing with you
rules.note: Net cash in every year since FY2013; passes outright. Caveat from the source data: LongTermDebt is tagged 0 from FY2014 on while lease-repayment tags keep running, so finance-lease obligations sit outside the captured debt family - this is an upper bound on net cash, not a point estimate. Even a generous lease add-back leaves the company nowhere near 2.5x.

rules.name: Why competitors cannot take the business
rules.note: Landstar does not own trucks or employ salespeople: ~1,000 independent commission agents own the shipper relationships and ~8-10k owner-operator BCOs haul the freight, both tied in by variable-cost economics that let Landstar stay profitable through troughs (FY2025 still 29% ROIC on a -41% earnings year). A new entrant has to recruit both sides at once. It is a real mechanism, though weaker than it was: digital brokers compete on the same price-per-load and the agent model is not legally exclusive.

rules.name: Management treats the dividend as a promise
rules.threshold: no cut in FY2020/FY2021; no cut in window
rules.value: no cut; FY2014 step is a timing artifact
rules.note: FY2019 $0.70 -> FY2020 $0.79 -> FY2021 $0.92 regular DPS, raised straight through COVID with the $2.00 special intact. The one apparent cut in the window (FY2013 $0.35 -> FY2014 $0.26) is a declaration-timing artifact of the December-2012 tax acceleration: the filed quarterly regular rate series is strictly monotonic from $0.04 to $0.40 with no reduction anywhere. FY2008 is outside the XBRL window, so the 2008-09 recession cannot be tested from the data.

analysis.assessment: Landstar passes 8 of 10 rules on the mechanical rubric, but the two it fails are the two that define the snowball: at $169.14 the regular dividend of $1.60 (4 x $0.40) yields 0.95%, less than two-thirds of the 1.5% floor, and 5-yr FCF growth of 3.6% is eleven points behind 14.6% dividend growth. What you are buying is the compounding, not the income - 14.6% five-year regular DPS growth off a regular payout of just 25% of FCF and 47% of trough net income, funded by a business earning 29% ROIC at the bottom of a freight recession with $396.7M of net cash and $9.9M of annual capex. The recurring $2.00 December special triples the cash yield to 2.10% but is explicitly discretionary: it consumed $68M of a $115M net income year, which is why total declared dividends were 106% of FY2025 earnings. The thing most likely to break it is the cycle, not the balance sheet - EBITDA has fallen from $628.5M (FY2022) to $198.0M (FY2025) and revenue is still declining, so another leg down forces a choice between the special and the buyback long before the regular is ever at risk. At a 0.95% starting yield you need roughly eight years of 14.6% growth just to reach a 3% yield on cost, which is a long wait for a business whose earnings have compounded at zero over the last five.
analysis.moat: Asset-light freight brokerage run through a network of ~1,000 independent commission agents who own the shipper relationships and ~9,000 owner-operator BCOs who haul the freight - a two-sided network on fully variable costs that a new entrant must recruit from both ends at once.
strengths: 29.0% ROIC at a cyclical trough (79.2% at the FY2022 peak) on $9.9M of FY2025 capex - the growth is nearly free
Net cash of $396.7M (-2.0x EBITDA), net cash in every year since FY2013
Regular dividend costs only $54.2M against $215.0M of trough FCF (25.2%), leaving several doublings of runway
14.58% 5-yr regular DPS CAGR with every quarterly step independently filed and the current $0.40 rate confirmed into Q1-2026
Raised straight through COVID (0.70 -> 0.79 -> 0.92) and through the 2023-25 freight recession, keeping the $2.00 special intact
risks: 0.95% forward regular yield - the income is almost irrelevant for a decade
5-yr FCF CAGR 3.6% and 5-yr net income CAGR negative: the dividend is outgrowing the business
FY2025 total declared dividends were 106% of net income; the $2.00 special is the discretionary piece and a further cycle leg down puts it, not the regular, at risk
Freight brokerage is structurally price-competitive and digital brokers attack the same spread; agent relationships are not exclusive
Revenue -1.6% and EBITDA down 69% from the FY2022 peak with no confirmed trough yet
analysis.sectorNote: Standard industrial rules fit an asset-light broker well - FCF is close to net income and capex is trivial - so no sector adjustment was needed for rules 4, 7 or 8. The one model-specific adjustment is the special dividend: rules 2 and 4 are scored on the REGULAR dividend (rule 2) and on total declared dividends (rule 4) with the regular-only figure given alongside, because Landstar's $2.00 December special has been paid every year since FY2019 but is formally discretionary and is what pushes declared payout of net income to 106%. Net debt/EBITDA is a lower bound on leverage: finance-lease obligations fall outside the tagged debt family from FY2014 on.

estimateCorrections.why: Filed data gives a 5-yr regular DPS CAGR of 14.58% (FY2020 $0.79 -> FY2025 $1.56), 4.6pp above the prior 10% estimate. Every quarterly step is an independent filed fact and the live $0.40 rate confirms the endpoint.

The in-data streak of consecutive regular increases is 11 (FY2015-FY2025) and is NOT window-limited, so the prior 15 cannot be preferred. 15 matches neither the filed reading (11, broken by the filed FY2013 $0.35 against FY2014 $0.26) nor the alternative run-rate reading (17). The FY2014 break is very likely a declaration-timing artifact, so 11 is conservative.

Prior 30% was roughly the regular-only figure (actual 25.2%). On total declared dividends including the recurring $2.00 special, FY2025 payout is $122.2M / $215.0M FCF = 56.9%, 27pp higher - and 106% of net income. The screen should show the declared-basis figure with the regular-only figure noted, or it understates how much of the cash return is discretionary.

The screen should use the current run-rate regular of $1.60 (4 x $0.40, confirmed by the Q1-2026 declaration and live regularDividendIfSpecial) rather than the FY2025 realised $1.56, which is depressed by Q1-2025 still being at $0.36. Using $1.56 understates the yield by 2.6%.

Every year cross-checked against divPaid / weighted basic shares; all 18 years agree within 0.5%.

No filed DPS sits materially ABOVE the cash-derived figure anywhere, and no separate special-dividend fact appears in dpsAllFacts. live.regularDividendIfSpecial is null, consistent. The FY2013->FY2014 jump (0.56 -> 0.84, +50%) is a genuine regular-rate increase, not a special: the quarterly declared facts step 0.13 -> 0.20 in Sep-2013 and the cash-paid tag independently confirms 0.84, with divPaid/shares = 0.8396.

Low risk - the two tags overlap in FY2013 (both 0.56) and FY2014 (both 0.84), and declared-vs-paid timing creates no level break for this filer because the rate steps once a year in fiscal Q1.

SPLITS - no adjustment made to any year, deliberately. splitFacts is empty; divPaid/sharesBasic reproduces the filed DPS within 0.5% in ALL 18 years (FY2009 0.3198 vs 0.32 ... FY2026 2.3711 vs 2.38), so every year is already on one consistent share basis. sharesBasic drifts smoothly from 84.1m (FY2009) to 71.9m (FY2026) on buybacks with no step-change anywhere. JKHY's last 2:1 split predates this data window. splitAdjustments is empty and no fiscal year was divided or multiplied.

Cross-check disagreements, worst two: FY2021 divPaid/shares = 1.7711 vs filed 1.78 (-0.50%) and FY2026 = 2.3711 vs filed 2.38 (-0.37%). Both are the heaviest buyback years (431.5m and 448.2m), so weighted average shares exceed the count on register at later record dates. Timing, not a special. The other 16 years are all inside 0.2%.

FCF understates reinvestment. The capex family carries only PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment (67.1m in FY2026). JKHY separately capitalises software: tagHints shows PaymentsToDevelopSoftware at 184.2m in FY2026 (18 points, full history) plus PaymentsToAcquireSoftware 4.1m. Per the stated rule those were NOT deducted. Including them, FY2026 FCF would be roughly 510.5m and payoutFcf roughly 0.334 instead of 0.245. Treat every payoutFcf here as a floor.

Revenue is null for FY2019-FY2026: the table only joins the Revenues tag (ends FY2018). The RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax series (FY2017-FY2026) is listed in families.revenue candidates but no values were supplied. Consequently latest.fcfMargin is null - not derivable.

netDebt and netDebtToEbitda null for FY2022-FY2026: the table carries no cash for those years (the cash family switches to CashCashEquivalentsRestrictedCashAndRestrictedCashEquivalents, values not supplied) and no debtLT for FY2024-FY2026. This includes the latest year, so current leverage could not be measured at all. FY2009 and FY2010 are also null - no debt tags in the table for those years, and assuming zero was rejected since FY2011 shows 127.9m of LT debt.

netDebt for FY2018-FY2021 assumes debtCur = 0 (judgement call): debtLT is present (0 / 0 / 0.208m / 100.083m) but no current-debt tag is reported after FY2017. The DebtCurrent family genuinely stops at FY2017, so the error is likely nil to small.

ROIC for FY2022-FY2026 rests on an incomplete invested-capital base: cash missing for all five years, debt missing for FY2024-FY2026, so the denominator is effectively equity (plus debtLT where available). Not netting cash biases these ROICs slightly LOW; missing debt biases them slightly high. Reported rather than nulled because equity dominates the base (2.05bn in FY2026), but FY2022-FY2026 ROIC is approximate.

FY2018 effective tax computes to -2.49% (tax = -8.876m on pretax 356.158m, the TCJA remeasurement benefit). Per the stated rule the actual ratio was used, which inflates FY2018 ROIC to 28.4% - the highest in the series and not comparable. At 21% it would be about 21.9%. FY2018 payoutNi (0.2877) is likewise flattered by the one-off benefit inside net income (365.0m, vs 271.9m the next year).

Effective tax falls back to 21% for FY2022-FY2026: the pretax family switches tags at FY2020 and the table carries no pretax value from FY2022 on. Actual FY2019-FY2021 rates were 21.7-22.2%, so the fallback is close.

EBITDA = opIncome + Depreciation only. The da family is the Depreciation tag, which excludes amortisation of intangibles and of capitalised software; CapitalizedContractCostAmortization (195.7m FY2026) and CapitalizedComputerSoftwareAmortization are tagged separately and were not added. EBITDA here is therefore not a full D&A add-back. Interest expense also stops after FY2023.

Streak is window-limited: regular DPS rises in every year of the data - FY2010 through FY2026 is 17 consecutive increases, with FY2009 the first observable year. No cut and no hold anywhere, including FY2020 and FY2021. JKHY's real increase streak is generally held to start well before FY2009, so 17 is a floor. priorEstimates.streak of 35 is not verifiable from this data and was not used.

priorEstimates rejected as instructed: growth5y guessed 7 (actual 5-yr DPS CAGR 5.98%), payoutPctFcf guessed 40 (actual 24.5% on PP&E-only capex, about 33% including capitalised software), streak guessed 35 (17 verifiable).

normalised.notes: JKHY, June FYE, 18 fiscal years FY2009-FY2026. No splits and no specials in the window - an unusually clean series. Regular DPS comes straight from filed annual facts (declared tag FY2013+, cash-paid tag FY2009-FY2012) and the divPaid/sharesBasic cross-check agrees within 0.5% in every single year, which is itself the proof that no year sits on a stale share basis; splitAdjustments is empty by evidence, not by omission. Dividend cadence is metronomic: +12 cents a year for the last five years, giving 5.98% 5-yr and 5.62% 3-yr CAGR, decelerating from 8.42% over 10 years as the fixed-cent increment shrinks in percentage terms. Coverage is strong and improving - FY2026 payout is 34% of net income and 25% of PP&E-only FCF, though the honest figure adds the 184m of capitalised software development, lifting FCF payout to roughly one third. FY2026 was a step-change year for cash generation (CFO 762m, +19%) alongside a 448m buyback. The main gaps are in the supplied extract rather than the filings: no revenue after FY2018 and no cash balance after FY2021, which null out fcfMargin and every recent leverage metric.

issues.detail: latest.payoutFcf = 0.2452 is computed on a capex base of PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment only (67.1m in FY2026). JKHY's dominant reinvestment line is capitalised software development — PaymentsToDevelopSoftware 184.2m plus PaymentsToAcquireSoftware 4.1m in FY2026 — which for a bank-core software vendor is real, recurring, non-discretionary spend, not an acquisition. issues.detail: Effective tax falls back to 21% for FY2022-FY2026 because the pretax family switches tags at FY2020 and no pretax value is in the table from FY2022. The rule's 21% fallback was applied correctly, but tax expense IS present in all five years and net income + tax gives a defensible pretax proxy implying 22.2-23.3% effective rates, so these five ROICs are each biased about 2-3% high on the tax factor alone.

The FY2022-FY2026 invested-capital denominators omit cash entirely (cash tag stops FY2021) and omit debt for FY2024-FY2026 (debtLT stops FY2023 in the supplied table, though the families.debtLT candidate list shows LongTermDebt has 12 points running to 2026-06-30 - the values simply were not supplied). So the denominator is equity, or equity+debtLT, not the rule's equity+debtLT+debtCur-cash. Two offsetting biases, magnitude unknown. The record discloses this.
issues.suggested: Either null these five ROICs or label them approximate in the field itself, not only in dataQuality; if the extract can be re-pulled, LongTermDebt and CashCashEquivalentsRestrictedCashAndRestrictedCashEquivalents both run to FY2026 and would close the gap.

issues.detail: FY2018 uses the actual effective tax of -2.49% (tax -8.876m on pretax 356.158m, the TCJA remeasurement benefit), producing ROIC 0.2837 - the series high - and payoutNi 0.2877 on net income of 365.034m that falls to 271.885m the next year. Rule-compliant and disclosed, but FY2018 is not comparable to any adjacent year and will distort any max/mean of the ROIC series.
issues.suggested: At a normalised 21% rate FY2018 ROIC is about 0.2187. Recommend excluding FY2018 from any ROIC max/trend read.

issues.detail: Inconsistent missing-data convention. FY2009 and FY2010 have cash (118.251m / 125.518m) but no debt tag, and the record returns null, explicitly refusing to assume zero debt. FY2018-FY2021 have debtLT but no debtCur, and the record DOES assume debtCur = 0, producing signed netDebt values. Both choices are individually defensible and both are disclosed, but the same record applies opposite rules to the same kind of gap.
issues.suggested: State one convention. If assuming zero for a genuinely discontinued tag family is acceptable (DebtCurrent ends FY2017), the same logic supports FY2009/FY2010 netDebt of -118,251k and -125,518k; otherwise null FY2018-FY2021 as well.

issues.detail: Narrative inaccuracy, numbers unaffected. The note says the FY2013->FY2014 step is visible because 'the quarterly declared facts step 0.13 -> 0.20 in Sep-2013'. The Sep-2013 0.20 fact is tagged CommonStockDividendsPerShareCashPaid, not Declared (the Declared tag has no quarterly facts before Sep-2014), and the 0.20 rate already appears inside FY2013 - FY2013's quarters are 0.115/0.115/0.13/0.20 summing to 0.56, so the rate rose in the Apr-Jun 2013 quarter and FY2014's +50% is the full-year effect of a step that began in FY2013 Q4.
issues.suggested: Reword to: 'the quarterly cash-paid facts step 0.13 -> 0.20 in the Apr-Jun 2013 quarter, so FY2014 carries a full year at the higher rate'. The conclusion (regular increase, not a special) stands.

issues.detail: gMax of 12.528% is arithmetically correct over 17 CAGR years but is dominated by the single FY2013->FY2014 +50% step; it is not a usable long-run growth rate for this filer, whose current cadence is a fixed +12 cents (5.62% 3-yr, 5.98% 5-yr and decelerating as the fixed increment shrinks in percentage terms). The record already says this in dataQuality, but gMax sits unqualified in the growth object.
issues.suggested: No numeric change; ensure downstream consumers weight g3/g5 over gMax for JKHY.

rules.name: Small enough to grow
rules.note: live marketCap 11,295,656,184 at $158.98 (2026-09-17). Passes the <$15B bar but is mid-cap, not the ideal sub-$5B size, so size no longer contributes much to growth.

rules.name: Starting yield in band
rules.note: FY2026 filed regular DPS 2.38 / 158.98 = 1.497% - literally on the line. On the current declared rate (0.61/qtr from FY2026 Q3, TTM 2.41, forward 2.44) the yield is 1.52-1.53%, so the band is cleared on a current-rate basis. There is no margin here: a 2% rally puts JKHY out of the band.

rules.name: Dividend growth above 8%/yr
rules.note: 2.38 vs 1.78 five years ago. The cadence is a fixed +12 cents a year (1.90/2.02/2.14/2.26/2.38), so the percentage rate mechanically decays: 10-yr 8.42%, 5-yr 5.98%, 3-yr 5.62%. gMax of 12.53% is an artifact of the one-off +50% FY2014 step and should not be used. This is the clearest failure in the screen.

rules.name: Payout with room left
rules.note: 170.4m dividends / 694.9m FCF (CFO 762.0m less PP&E capex 67.1m) = 24.5%. JKHY capitalises software development separately - PaymentsToDevelopSoftware 184.2m plus PaymentsToAcquireSoftware 4.1m in FY2026 - which is real recurring reinvestment for a core-banking vendor; including it, FCF is ~506.5m and payout ~33.6%. Both readings sit inside the band; treat 24.5% as a floor and 33.6% as the honest number. Payout on net income is 33.9%.

rules.name: Streak long enough to prove policy, short enough to still be fast
rules.note: The XBRL window starts FY2009 and DPS rises in every observable year (FY2010-FY2026 = 17 consecutive increases), so the data streak is window-limited and 17 is a floor. Prior research puts the real streak at ~35 years, which is plausible for this filer and is the figure used. At 35 years JKHY sits past the upper bound - a mature, fully-established policy, which is exactly why the growth rate has decayed to the mid-single digits. On the 17-year data streak alone it would pass; the honest, longer figure does not.

rules.name: Earnings growing at least as fast as the dividend
rules.note: FCF 439.1m (FY2021) -> 694.9m (FY2026). Cash generation is outgrowing the payout by ~3.6pp a year, and FY2026 was a step-change year (CFO +19% to 762.0m). Net income grew faster still, 311.5m -> 502.8m (10.05%/yr). The dividend is being under-served relative to earnings power, which is why payout has fallen from 30.5% to 24.5% of FCF over the period.

rules.name: High return on invested capital
rules.note: FY2026 operating income 635.0m x (1-21% fallback tax) / invested capital 2,051.9m = 24.45%. Using tax/(NI+tax) instead of the 21% fallback gives 23.8%. The denominator is incomplete for FY2022-FY2026 (no cash balance after FY2021, no debt tag after FY2023), so this is approximate - but the series runs 19-27% for eighteen straight years, so the conclusion is not close to the threshold. FY2018's 28.4% is a TCJA tax artifact and should be ignored.

rules.name: Balance sheet not competing with you
rules.note: Not assessable: the extract carries no cash balance after FY2021 and no debt tag after FY2023, so FY2022-FY2026 net debt is null. Every measurable year is either net cash or trivially levered - FY2012-FY2020 all net cash (as low as -0.49x), FY2021 +0.11x, FY2011 0.35x. Nothing in the record suggests leverage has become an issue, but it could not be verified for the latest year and is marked null rather than assumed.

rules.name: Why competitors cannot take the business
rules.note: JKHY runs the core deposit/loan ledger for ~7,500 community banks and credit unions. Ripping out a core is a multi-year, board-level project that touches every branch, teller and regulatory report, so contracts renew at very high rates and pricing is negotiated, not bid. The moat sentence is kept as written - the data supports it: 24.5% ROIC sustained across eighteen years and a 45% EBITDA margin are what durable switching costs look like.

rules.name: Management treats the dividend as a promise
rules.threshold: no cut in FY2020/2021; any cut in window fails
rules.note: FY2020 1.66 > FY2019 1.54 and FY2021 1.78 > 1.66 - raised straight through COVID. No cut and no hold anywhere in FY2009-FY2026. 2008 is outside the XBRL window and cannot be checked from this data.

analysis.assessment: JKHY is a high-quality compounder that has grown out of the growth half of this screen. The snowball starts at a 1.50% yield (2.38 on a $158.98 price; 1.52% on the current 0.61 quarterly rate) and compounds at 5.98% - a fixed +12 cents a year that gets slower in percentage terms every single year, from 8.42% over ten years to 5.62% over three. What is not in doubt is the safety: 24.5% of PP&E-only FCF, ~33.6% once the 184m of capitalised software development is deducted, 33.9% of net income, 24.5% ROIC sustained across eighteen years, and no cut or hold since at least FY2009 including straight through COVID. FY2026 was the strongest cash year in the series - CFO 762.0m, +19% - and FCF has compounded at 9.61% against the dividend's 5.98%, so there is genuine room to accelerate the raise if management chose to. The thing most likely to break the snowball is not the balance sheet but the cadence itself: at a fixed 12-cent increment the growth rate falls below 5% within four years, and a 1.5% starting yield gives no cushion for that - the thesis needs Jack Henry to convert its widening coverage into a percentage-based raise, or the total return depends entirely on the multiple.
analysis.moat: Core banking software for community banks; replacing it takes years.
strengths: Coverage is wide and widening: 24.5% of FCF (33.6% including capitalised software), 33.9% of net income, down from 30.5%/43.0% of FCF earlier in the decade
FCF compounding at 9.61% vs a 5.98% dividend - earnings are outrunning the payout by 3.6pp a year
ROIC 19-27% every year for eighteen years, 24.5% in FY2026, on a capital-light recurring-revenue model
Eighteen years without a cut or a hold, including raises through FY2020 and FY2021
Balance sheet effectively unlevered in every year it can be measured; net cash in nine of them
Share count down 84.1m to 71.9m with no dilution events, so per-share dividend growth is supported by buybacks as well as earnings
risks: 5-yr DPS CAGR of 5.98% is 2pp below the screen's bar and decaying by construction - a fixed 12-cent increment on a rising base
Starting yield of 1.497% is exactly on the 1.5% line; the entry is only defensible at or below today's price
Headline FCF payout of 24.5% excludes 188m of software capex; the real figure is ~33.6% and peer comparisons on a PP&E-only basis flatter JKHY by roughly a third
Latest-year leverage is unverifiable - no cash balance after FY2021, no debt tag after FY2023 - so rule 8 is unscored, not passed
At ~35 years the dividend policy is mature; the historical pattern for such filers is further deceleration, not reacceleration
Core-banking conversions are slow in both directions: the moat that protects the installed base also caps the rate at which JKHY can take share from FIS and Fiserv
analysis.sectorNote: No sector adjustment needed - JKHY is an ordinary corporate, not a REIT, insurer or regulated utility, so FCF = CFO - capex applies as written. The one model-specific adjustment that matters is the capex definition: a core-banking software vendor capitalises development spend (PaymentsToDevelopSoftware 184.2m in FY2026) outside PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment, so rule 4 is reported both ways - 24.5% on the rule's literal capex family and 33.6% on the economically honest one. Rule 8 is marked null for data reasons, not sector reasons.

normalised.dpsMethod: Filed annual CommonStockDividendsPerShareDeclared (~364-365 day duration, fp=FY) used for FY2009, FY2010, FY2011, FY2012, FY2013, FY2022, FY2023, FY2024, FY2025. FY2014-FY2019 have no annual or quarterly DPS fact and are derived as PaymentsOfDividendsCommonStock / WeightedAverageNumberOfSharesOutstandingBasic (basis 'derived-from-cash'). FY2020 and FY2021 use DividendsCommonStock (DECLARED dollars, common-only) / sharesBasic: FY2020 = 126,468,000/51,838,219 = 2.4397 and FY2021 = 177,051,000/66,802,242 = 2.6504 (basis 'derived-from-declared'). The filed FY2021 fact of 2.4056 was REJECTED - see dataQuality. NO SPLIT ADJUSTMENT: splitFacts is empty, sharesBasic rises monotonically 9.16M -> 110.72M with no step, and divPaid/sharesBasic reconciles to filed DPS on one consistent basis in FY2010 (2.0036 vs 2.04), FY2012 (1.5955 vs 1.60), FY2022 (2.8007 vs 2.805) and FY2025 (3.0766 vs 3.081). The FY2010->FY2011 drop 2.04 -> 1.60 is a genuine CUT (quarterly declared facts 0.51/qtr in 2010 -> 0.40/qtr in 2011-2012), not a 0.784 share-basis change.

specials.note: No special dividend. Justified only from facts in the file: (1) for every year where quarterly declared facts exist alongside the filed annual figure, the annual equals the sum of its own quarters - FY2023 0.72+0.729+0.729+implied 0.741 = 2.919, FY2024 0.741+0.75+0.75+implied 0.759 = 3.000, FY2025 0.759+0.768+0.768+implied 0.786 = 3.081, and each implied Q4 equals the NEXT year's filed Q1 exactly (0.741 = 2024 Q1, 0.759 = 2025 Q1, 0.786 = 2026 Q1), a three-times-confirmed ladder with no lump anywhere; (2) no year shows filed DPS materially ABOVE divPaid/sharesBasic, which is the signature of a special - the only large gaps run the other way (FY2021 and FY2011); (3) splitFacts is empty and live.regularDividendIfSpecial is null. The 91-day 0.262 (2025-10-01/12-31) and 30-day 0.253 (2024-12) facts are MONTHLY rates mis-scoped onto quarter/month windows (0.786/3 and 0.759/3) and were correctly not summed.

rules.name: Why competitors cannot take the business
rules.value: Long-dated triple-net leases to investment-grade tenants
rules.note: The in-place portfolio is genuinely protected: rent is contractual for the remaining lease term with escalators and tenant-borne taxes, insurance and maintenance, and a tenant cannot switch landlords without moving its store. The mechanism protects existing cash flow, not future growth - new acquisitions are won on cap rate and cost of capital, which is a price competition.

rules.name: Management treats the dividend as a promise
rules.threshold: no cut/suspension anywhere in the window
rules.note: FY2020 (2.4397) and FY2021 (2.6504) both rose, so the pandemic test was passed. But the rule fails on any cut in the window: FY2011 is a verified -21.6% cut after the Borders Group tenant bankruptcy, corroborated by quarterly declared facts falling 0.51/qtr to 0.40/qtr with no share-count step (not a split). 2008 is outside the XBRL window and cannot be checked.

analysis.assessment: ADC yields 4.62% on the $3.163 TTM monthly run-rate at $68.50, which is above the 4.0% band ceiling, and grows that dividend at roughly 4.8-5.6%/yr over five years and only 3.18%/yr over the last three fully filed years - a ~8% total-return snowball that decelerates rather than compounds. Coverage is adequate but not roomy: on the REIT-appropriate basis, dividends took 67.6% of FY2025 CFO ($340.7M of $504.1M), up from 60.8% in FY2022, so the payout ratio has been drifting the wrong way even as CFO grew 28.7%/yr. The growth is bought, not earned - shares outstanding went 51.8M to 110.7M in five years and acquisition spend was $1.44B in FY2025 against $504M of CFO, which means the dividend's growth depends on continuous access to equity at a price above NAV and debt below cap rates. ROIC never exceeds 4.89% in any observable year and net debt/EBITDA was 5.77x at its last measurable reading (FY2021, now unobservable), so there is no internal engine and no balance-sheet cushion. The thing most likely to break it is a sustained period where the share price sits below the level at which issuing equity is accretive: the ATM shuts, acquisitions stop, and a dividend already at two-thirds of CFO has nothing behind it - exactly the mechanism that produced the -21.6% cut in FY2011.

rules.name: Small enough to grow
rules.note: Live marketCap 1,062,329,885 at $164.37 (2026-09-17). Micro/small-cap, deep inside the ideal band; ~6.5M shares outstanding after a 37% reduction from 10.6M in FY2009.

rules.name: Starting yield in the usable band
rules.note: Regular annual DPS on the current basis is 2.28 (4 x the 0.57 quarterly rate); 2.28/164.37 = 1.39%. On the filed FY2025 DPS of 2.04 the yield is 1.24%. No special dividends, so this is a clean regular yield. Misses the 1.5% floor by 11bp - the entry yield is the weak link, because management routes far more cash to buybacks (47.1M in FY2025) than to dividends (13.8M).

rules.name: Dividend growth above 8%/yr
rules.note: 5-yr DPS CAGR FY2020 0.95 -> FY2025 2.04 = 16.51%; 3-yr is 16.51% and the FY2017-FY2025 rate off the first full year is 16.77%. Strong band. If the disputed FY2022 quarterly reading (1.34) were used instead of the filed 1.29, the 3-yr CAGR would be 14.98% - still strong. Nine straight Q4 raises, and the 0.49 -> 0.57 raise (+16.3%) already declared keeps the pace.

rules.name: Payout with room left
rules.note: FY2025 dividends 13.831M / FCF 18.556M = 74.5%, above the 60% ceiling. This is a cash-conversion artefact, not a payout decision: FY2025 CFO collapsed to 22.4M against 54.8M of net income on working-capital/bonus timing. On net income the payout is 25.3%, and on 3-yr average FCF ((57.7+33.1+18.6)/3 = 36.5M) it is 37.9% - both comfortably inside the band. Marked fail on the literal rule; the honest read is that the structural payout is ~25-38% with real room.

rules.name: Streak long enough to prove policy
rules.note: Nine consecutive increases, FY2017 through FY2025, off a dividend initiated in fiscal 2016 at 0.14/quarter. NOT window-limited: the XBRL window starts FY2009 and strictly contains the initiation year, so the prior research estimate of 10 cannot be layered on - the tenth increase does not exist yet. The already-declared 0.57 rate makes FY2026 the tenth, so this rule flips to pass within a year. Fails now on a technicality, but for the good reason that the policy is young rather than broken.

rules.name: Earnings growing at least as fast as the dividend
rules.note: On the literal FCF test this fails badly: FCF went 37.569M (FY2020) -> 18.556M (FY2025) = -13.16%/yr. But FCF is plainly erratic here (73.1M in FY2021, 21.3M in FY2022, 57.7M in FY2023, 18.6M in FY2025) on a business with no real capital intensity, so per the rule's carve-out I used net income: 24.507M -> 54.782M = 17.45%/yr, just ahead of the 16.51% dividend CAGR. Revenue 508.4M -> 751.6M and EBITDA 47.6M -> 97.3M corroborate. Pass on net income, stated as such.

rules.name: High return on invested capital
rules.note: FY2025 NOPAT 83.124M x (1 - 28.46%) = 59.5M over equity 213.6M less cash 18.2M = 30.4%. Debt is absent from the source, so the denominator omits borrowings and this is a ceiling; FY2025 interest of 4.659M at a ~6% cost implies roughly 75-80M of debt, which puts the true figure near 22%. Either number clears the 15% strong bar comfortably, and the five-year trend (15.5% -> 30.6% -> 24.3% -> 25.4% -> 26.9% -> 30.4%) is consistent. An asset-light consultancy whose capital is people, so high ROIC is structurally expected.

rules.name: Balance sheet not competing with you
rules.note: Not assessable: the source has no debt family at all (no DebtCurrent, LongTermDebt, LongTermDebtNoncurrent or LineOfCredit), so netDebt is null for all 17 years and zero was correctly not substituted. Indirect bounding: interest of 4.659M implies ~75-80M drawn, against cash of 18.2M and EBITDA of 97.3M, so indicative net debt/EBITDA is roughly 0.6x - well clear of 2.5x. Treated as null rather than a pass because the figure is inferred, not filed.

rules.name: Why competitors cannot take the business
rules.note: CRAI sells the testimony and reports of named PhD economists whose credibility has been accepted by courts, antitrust agencies and regulators; law firms retain the individual expert and the case team around them, and a challenger cannot manufacture a Daubert-survivable track record or the conflict-cleared roster that follows from it. Pricing is on billable rates that rise with that reputation, not bid down - revenue grew 324.8M -> 751.6M (FY2016-FY2025) while headcount economics held. The honest weakness is that the franchise walks out of the door in people's heads: expert teams do defect, which is the real competitive risk rather than price.

rules.name: Management treats the dividend as a promise
rules.note: Through COVID the dividend rose 14.5% in FY2020 and 14.7% in FY2021, with no hold or suspension anywhere in the FY2016-FY2025 data. 2008 is outside the XBRL window and, more to the point, CRAI paid no dividend at all before fiscal 2016, so there is no earlier cut to find. Buybacks are treated as the flexible lever and the dividend as the fixed one, which is the right ordering.

analysis.assessment: CRAI is a $1.06B consultancy compounding the dividend at 16.5%/yr off a nine-year streak, but the snowball starts cold: 2.28 annualised on a $164.37 price is a 1.39% yield, below the usable floor, because management spends roughly 3.4x more on buybacks (47.1M in FY2025) than on dividends (13.8M). The runway is genuinely long - 25.3% of net income and ~38% of three-year average FCF - so the headline 74.5% FY2025 FCF payout is a cash-conversion artefact of a 22.4M CFO against 54.8M of net income, not a stretched policy. Earnings are keeping up (net income 17.45%/yr vs DPS 16.51%/yr, revenue 508M -> 752M over five years) on a 30.4% reported ROIC that is closer to ~22% once the ~75-80M of inferred borrowings are added back, and leverage looks near 0.6x EBITDA although no debt is actually filed. At this yield you are buying growth, not income: a 15-year hold at mid-teens growth gets you to a 10-12% yield on cost, and nothing gets there faster. The thing most likely to break it is the revenue engine, not the balance sheet - billings track antitrust, litigation and regulatory activity, so a quiet enforcement cycle or the defection of a few senior expert teams hits revenue and the bonus-heavy cost base at once, and CFO has already shown it can halve in a year.
analysis.moat: CRA sells named PhD economists whose testimony courts and antitrust agencies have already accepted - a Daubert-survivable, conflict-cleared expert roster that a competitor cannot assemble on demand, which is why the work is retained at rising rates rather than bid on price.
strengths: 16.51% 5-yr DPS CAGR with nine straight Q4 raises and a tenth (0.49 -> 0.57, +16.3%) already declared.
Payout is genuinely low on the durable denominators: 25.3% of net income, ~37.9% of 3-yr average FCF.
ROIC of 30.4% reported / ~22% debt-adjusted on an asset-light people business; capex is 0.5-2.4% of revenue in most years.
Net income compounding at 17.45%/yr, slightly ahead of the dividend, with revenue 324.8M -> 751.6M since FY2016.
Aggressive buyback shrinking the share count 10.6M -> 6.5M, which mechanically amplifies per-share dividend growth.
Dividend raised straight through FY2020 and FY2021 with no hold or cut anywhere in the window.
risks: 1.39% entry yield fails the usable band; the snowball needs ~5 more years of mid-teens growth just to reach a 2.5% yield on cost.

Cash conversion is erratic - CFO was 22.4M against 54.8M of net income in FY2025 and 25.1M against 43.6M in FY2022; a third weak year would make the FCF payout structural rather than a timing artefact.
No debt is filed anywhere in the source, so leverage is unverifiable; interest rising from 0.24M (FY2015) to 4.659M (FY2025) shows borrowings have grown alongside the buyback.
Revenue is tied to litigation, antitrust and regulatory activity - a quieter enforcement cycle hits billings directly.
The moat is human: senior expert teams can and do leave, taking client relationships with them.
Streak is only 9 years, so the dividend policy is not yet proven across a full cycle (no dividend existed in 2008-09).
analysis.sectorNote: Standard industrial/professional-services model, so the rules mostly fit as written. Two exceptions: rule 4 was read on net income (25.3%) and 3-yr average FCF (37.9%) alongside the failing single-year FCF figure (74.5%), because a people business with ~1% capex intensity has FCF that swings entirely on bonus and receivable timing; and rule 8 is marked null rather than passed because the filer's debt is absent from the XBRL source, with an interest-implied ~0.6x noted as indicative only.

issues: NO SPLITS APPLIED. splitFacts is empty, no year's DPS is an r-multiple of its neighbours once specials are removed, and sharesBasic falls smoothly from 99.9m (FY2009) to 75.1m (FY2025) with no step-change. splitAdjustments is therefore empty and zero fiscal years were rescaled. The ~2x DPS years (2010, 2012, 2016, 2020, 2024) are specials, not old share bases - proven because divPaid/sharesBasic also doubles in exactly those years, which a split-basis artifact could not do (a stale share basis moves DPS and shares in opposite directions and leaves divPaid/shares unchanged).

Systematic cross-check bias: in every non-special year divPaid/sharesBasic sits 2.7%-5.7% ABOVE the filed regular DPS (FY2009 0.9857 vs 0.96; FY2013 1.0183 vs 0.98; FY2017 1.0421 vs 1.00; FY2019 1.1222 vs 1.08; FY2021 1.1281 vs 1.08; FY2025 1.3957 vs 1.33). The gap is one-directional and stable, consistent with dividends paid on unvested restricted shares (excluded from weighted-average basic shares) plus intra-year timing against a share count falling all year on buybacks. Judgement call: filed DPS kept, no rescaling.

Cross-check outside the ~5% tolerance in FY2022 (+5.7%: 1.1417 vs 1.08) and FY2023 (+5.4%: 1.1698 vs 1.11), and marginally in FY2024 (+5.1%: 2.3235 vs 2.21 declared incl. special). These are the three heaviest buyback years (218m, 177m, 138m), which widens exactly the bias above; no basis change is implied.

FY2024 special timing is a judgement call: the 1.00 special sits inside the Q2 rate fact (1.31) rather than Q4 as in 2016 and 2020, and the regular rate stepped 0.28 -> 0.31 in that same quarter. I read Q2 as 0.31 regular + 1.00 special, giving regular FY2024 = 1.21. If the Q2 regular had still been 0.28, regular FY2024 would be 1.18 and g3/g5 would be slightly lower.

FY2009-FY2013 regular DPS is on a CASH PAID basis (CommonStockDividendsPerShareDeclared does not exist before FY2014), so it can differ from declared by a quarter of timing. FY2010's 1.26 special in particular is a cash-paid-in-Q1 amount probably declared in late 2009.

FY2008 excluded from the dps series: annual cash-paid DPS is 3.69 against a 0.96 regular run-rate, implying a ~2.73 special, but there are no FY2008 quarterly facts and no FY2008 row in the table, so the regular/special split is not derivable. Not invented.

EBITDA null for FY2009-FY2012: the da family (Depreciation) starts 2013-12-31 and DepreciationAndAmortization was not joined into the table for those years. netDebtToEbitda is null there as a consequence.

Net debt null for FY2009-FY2020: LongTermDebt is only present 2021-2025 and no current-debt tag exists anywhere in the file. FHI paid interest every year (15.9m in FY2011), so debt existed - it is simply untagged here. Not zero-filled.

ROIC judgement call: invested capital = equity + debtLT + debtCur - cash, but debtLT is missing before FY2021 and debtCur is missing in all years. ROIC was computed with the missing debt components absent, which understates invested capital and OVERSTATES ROIC for FY2009-FY2020 - the 0.48/0.66/0.64 readings in 2009/2010/2017 are inflated. FY2021-FY2025 ROIC (0.24-0.40) includes long-term debt and is the comparable set, though still without any current debt.

The two common-stock tags differ by under 0.1% where they overlap; PaymentsOfDividends for FY2024 (184,811k) is 262k above DividendsCommonStockCash (184,549k), so the choice moves payout ratios by well under 1%.

rules.name: Management treats the dividend as a promise
rules.threshold: no cut in FY2020/2021; any cut/suspension in window fails
rules.note: FY2020 and FY2021 both held the regular rate at 1.08 - held, not cut (cut2020=false). No regular-dividend cut anywhere in FY2009-FY2025. FY2008 is outside the XBRL window and is not assessed. Capital return is real but tilted to buybacks: 263m of repurchases in FY2025, about 2.5x the 104.8m dividend, plus a recurring ~$1.00 special roughly every four years.

analysis.assessment: FHI is a $4.3B net-cash asset manager yielding 2.35% on its 1.33 regular dividend (2.68% on the freshly raised 0.38/qtr run-rate), paying out just 35.6% of free cash flow and earning a 40.4% return on invested capital - the quality and the runway are genuinely there. What it does not have is growth: the regular dividend compounded at 4.25% over five years and 2.89% over ten, with three multi-year flat stretches, and only 3 consecutive increases because FY2022 held at 1.08. Free cash flow actually shrank at -3.9% a year off the strong FY2020 base while the dividend grew, so the coverage that looks comfortable today is being funded by a business whose cash generation is flat-to-down, not rising. The snowball here is a slow one - roughly 2.4% yield plus low-to-mid-single-digit growth, topped up by a ~$1.00 special every four years (2016, 2020, 2024, so 2028 next) and buybacks running 2.5x the dividend, which shrink the count ~5%/yr and do more of the per-share work than the payout does. The thing most likely to break it is rates: money-market fee income and waiver economics move with short-term rates, and a sustained cutting cycle would compress the earnings base and push FHI straight back into another multi-year dividend freeze rather than a cut.

normalised.dpsMethod: Filed annual CommonStockDividendsPerShareDeclared (~364-365 day FY duration, 10-K) for every year FY2009-FY2025. Only FY2009 was divided by 2 for the 2-for-1 split effected 2012-03-23; FY2010-FY2012 were already restated post-split in the FY2012 10-K and were left untouched. Quarterly facts were NOT summed because dpsAllFacts contains mixed-basis and mis-dated quarterly durations (see issues); they were used only as corroboration. Every year was cross-checked against divPaid / weighted basic shares and against CommonStockDividendsPerShareCashPaid where available.

Evidence for adjusting exactly one year: (i) sharesBasic steps from 77,967,141 (FY2009) to 155,697,056 (FY2010), a clean 2x step marking the basis boundary; (ii) FY2009 divPaid/shares = 0.2255 which on the OLD basis is 0.4510, self-consistent with its filed DPS of 0.46 (+2.0%), so FY2009 is pre-split; (iii) FY2010 divPaid/shares = 0.2328 is self-consistent with filed 0.24 (+3.1%) on the NEW basis, so FY2010 is already restated. This matches the restatement window exactly: the FY2012 10-K restated FY2012, FY2011 and FY2010; FY2009 last appeared in the FY2011 10-K (filed Sept 2011, pre-split). Adjustments applied: DPS 0.46 -> 0.23; sharesBasic 77,967,141 -> 155,934,282. No later split: coverSharesOutstanding 115,911,056 (2026-05-21) vs FY2025 basic 118,700,000 is buyback shrinkage.

specials.note: No special dividend found. Filed annual DPS never exceeds divPaid/weighted-basic-shares by more than ~10.6% (FY2013), and that gap is fully explained by declaration-vs-payment timing during a rapid raise: FY2013 declared quarters 0.09+0.10+0.13+0.13 = 0.45, while CommonStockDividendsPerShareCashPaid for the same quarters = 0.09+0.09+0.10+0.13 = 0.41, matching the 0.4068 implied by cash paid / shares. issues: SPLIT (key judgement): FY2009 is the ONLY year adjusted for the 2-for-1 split effected 2012-03-23 (DPS 0.46 -> 0.23; sharesBasic 77,967,141 -> 155,934,282). FY2010, FY2011 and FY2012 were already restated post-split by the FY2012 10-K and were deliberately NOT divided. Evidence: sharesBasic steps exactly 2x between FY2009 (77.97M) and FY2010 (155.70M); divPaid/shares is self-consistent with the filed DPS inside each basis (FY2009 0.4510 vs 0.46 on the old basis; FY2010 0.2328 vs 0.24 on the new basis). SPLIT consequence: had FY2009 been left unadjusted the series would read 0.46 -> 0.24, a false 48% cut in FY2010 and a broken streak. After adjustment the series rises every single year.

Substituted NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivitiesContinuingOperations: FY2014 = 317,800,000, FY2015 = 212,800,000. That tag matches the primary exactly for FY2012/FY2013 but differs for FY2016 (286.1M vs 291.3M) and FY2017 (310.3M vs 317.8M), so FY2014/FY2015 CFO, FCF and payoutFcf may be understated by roughly 1-2%.

Regular DPS comes straight from the filed annual CommonStockDividendsPerShareDeclared tag for all 17 years, with a single split adjustment applied to FY2009 only for the 2-for-1 split effected 2012-03-23. The resulting split-adjusted series rises every single year: 0.23, 0.24, 0.28, 0.335, 0.45, 0.61, 0.67, 0.69, 0.71, 0.74, 0.80, 0.84, 0.86, 0.90, 0.96, 1.04, 1.14. Coverage is comfortable: FY2025 dividends of 131.9M against 339.9M FCF (38.8% payout) and 367.0M net income (35.9%), with a 9.2% FCF margin on 3,690.9M revenue. rules.name: Small enough to grow

rules.note: 1.14 FY2025 regular DPS / $86.33 = 1.32%. Even on the FMP ttm of 1.24 it is only 1.44%, and on the >=1.20 FY2026 run-rate 1.39%. Below the band on every basis - you are buying growth, not income.

rules.note: 0.84 (FY2020) -> 1.14 (FY2025). Misses the bar, though the trend is improving: 3-yr CAGR is 8.20% (0.90 -> 1.14) and the FY2026 raise to a 0.30 quarterly rate is another ~5-6%. 10-yr is only 5.46%.

rules.name: Payout with room left
rules.note: FY2025 dividends 131.9M / FCF 339.9M. Comfortably mid-band; net income payout 35.9%. Spikes to 76.6% (FY2015) and 65.8% (FY2022) were weak-CFO years, not policy. Net debt is a floor (current maturities may be excluded), which does not affect this rule.

rules.name: Streak long enough to prove policy, short enough to still be fast
rules.note: XBRL shows 16 straight increases FY2010-FY2025 with no hold, and the series starts at FY2009, so it is window-limited. Prior research streak of 30 is plausible for Donaldson and is used; it sits exactly at the upper bound, meaning the policy is proven but the easy-acceleration phase is likely behind it.

rules.name: Earnings growing at least as fast as the dividend
rules.note: FCF 262.6M (FY2020) -> 339.9M (FY2025). A narrow 1.0pp miss, and endpoint-sensitive: FY2020 was a strong CFO year and FY2023/FY2024 FCF was above 400M. Net income CAGR is 7.39% and EBITDA 6.82%, both above the dividend, so the miss is cash-conversion timing rather than an earnings shortfall - but the rule as written fails.

rules.name: High return on invested capital
rules.note: FY2025 ROIC 19.0%, and 17.8%-26.3% in every measurable year FY2010-FY2025 (FY2018's 15.6% is a TCJA tax artefact; FY2009 is null for missing debt facts). Strong-tier, and consistent - the best number in this record.

rules.name: Balance sheet not competing with you
rules.note: Net debt 490.8M / EBITDA 594.9M. Has sat in a 0.48x-1.07x band since FY2015. Treat 0.83x as a floor: debtCur used ShortTermBorrowings only and may exclude current maturities of long-term debt, but the headroom to 2.5x is far too wide for that to matter.

rules.name: Why competitors cannot take the business
rules.value: replacement-filter aftermarket on a large installed base
rules.note: Filters are spec'd into engines and industrial systems at OEM design-in, then replaced on a service interval for the life of the equipment; the aftermarket is roughly two-thirds of sales, is bought by fleet and plant maintenance buyers who will not risk a non-spec part on a $400k machine, and the filter is a trivial share of the owner's cost. That is a durable switching-cost mechanism, corroborated by the 19-23% ROIC and 9.2% FCF margin, not price competition.

rules.name: Management treats the dividend as a promise
rules.note: DPS rose 0.80 -> 0.84 -> 0.86 straight through COVID, and PaymentsOfDividendsCommonStock rose every single year of the window. 2008-09 is outside the XBRL window and cannot be tested from this data.

analysis.assessment: Donaldson is a high-quality compounder that fails the entry math rather than the business test: 19.0% ROIC, 0.83x net debt/EBITDA, a 38.8% FCF payout and 16 data-confirmed (likely ~30 actual) years of unbroken increases, all intact. But the snowball starts at a 1.32% yield on 1.14 of FY2025 dividends against an $86.33 price and compounds at only 6.30% over five years, so the yield-on-cost is still under 2.5% a decade out - the combination of a sub-band yield and sub-8% growth is what caps this at candidate. There is genuine runway: the payout could roughly double before hitting the 60% ceiling, 3-yr DPS growth has re-accelerated to 8.20%, and FY2026 is running at a >=1.20 rate (FMP ttm 1.24 implies a Q4 raise to roughly 0.34). The thing most likely to break it is not the dividend but capital allocation: 331.5M of FY2025 buybacks is 2.5x the 131.9M dividend, and management has consistently chosen shrinking the share count over accelerating the payout, so the dividend stays a slow 6-8% grower unless that priority changes. Watch FCF conversion too - FY2022 (167.3M) and FY2025 (339.9M, down from 406.9M) show working-capital swings big enough to push payout above 60% in a bad year.

estimateCorrections.why: Filed split-adjusted DPS 0.84 (FY2020) -> 1.14 (FY2025) is a 6.30% CAGR, 2.7pp below the estimate. The 9% guess looks like an extrapolation of the older 2011-2014 era (15-20% raises) or of the recent 3-yr rate of 8.20%; the actual five-year window includes the deliberately small FY2020 (+4.8%) and FY2021 (+2.4%) COVID-era raises. This flips rule 3 from pass to fail.

FY2025 dividends 131.9M against FCF 339.9M (CFO 418.8M less capex 78.9M) is 38.8%, 8.8pp above the estimate. The 30% figure would match FY2024 (30.2%) or FY2021 (31.3%); FY2025 FCF fell from 406.9M while dividends rose to 131.9M. Rule 4 still passes, but with less headroom than assumed.

No change to the screen value, but the basis is now explicit: only 16 consecutive increases (FY2010-FY2025) are derivable, and the data window starts at FY2009 so the measured streak is window-limited. The 30 is retained from prior research as plausible and is flagged as research-sourced rather than data-confirmed.

analysis.moat: Filtration with a large replacement-filter aftermarket attached to an installed base that was spec'd in at OEM design-in, so the recurring filter sale is protected by switching cost and warranty risk rather than price.
strengths: ROIC 19.0% in FY2025 and 17.8-26.3% in every measurable year since FY2010 - genuinely capital-light for an industrial.
Payout 38.8% of FCF and 35.9% of net income: the dividend could roughly double before stressing the 60% ceiling.
Net debt/EBITDA 0.83x, in a 0.48-1.07x band since FY2015; the balance sheet is not competing for the dividend.
No cut and no hold anywhere in the 16-year window, including FY2020 and FY2021 - the promise held through COVID.
3-yr DPS growth of 8.20% versus 5.46% over 10 years: the raise rate is re-accelerating, and FY2026 is already at a >=1.20 run-rate.
risks: 1.32% starting yield (1.44% on ttm 1.24) is well below the 1.5-4.0% usable band - the snowball starts very small.
6.30% 5-yr DPS CAGR misses the 8% bar; at that rate yield-on-cost is still under 2.5% in ten years.
5-yr FCF CAGR of 5.30% lags the 6.30% dividend growth, so the payout ratio has been drifting up (30.2% in FY2024 to 38.8% in FY2025).
FY2025 buybacks of 331.5M are 2.5x the 131.9M of dividends; management's revealed preference is share count over payout, which caps dividend acceleration.
FCF is working-capital volatile (167.3M in FY2022 against 426.0M in FY2023); a repeat of FY2022 with today's dividend would put payout near 79%.
Reported net debt of 490.8M may exclude current maturities of long-term debt (debtCur = ShortTermBorrowings only), so 0.83x is a floor - immaterial at this leverage but worth noting.
Streak at the top of the 10-30 band: a 30-year record signals a mature, institutionalised policy, not one about to speed up.
analysis.sectorNote: Donaldson is a straightforward industrial manufacturer, so all ten rules apply as written with no sector substitution: FCF = CFO - capex is the right payout denominator (FCF is positive in all 17 years and averages ~9% of revenue), net debt/EBITDA is meaningful, and ROIC on equity + total debt - cash is economically sensible for an asset-light filtration business. The only judgement calls are non-sectoral: rule 5's streak is window-limited by the XBRL start (FY2009) and takes the prior research figure of 30, and rule 6 was assessed on FCF as specified - on net income (7.39% CAGR) or EBITDA (6.82%) it would pass, and that divergence is noted rather than used to override the rule.

stocks.m: Welders are trained on Lincoln equipment and procedures at its own welding schools and the technical colleges it supplies, and every installed machine pulls a recurring stream of matched consumables that no fabricator will risk swapping on a certified weld.

normalised.dpsMethod: Rule (a): filed annual CommonStockDividendsPerShareDeclared facts with ~364-365 day durations (form 10-K, fp FY) used directly for FY2009-FY2025. FY2008 (1.02, also a filed annual fact) is on the pre-split share basis and was divided by 2 for the 2-for-1 split effected in Q2 2010, giving 0.51. FY2009-FY2025 are already post-split in the data (2009 was restated inside the split-year 10-K's comparative window; verified against the quarterly rate facts and against divPaid/sharesBasic). No special dividends found: the filed DPS never sits far above divPaid/shares. Quarterly rate facts corroborate every year (e.g. FY2010 = 0.14+0.14+0.14+0.155 = 0.575 post-split; FY2025 = 4 x 0.75 + Q4 step to 0.79 = 3.04).

splitAdjustments.note: 2-for-1 split effected during Q2 2010 (splitFacts is empty, so the date is inferred, not filed: the Q1-2010 10-Q tagged Q1 declared DPS at 0.28, while the Q2-2010 10-Q restated the same H1 period to 0.28 total with Q2 = 0.14, so the restatement lands between 2010-04-01 and 2010-06-30; corroborated by table sharesOut (CommonStockSharesOutstanding) stepping 42,637,247 (2009-12-31) -> 84,241,600 (2010-12-31)). ONLY FY2008 was adjusted (1.02 / 2 = 0.51). FY2009 and FY2010 were left alone because they are already post-split: FY2009 filed DPS 0.545 = 1.09 pre-split (quarterly rates 0.27/0.27/0.27/0.28) / 2, and divPaid/sharesBasic for 2009 = 0.5402 (-0.9% vs 0.545) and for 2010 = 0.5611 (-2.4%), i.e. self-consistent on the post-split basis. That is exactly the expected restatement window (split year 2010 plus the two prior years 2009 and 2008 restated in later filings), except that the FY2008 annual DPS value retained by the XBRL frames series is the originally filed pre-split value, which is why it and only it needed dividing. No sharesBasic value needed multiplying: the weighted-basic series is post-split from 2009 onward (84,782,000 in 2009 vs 84,407,000 in 2010 - smooth, no step), and 2008 shares are not in the table.

specials.note: No special dividend detected. The only year where filed DPS sits far from divPaid/sharesBasic is FY2012 (+23.9%) and its mirror FY2013 (-27.6%), and that is a cash-timing artifact, not a special: DividendsCommonStockCash (declared basis) gives 0.7117 for 2012 and 0.8293 for 2013, matching filed DPS of 0.71 and 0.83 within 0.2%. PaymentsOfDividendsCommonStock for 2012 (73,112k) carries five quarterly payments because the Q4-2012 dividend was paid inside calendar 2012 (the widespread pre-2013-tax-change acceleration), leaving only three in 2013 (49,277k). live.regularDividendIfSpecial is null and live.ttmDividend 3.12 is the cash-paid TTM (0.75 + 0.79 x 3); the declared-basis run rate is 3.16 (4 x 0.79). Neither implies a special.

normalised.notes: LECO, calendar fiscal year (--12-31). Regular DPS comes straight from filed annual CommonStockDividendsPerShareDeclared facts for FY2009-FY2025; only FY2008 needed split adjustment (2-for-1 effected in Q2 2010, 1.02 -> 0.51). No special dividends. Eighteen data points with 17 consecutive year-over-year increases ending FY2025, no cut or hold, including through 2020 (1.90 -> 1.98). DPS CAGRs: 9.43% over 3 years, 8.95% over 5, 9.83% over 10, 11.07% over the full 2008-2025 window. FY2025 FCF of 534.2m covers the 168.2m of dividends paid 3.2x (31.5% payout on FCF, 32.3% on net income); the payout on FCF has sat in a 26-42% band since 2015 with no trend toward stress. Q4-2025 raised the quarterly rate to 0.79, an annualised 3.16. Share count is down steadily from 84.8m (2009) to 55.4m (2025) on continuous buybacks (338m repurchased in 2025, roughly double the dividend). Main data gaps: long-term debt is missing for FY2020-FY2025, so net debt, net-debt/EBITDA and ROIC are null for the whole recent period (ROIC ran 19-24% through 2011-2019, so the franchise quality is visible in the earlier window); and revenue is missing for FY2023-FY2025, so FCF margin for the latest year is null. The FY2012/FY2013 payout ratios are distorted by the December-2012 dividend acceleration, a cash-timing artifact and not a special dividend.

verdicts.summary: No blocking issue. Recomputed all DPS cross-checks, the split reconstruction (FY2008 only, ratio 2), FCF/payout/EBITDA/netDebt/ROIC for all 17 table years, all four CAGRs, the 17-year streak, fiscal-year alignment and the CFO backfill - every figure reproduces the record exactly.

verdicts.summary: All external checks pass: DPS 3.04 vs live ttmDividend 3.12 (+2.6%, explained by the Q4-2025 step to 0.79); implied share count from marketCap/price 54.51m matches cover shares 54,505,757 to 0.001%; implied yield 1.19% is low but inside the sanity band; 8.95% 5-yr DPS CAGR is coherent for a high-ROIC industrial; divergences from priorEstimates are all named and explained. FMP split and dividend-history endpoints were access-denied, so the 2010 split rests on internal filing evidence.

'4 x 0.75 + 0.79' typo; value 3.04 is correct.
ttmDividend 3.12 reconciles on a cash-paid basis; declared-basis run rate is 3.16.
All three latest-year quality metrics null; downstream readers must not treat null as zero leverage. FY2025 EBITDA 816.6m against a 13.9B cap implies roughly 1x net debt/EBITDA, not 0x.

rules.name: Small enough to grow
rules.note: Live market cap 13,915,330,740 at $255.30 (2026-09-17). Passes, but only 7% below the $15B ceiling and nearly 3x the ideal zone - the easy-growth phase is behind it.

rules.name: Starting yield in the usable band
rules.note: 3.04 / 255.30 = 1.19%; even on the current Q4-2025 declared run rate of 3.16 it is 1.24%. Roughly 25 bp short of the band - this is the one hard fail and it is a price problem, not a policy problem.

rules.name: Dividend growth above 8%/yr
rules.note: 5-yr DPS CAGR 8.95% (1.98 -> 3.04); 3-yr 9.43%, 10-yr 9.83%, 17-yr 11.07%. Passes but is decelerating - the Q4-2025 raise was only +5.3% (0.75 -> 0.79), so forward growth looks nearer 5-6% than 9%.

rules.name: Payout with room left
rules.note: FY2025 dividends paid 168.2m / FCF 534.2m = 31.5% (32.3% of net income). The FCF payout has sat in a 26-42% band every year since 2015 with no drift upward. Comfortably mid-band.

rules.name: Streak long enough to prove policy
rules.note: The data shows 17 consecutive increases FY2008-FY2025 with no hold or cut, and the window starts at the first XBRL year, so it is window-limited. Prior research streak of 30 years is plausible for LECO and is the figure used; it sits exactly on the upper limit, so any further year would push this out of the 'still fast' zone.

rules.name: Earnings growing at least as fast as the dividend
rules.note: FCF grew 292.2m (2020) -> 534.2m (2025), a 12.83% CAGR, ~3.9pp ahead of the dividend, so the payout ratio has been falling, not rising. Net income agrees directionally (206.1m -> 520.5m).

rules.name: High return on invested capital
rules.value: n/a for FY2025; 21.6% at FY2019 (last computable)
rules.note: Not assessable: long-term debt is absent for FY2020-FY2025 in this extract, so invested capital and ROIC are null for the whole recent period. Every computable year from FY2011 to FY2019 ran 13.9%-23.7% (19-24% in eight of nine), so the franchise clears the bar historically - but the latest six years are unverified here, not confirmed.

rules.name: Balance sheet not competing with you
rules.value: n/a for FY2025; 1.21x at FY2019 (last computable)
rules.note: Same missing debt series. Null must not be read as net cash: the company ran net cash through 2014 but has carried net debt since 2015, peaking at 1.21x EBITDA in 2019. FY2025 EBITDA of 816.6m against a 13.9B cap implies something near 1x, comfortably inside the limit, but it is an inference, not a measurement.

rules.name: Why competitors cannot take the business
rules.value: training pipeline + consumables razor-blade installed base
rules.note: Welders are trained on Lincoln equipment and procedures at Lincoln's welding schools and at the technical colleges it supplies, and the machine then locks in a stream of matched filler-metal consumables that a buyer will not risk swapping on a certified weld. That is switching cost plus a recurring revenue annuity, not a price argument - and the 19-24% ROIC through 2011-2019 is what it looks like in the numbers.

rules.name: Management treats the dividend as a promise
rules.note: The dividend rose through COVID (FY2020 +4.2%, FY2021 +5.6%) and in every other year of the window; no cut, suspension or hold anywhere in FY2008-FY2025. 2008-09 is inside this window and the dividend rose in FY2009 too, even with payout at 94% of net income at the recession trough.

analysis.assessment: Lincoln Electric is a genuinely high-quality compounder trading at a price that has eaten the yield: at $255.30 the $3.04 regular dividend yields 1.19%, a quarter-point below the usable band, and that is the only hard fail among the eight assessable rules. Everything behind the dividend is in good order - 31.5% of FY2025 free cash flow (168.2m of 534.2m), a 5-yr DPS CAGR of 8.95% against 12.83% FCF growth so the payout ratio is falling, 17 consecutive increases in the data (very likely ~30 in reality) with raises straight through 2020, and a share count down from 84.8m to 55.4m. The snowball here is a low-yield, high-growth one: you start at ~1.2%, compound the dividend at roughly 9% with an owner's yield that doubles about every eight years, and rely on buybacks (338m in 2025, twice the dividend) to do most of the per-share work. The thing most likely to break it is not the dividend but the entry price plus the deceleration already visible - the Q4-2025 raise was only 5.3% (0.75 to 0.79), and a cyclical industrial whose revenue fell 12% in 2015-16 and 18% in 2020 can flatten growth for a couple of years without breaking policy. The honest caveat: FY2020-FY2025 leverage and ROIC are unavailable in this extract because the long-term-debt series was not pulled, so the balance-sheet and returns rules rest on FY2019 readings (1.21x, 21.6%) rather than current ones.
analysis.moat: Welders are trained on Lincoln equipment and procedures at its own welding schools and the technical colleges it supplies, and every installed machine pulls a recurring stream of matched consumables that no fabricator will risk swapping on a certified weld.
strengths: Payout of 31.5% of FCF with FCF growing 12.83%/yr against 8.95% dividend growth - the ratio has been falling, not rising, and sat in a 26-42% band every year since 2015.
Unbroken dividend policy across two recessions inside the window: raises in FY2009 (at a 94% NI payout trough) and through FY2020-FY2021.
ROIC of 19-24% in eight of the nine years it is computable (FY2011-FY2019) - the moat is visible in the returns, not just the story.
Relentless share shrinkage: 84.8m basic shares (2009) to 55.4m (2025), with 338m of 2025 buybacks running at roughly twice the dividend.
risks: Yield of 1.19% is below the usable band; the starting income is thin and the thesis depends on growth plus multiple maintenance.
Growth is decelerating - the Q4-2025 raise was +5.3% (0.75 -> 0.79) versus a trailing 5-yr CAGR of 8.95%.
Cyclical end markets: revenue fell 12% in 2015-16 and 18% in 2020, and FY2015 net income dropped 50% - earnings growth can stall for years at a time.
FY2020-FY2025 net debt/EBITDA and ROIC are unavailable in this extract; a reader treating null as zero debt would materially overstate balance-sheet quality.
At $13.9B market cap it is close to the $15B size ceiling, so the small-company growth tailwind is largely spent.
analysis.sectorNote: Standard industrial manufacturer - no sector adjustment needed. Rules 4, 6, 7 and 8 were applied on the ordinary FCF = CFO - capex basis. The only deviation is that rules 7 and 8 are marked null rather than failed because the long-term-debt series for FY2020-FY2025 was not materialised in this extract; both are scored as unassessable, not as passes, and the last computable readings (FY2019: ROIC 21.6%, net debt/EBITDA 1.21x) are given for context.

stocks.m: Convenience stores with prepared-food kitchen economics in towns too small to support a second modern competitor - the rural footprint blocks entry and the pizza/kitchen margin is what a fuel-led rival cannot replicate.

normalised.dpsMethod: FY2009-FY2014: filed annual CommonStockDividendsPerShareCashPaid (10-K/10-K/A, ~364-day durations). FY2015-FY2023: filed annual CommonStockDividendsPerShareDeclared (10-K, ~364-365 day durations). FY2024: no annual fact filed; summed the quarterly declared rates inside the May-2023/Apr-2024 fiscal year (Q1 0.43, Q2 0.43 implied from 0.86 cumulative, Q3 0.43 implied from 1.29 cumulative) and applied 4x the latest quarterly rate for the missing Q4 => 4 x 0.43 = 1.72. FY2025-FY2026: no DPS facts at all; derived by bracketing PaymentsOfDividends/sharesBasic against DividendsCommonStock/sharesBasic. NO split adjustment applied to any year.

specials.note: No special dividends found. splitFacts is empty and no year shows filed DPS materially ABOVE divPaid/sharesBasic - filed DPS runs 1-3% above cash-paid-per-share and 0-1.5% below declared-per-share, the normal declared-vs-paid lag for a company that raises its rate every June (fiscal Q1). The one large jump, FY2011 DPS 0.34 -> 0.505 (+48.5%), is a genuine regular-rate increase (2010 Couche-Tard hostile-bid defense), not a special: FY2011 divPaid/sharesBasic is 0.4840, within 4.2% of the filed 0.505, whereas a special would leave the regular rate far below cash paid.

issues: NO SPLIT ADJUSTMENT APPLIED - splitFacts is empty and the evidence rules out a split anywhere in the window. The only step-change in sharesBasic is FY2010 50,899,370 -> FY2011 42,284,664 (-17%), explained by the $501,026,000 PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock in FY2011 (Dutch-auction self-tender during the Couche-Tard hostile bid). A split would RAISE the share count, not cut it. Independently, divPaid/sharesBasic is self-consistent with the filed DPS in every year (max deviation 4.2%, FY2011), so no year sits on a different share basis. splitAdjustments.yearsAdjusted is empty: 0 years adjusted.

FY2011 is the only year where the cross-check deviates by more than ~3%: filed DPS 0.505 vs divPaid/sharesBasic 0.4840 (-4.2%). Judgement: buyback timing (shares fell through the year while the weighted-average denominator lags), not a special and not a basis error. Kept the filed 0.505.

MIXED DPS TAG BASIS: FY2009-FY2014 come from CommonStockDividendsPerShareCashPaid (cash paid) while FY2015-FY2023 come from CommonStockDividendsPerShareDeclared. Because the rate is raised every June (fiscal Q1), the cash-paid measure runs about one quarter behind declared, so FY2009-FY2014 are slightly conservative relative to later years. No overlap year exists to calibrate the two tags. This is the largest source of imprecision in gMax.

FY2024 DPS (1.72) is NOT a filed annual fact. Only three quarterly declared facts exist for FY2024 (Q1 0.43; Q2 cumulative 0.86 -> 0.43; Q3 cumulative 1.29 -> 0.43); Q4 is missing (DPS tags stop after the FY2024 Q3 10-Q). Applied rule (b): 4 x latest quarterly rate 0.43 = 1.72. Corroborated by DividendsCommonStock/sharesBasic = 1.7402 (+1.2%) and PaymentsOfDividends/sharesBasic = 1.6930 (-1.6%).

FY2025 DPS (2.00) and FY2026 DPS (2.28) are NOT filed - no DPS fact of any kind exists after 2024-01-31. Derived by bracketing each year between two per-share measures that straddle the filed rate: FY2025 PaymentsOfDividends/sharesBasic = 1.9482 and DividendsCommonStock/sharesBasic = 2.0310 -> midpoint 1.9896, taken as 2.0000 ($0.50/qtr); FY2026 PaymentsOfDividends/sharesBasic = 2.2430 and DividendsCommonStock/sharesBasic = 2.3135 -> midpoint 2.2782, taken as 2.2800 ($0.57/qtr). The straddle is validated on the nine years where the filed value is known: DividendsCommonStock/sharesBasic averages ~+0.4% above filed and PaymentsOfDividends/sharesBasic ~-2.0% below it, in every year without exception. Independent corroboration: FMP ttmDividend 2.36 as of 2026-09-17 equals 3 x 0.57 + 0.65 (three FY2026-rate payments plus one post-raise payment), which only reconciles if the FY2026 quarterly rate was 0.57. These two years remain judgement values, not filed values - hence confidence medium, not high.

EBITDA is derived, not filed: no operating-income tag exists in the extract. Used EBITDA = (pretax + InterestExpense) + DepreciationAndAmortization. This treats non-operating other income/expense as operating and ignores capitalized interest (InterestCostsCapitalized, $3,189,000 in FY2026), so EBITDA and every netDebtToEbitda are approximations.

Pretax income is only filed for FY2009-FY2019 (tag stops at 2019-04-30). For FY2020-FY2026 pretax was reconstructed as NetIncomeLoss + IncomeTaxExpenseBenefit. Verified exact on overlap years (FY2018: 317,903 + (-103,466) = 214,437 = filed; FY2019: 203,886 + 59,516 = 263,402 = filed).

FY2018 effective tax rate is NEGATIVE (-48.25%: IncomeTaxExpenseBenefit -$103,466,000 on $214,437,000 pretax - the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act remeasurement benefit). Applied the rule literally, so (1 - t) = 1.4825 and FY2018 ROIC of 15.58% is overstated; it is the highest ROIC in the series purely because of a one-off tax credit. I did not substitute the 21% fallback because the rate WAS derivable.

FY2009 has no sharesBasic, debtLT, debtCur or assets in the table (those tags start 2010-04-30), so FY2009 netDebt, netDebtToEbitda, roic and sharesBasic are null and no FY2009 per-share cross-check was possible.

Revenue is null for FY2009-FY2015. The Revenues tag starts 2016-04-30 and the table carries no earlier revenue; SalesRevenueNet exists in families (2009-2017, 9 points) but its series was not included in the extract, so I did not invent values. fcfMargin is only computable from FY2016 onward.

FCF was NEGATIVE in FY2013 (-$18,973,000), FY2015 (-$12,089,000) and FY2018 (-$157,624,000) - heavy new-store/acquisition build years - so payoutFcf is null for those three years per the rule. FY2014 payoutFcf is 4.9023 (490%) because FCF was barely positive at $5,527,000; arithmetically correct but meaningless as a payout ratio.
FY2017 payoutFcf 1.4203 (142%) and FY2020 payoutFcf 0.7033 (70%) are real but capex-cycle artifacts, not dividend stress. Over FY2021-FY2026 payoutFcf sits in an 11-17% band.

Two divPaid tags disagree by 2-4% in most years (PaymentsOfDividends = cash out the door; DividendsCommonStock = declared). I used the primary tag PaymentsOfDividends for fin.divPaid and all payout ratios, and used DividendsCommonStock only as the upper bracket in the FY2025/FY2026 DPS derivation. Using the other tag would raise every payout ratio by roughly 3%.

priorEstimates were materially off and are replaced: growth5y guessed 13% (actual 5-yr DPS CAGR 11.55%), streak guessed 26 years (only 17 consecutive increases are observable in this window, FY2010-FY2026; the streak runs to the start of the data so it may extend earlier - windowLimited is true, and the 26-year claim is neither confirmed nor refuted here), payoutPctFcf guessed 20% (actual FY2026 11.5%).

FY2026 revenue-based fcfMargin of 4.11% is structurally low because the Revenues tag is gross fuel revenue including motor-fuel excise/pass-through economics; it is not comparable to a non-fuel retailer's margin.

normalised.notes: Casey's General Stores, FYE April 30, so FY2026 = year ended 2026-04-30 (already filed). 18 fiscal years of cash-flow data (FY2009-FY2026) and 18 derivable DPS years. No stock split and no special dividend anywhere in the window; splitAdjustments is deliberately empty and the FY2011 share-count drop is a $501M self-tender, not a split. Regular DPS rises every single year from $0.30 (FY2009) to $2.28 (FY2026) - 17 unbroken increases inside the data, no cut and no hold, including through FY2020/FY2021. The dividend shape is a single annual raise declared each June (fiscal Q1), which is why declared-per-share runs about one quarter ahead of cash-paid-per-share every year. Growth is accelerating rather than decaying: 9.99% over 10 years, 11.55% over 5, 14.47% over 3 - the company moved from ~8-9% raises (FY2015-FY2022) to 13-16% raises (FY2024-FY2026) as FCF inflected. Coverage is not the binding constraint: FY2026 FCF of $722M covers the $83M dividend 8.7x (11.5% of FCF, 11.6% of net income), FCF compounded 14.7%/yr over 5 years, and net debt/EBITDA fell back to 1.29x in FY2026 after the FY2025 spike to 1.82x on the CEFCO acquisition. The real historical caveat is capex intensity - FCF was negative in three of eighteen years (FY2013, FY2015, FY2018) on build-outs, so the low payout ratio is better read as a buffer against the next build cycle than as free headroom. FY2025 and FY2026 DPS are derived, not filed, and are the main figures to re-verify once the FY2026 10-K DPS tags appear.

6. Fiscal-year labels vs period-end dates: every table key and dps.end is YYYY-04-30 matching the label year, consistent with fiscalYearEnd --04-30. No misalignment. PASS.
